title: A per-character effect the badge set cannot name is dropped with no record at all
body:
A condition affecting one character, whose id the running title has no glyph for, disappears from the roster card with no record anywhere — no badge, no tooltip, no debug log line.

## What breaks

You attach the automapper to a running game, cast Bless on one fighter, and look at his roster card. If the effect's id is one the badge set covers you get a glyph. If it is not, **nothing happens at all** — the card looks exactly as it did, and nothing anywhere says an effect was read and dropped.

**How a player ends up there**: they play Secret of the Silver Blades with the automapper attached and cast anything at all on one character. Since `#196 (The automapper's condition badges name a Silver Blades trait with Pool of Radiance's meaning)`, Silver Blades draws **no** condition badges — sixteen of the seventeen badged ids are unnamed in its own trait table, so drawing one would assert a meaning nobody has read. That refusal is right. The consequence is that on Silver Blades *every* per-character effect is now in this silent-drop path.

On Pool of Radiance and Curse it is narrower but still real: any effect outside the seventeen badged ids vanishes the same way.

## Root cause

There are two paths and only one of them keeps a record.

* **Whole-party effects** — `Snapshot.unbadged_party_effects` collects every party effect no glyph covers, and `automap/panel.py`'s `BottomStrip` writes each to the debug log once per id. That is deliberate and it works.
* **Per-character effects** — `Character.conditions` calls `badges()` and `RosterCard` calls `self.conditions.set_icons(...)` with whatever comes back. Anything `badges()` did not produce a glyph for is simply not in the list. There is no `unbadged_` equivalent, no log call, and no counterpart to the party-strip mechanism.

**This predates the per-title work and is not caused by it.** `#196` made it matter more by correctly emptying Silver Blades' badge set, and `docs/136-condition-badges.md` said "nothing is hidden" — which was true of the party strip and not of the cards. That sentence is now corrected to say which is which.

## What would fix it

Give the per-character path the counterpart the party path already has: a list of the ids a card read and could not draw, and a debug log line for them, in the shape `unbadged_party_effects` and `BottomStrip` already establish between them.

Two things worth deciding while doing it, neither large:

* **Whether it belongs on `Character` or on `Snapshot`.** Per party member is more precise; per snapshot is fewer log lines and matches what the party strip does.
* **Whether the log should say it once per session rather than once per poll.** The automapper polls continuously, so a naive line per read would flood the log — `BottomStrip`'s "once per id, not five times a second" is the precedent and the reason it exists.

Nothing here should put a new string in front of a player. The debug log is the exception `CLAUDE.md` names for addresses and developer detail, and it is where this belongs.

## Testing

A snapshot carrying a per-character effect id outside the badge set produces a log line naming it, and a card that badges everything it read produces none. `tests/test_pertitle_live.py` builds records with `tests/gamedata.py:synthetic_party`, which takes `race` and `trait_codes` since `#186 (The character sheet gives a Silver Blades elf a Pool of Radiance ability)`, so a Silver Blades character carrying a running effect is one line to construct.

Reverting the fix must turn it red, and the test must fail on the **missing line** rather than on a missing attribute.

Found in the code review of `#197 (A Curse or Silver Blades paladin or ranger has no class and no experience bar on its roster card)`, 2026-09-02.

*Priority guessed at Low: nothing is wrong on screen and no player is misled — the card is honest about what it can name. What is lost is the one signal that would tell somebody an effect was read and could not be drawn, which is the thing that would otherwise reveal the gap. Donald recurates these by hand.*

title: The C64 side of 0x0AB is unnamed, so the conversion drops it with no issue behind it
body:
`unnamed_0ab` is dropped converting a DOS character to the C64 and no issue stands behind it, which `.claude/rules/conversions.md` requires for every drop-list entry.

## What breaks

Nothing a player can point at yet, because nobody knows what the byte holds on
either side. That is the problem: it is on the drop list on the strength of
being unnamed, which is the third of `conversions.md`'s three reasons -- *"we do
not understand the bytes well enough to write them"* -- and that reason is
explicitly **a defect with a settling experiment, not a permanent exemption**.

`#131 (Lift WISH_EXPERIMENTAL_DOS_IMPORT, which needs the import working for
all three C64 titles)` cannot lift while it stands, and it was the one entry on
either table with no issue at all.

## Root cause

`#216 (Every converted DOS character carries the same identity byte at 0x0AB)`
fixed the **DOS writer**: every converted character was carrying the same value
there. Nothing has ever covered the **C64 side**, where no field has been
attributed to the offset.

So the DOS half is understood well enough to write and the C64 half is not, and
the drop-list entry is about the second.

## What would settle it

**Read what writes it**, which is now much cheaper than when this entry was
made. `tools/coldread.py` and `d6502` read a C64 routine out of an overlay;
`tools/trainerscan.py --refs` finds every instruction touching an address.
Tonight `#235 (Two unattributed DOS byte ranges in the combat tail are dropped
converting to C64, and nobody knows what they hold)` settled the C64 status byte
by finding the routine that draws it, and `#253 (A Curse or Silver Blades
party's square is read twelve bytes past where the engine writes it, since #220
moved the offset the wrong way)` settled a save offset from the engine's own
`BlockWrite` chain. The same method applies.

Three outcomes, all real: the byte has a C64 home and the drop closes; the C64
record has no such field, established by reading the layout, and the entry
becomes a legitimate exemption with a tested reason; or nothing writes it in
either port and both sides can stop carrying it.

**A census will not answer this on its own.** Whatever the value is, it is the
same in every specimen anybody has, which is how it came to be called unnamed.
And `.claude/rules/testing.md` now says a save found on a disk is not evidence
about the game -- so the code is the route.

`Priority: Low` guessed: nothing a player sees, and it is one byte. It is on
this list only because `#131` cannot lift while any drop lacks an issue, and
that is a cheap thing to fix compared with the others.

Documentation: [`docs/117-save-conversion.md`](https://github.com/malcyon/wish/blob/main/docs/117-save-conversion.md)

title: Phase 2B animal-dialog regression test: provide the canonical Core parentage fixture
body:
# Phase 2B animal-dialog regression test: provide the canonical Core parentage fixture

Phase: Phase 2B regression-evidence maintenance
Milestone: `0.2.3`
Classification: codehealth / test-harness bug
Priority: P2

## Problem

The latest full-suite run and the focused dialog regression run both fail:

```text
tests/test_phase2b_animal_dialog_statistics_regressions.py::
AnimalDialogStatisticsRegressionTests::test_animal_section_mode_is_independent_of_localized_title
```

The test constructs a minimal fake backend whose `records` object implements only `get()`. Calling `_set_animal_dialog_context()` now correctly fails closed while loading the canonical Core parentage projection:

```text
ValueError: Core parentage data is unavailable. Reload and try again.
```

The same failure was reproduced against clean starting commit `750fa94e2b48c63ba2e7553d2d94f9a21860894e`, so it is pre-existing test-fixture drift rather than a regression introduced by the current Heritage, Projects, or Plot work. It nevertheless blocks trustworthy full-suite evidence.

## Required solution

- Adapt the test double to the supported Core parentage/backend contract used by `_set_animal_dialog_context()`.
- Keep the test's actual purpose: section-preference identity must be derived from canonical dialog mode and role, never from the localized window title.
- Provide the minimal canonical parentage data path or an explicit supported no-parentage fixture; do not weaken the production fail-closed behavior and do not make the test depend on a localized title workaround.
- Preserve read-only behavior and assert that context setup performs no unintended domain mutation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The named localized-title test passes with the canonical backend fixture.
- [ ] The full `tests/test_phase2b_animal_dialog_statistics_regressions.py` module passes without changing the production availability guard.
- [ ] The fixture models the current `load_core_data`/Core parentage contract, or uses the repository's supported test backend rather than an obsolete `get()`-only stub.
- [ ] The test remains valid across the shipped localized dialog titles and continues to assert the stable prefix `edit:experimental`.
- [ ] The complete suite no longer reports this dialog harness failure.

## Technical anchors

- `tests/test_phase2b_animal_dialog_statistics_regressions.py::AnimalDialogStatisticsRegressionTests::test_animal_section_mode_is_independent_of_localized_title`
- `ProgTrack.v.0.2.3.py::_set_animal_dialog_context`
- `ProgTrack.v.0.2.3.py::_load_core_parentage_records`
- Phase-2B dialog behavior originally delivered under #84

## Validation evidence

- `Q:\GitHub\Issue Tracker\Tests\2026-09-09-milestone-0.2.3-luna\focused-results.md`
- `Q:\GitHub\Issue Tracker\Tests\2026-09-09-milestone-0.2.3-luna\baseline-localized-title.txt`

## Dependencies and sequencing

This is independent of #186, #195, #196, and #199. It is a release-evidence blocker for the 0.2.3 regression gate and should be completed before claiming the full suite is clean.

## Notes for publication

This is test infrastructure maintenance. It does not change the semantics of parentage, animal-dialog section preferences, localization, or Core/Heritage ownership.

title: fix(seed): l'indicateur d'activité est vide sur les données du make seed
body:
Relevé en faisant l'essai à blanc du README (#63), sur la pile Docker complète.

`make seed` s'exécute correctement — `status=succeeded, lus=19, importés=26, doublons=14, rejetés=0` — mais l'un des quatre indicateurs exigés reste vide :

```
GET /api/v1/metrics/activity  -> {"points": [], "filters_applied": {}, "warnings": []}
GET /api/v1/metrics/tools     -> 3 points
GET /api/v1/metrics/models    -> des points
GET /api/v1/metrics/quality   -> des points
```

Vide aussi avec une plage explicite (`?from_date=2020-01-01&to_date=2030-01-01`).

## Cause

`activity` groupe les sessions par jour, et les sessions importées n'ont pas de date :

```
GET /sessions?limit=2
{"items": [{"id": 2, "external_id": "codex:a611…", "started_at": null, "ended_at": null, …}]}
```

Le mapping construit par `interfaces/cli/seed.py` ne couvre, pour l'entité `session`, que `external_id` et `agent_name` — `started_at` n'y figure pas.

Et le fichier d'exemple ne porte pas d'horodatage directement exploitable au niveau de la session. Ses seuls champs temporels sont `timing_events` (une structure imbriquée) ; il n'y a ni `started_at`, ni `timestamp`, ni `date` à plat.

## Pourquoi ça compte

`make seed` est le chemin de démonstration du projet, celui que le README propose en une commande et qu'un correcteur suivra. Il produit aujourd'hui un tableau de bord où **un indicateur sur quatre est vide**, sans que rien n'explique pourquoi — ni message, ni avertissement. C'est le cas le plus visible du projet.

## À faire

Deux directions, à trancher :

- **Dériver `started_at` de `timing_events`** dans le mapping du seed, avec les opérateurs existants si la structure s'y prête. À vérifier : la whitelist d'opérateurs permet-elle d'atteindre une valeur imbriquée et de la convertir en date ?
- **Si le fichier ne permet honnêtement pas** de dater une session, le dire : livrer un second échantillon horodaté pour le seed, ou faire remonter un `warning` explicite dans la réponse de `/metrics/activity` plutôt qu'une liste vide indistinguable de « aucune donnée ».

La seconde option est la plus honnête si la première n'est pas atteignable — un indicateur vide sans explication se lit comme un bug du produit.

En attendant, la limite est écrite dans la section « Limites connues » du README.

title: fix: start --back deletes the work file with no warning
body:
## Problem

`honepad start <problem> <lang> --back` deletes the candidate's work file with no warning and no confirmation. The console path for the same action warns first.

`cmd_start` (`src/honepad/cli.py:316`) calls `drop_level`, which goes to `slice_work_to_level` → `ensure_work_copy(..., reset=True, level=...)` (`src/honepad/session.py:423`). `reset=True` rewrites the file from the stub, so everything written above the dropped level is gone too.

The console asks first (`src/honepad/console.py:477`):

> `3 reset rewrites your work file from the stub. This deletes what you wrote:`

followed by the work path, then a yes/back/all prompt. The CLI flag does none of that. Its help text (`cli.py:790`) is:

> `--reset starts over at level 1. --back drops one unlocked level.`

Nothing there says the work file is rewritten.

### Repro

1. `honepad start bank_system python3` and reach L2.
2. Write anything in the work file.
3. `honepad start bank_system python3 --back`.
4. The work file is back to the L1 stub. Nothing in the output mentions it.

## Proposed shape

Make the two paths agree. Preferred: `--back` and `--reset` print the same "this deletes what you wrote" line plus the work path, then require confirmation when stdin is a tty, with `--yes` (or `--force`) to skip it for scripted use. When stdin is not a tty, print the warning and proceed — do not hang waiting for input.

At minimum, print the warning line and the work path before the rewrite on both flags, and say so in `--help`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `start --back` prints the work path and a line saying the file is rewritten from the stub, before the rewrite.
- [ ] `start --reset` prints the same.
- [ ] On a tty, both prompt for confirmation; answering no leaves the work file and the session untouched and exits 0.
- [ ] `--yes` skips the prompt.
- [ ] Non-tty stdin never blocks.
- [ ] `start --help` mentions that both flags rewrite the work file.
- [ ] Pytest covers: `--back` declined leaves the file byte-identical; `--back --yes` rewrites it; non-tty does not block.

## Non-goals

- Changing the console `3 reset` wording.
- Backing up the old work file.
- Changing what `drop_level` does to the session.

title: nodeman_client omits `alg` from the generated data JWK, so mqtt-bridge cannot verify signed messages
body:
## Summary

`nodeman_client enroll` generates the node's data-signing JWK without an `alg`
member. NodeMan stores that key as the node's public key, and `mqtt-bridge`
then cannot verify anything the node signs: it reads the algorithm from the
stored JWK, gets `jwa.InvalidKeyAlgorithm`, and discards every message.

A node enrolled with the stock client therefore publishes signed `new_qname`
events that never reach NATS, and the only symptom is an error on the Core
side. EDM itself logs no problem, because `lestrrat-go/jwx` derives `EdDSA`
locally from the private Ed25519 key.

`nodeman/client.py` already imports `jwk_to_alg` and applies it to the
enrollment key and to `data_alg` (lines 29-30 and 66), but not to the key it
generates at line 272:

```python
data_key = JWK.generate(kty=args.kty, crv=args.crv, kid=name)
```

## Reproduction

nodeman `d1ac412`, mqtt-bridge `abe75e1`, edm `64b50bf`.

1. Enroll a node with the stock client:

```sh
nodeman_client --data-jwk-file data.json --tls-cert-file tls.crt \
  --tls-key-file tls.key --tls-ca-file tls-ca.crt \
  enroll --file enrollment.json
jq -c 'keys' data.json
```

```
["crv","d","iss","kid","kty","x"]
```

There is no `alg`. The same omission is visible without the server:

```sh
python -c 'from jwcrypto.jwk import JWK; import json; \
print(sorted(json.loads(JWK.generate(kty="OKP", crv="Ed25519", kid="n").export(private_key=True)).keys()))'
```

```
['crv', 'd', 'kid', 'kty', 'x']
```

2. Point EDM at that `data.json` and publish one `new_qname` event. EDM reports
   no problem and signs the message:

```
{"msg":"starting signing MQTT publisher","jwk_id":"node.edge.test","jwk_alg":"EdDSA"}
```

3. `mqtt-bridge` receives it, fetches the public key from NodeMan, and drops it:

```
{"level":"INFO","msg":"Key not found in cache, contacting nodeman..."}
{"level":"ERROR","msg":"Failed to verify signature on message. Discarding..."}
{"level":"ERROR","msg":"Bad signature from MQTT, err: 'WithKey() option must be
 specified using jwa.SignatureAlgorithm (got jwa.InvalidKeyAlgorithm)'"}
```

Nothing arrives on the NATS subject. Adding `alg` to the same key and
re-enrolling makes the identical event flow through end to end.

## Expected behaviour

A node enrolled with `nodeman_client` should produce messages that `mqtt-bridge`
can verify, without the operator having to patch the client.

## Suggested fix

Set the algorithm on the generated data key, reusing the helper already
imported in this module:

```python
 data_key = JWK.generate(kty=args.kty, crv=args.crv, kid=name)
+data_key["alg"] = jwk_to_alg(data_key)
 x509_key = generate_x509_key(kty=args.kty, crv=args.crv)
```

Normalising `alg` server-side when the enrolled public key is stored would also
protect nodes enrolled by other clients. `mqtt-bridge` deriving the algorithm
from `kty`/`crv` when the stored JWK has none would make the pipeline robust
against either side; I have filed that separately.

title: config: the shipped example sets api_threshold to 0.6, the value the code's own measurement rejected
body:
`palinode.config.yaml.example`, the `search:` block (line 125 onward; the two lines that matter are 134 and 136):

```yaml
  # Default threshold for MCP server searches (lower = more results)
  mcp_threshold: 0.4
  # Default threshold for FastAPI searches (higher = more precision)
  api_threshold: 0.6
  # Default number of results
  default_limit: 10
```

`palinode/core/config.py`, `SearchConfig` (lines 209–210 and 223):

```python
    mcp_threshold: float = 0.4
    api_threshold: float = 0.5
    ...
    default_limit: int = 15
```

**`api_threshold: 0.6` is the value the code's own docstring measured and rejected.** Same class, a few lines up (line 193 onward): *"api_threshold=0.6 measurably drops ~1 in 4 genuinely relevant results overall, and ~2 in 5 on natural-language queries specifically … Lowered to 0.5."* The code was lowered; the example a new user copies into place was not. Anyone who starts from the example gets the measured-worse search. `default_limit` drifted the same way (10 against 15), harmlessly.

**Nothing catches this.** `tests/test_example_config_keys_have_readers.py` checks that every top-level *key* in the example is read somewhere in `palinode/` — deliberately a usage check, not a value check, and it should stay that. So the next time a default is re-measured in code, the example will drift again.

**The fix, two parts:**

1. Set `api_threshold: 0.6` → `0.5` and `default_limit: 10` → `15` in the example.
2. Add a **new** test file — a value-parity test, not an extension of the readers test — that loads the example with `yaml.safe_load`, walks every **scalar leaf**, and asserts it equals the corresponding dataclass default. Three things it has to handle, and all three are in the tree today:
   - **Nested sections are not drift.** A dict in the example against a nested dataclass in code (`embeddings.primary`, `services.api`, `compaction.layer_split`, …) has to be compared leaf by leaf; a top-level comparison reports every one of them as a mismatch.
   - **`consolidation.schedule` differs on purpose.** `"0 11 * * 0"` in the example (line 173) against `"0 3 * * 0"` in code, and line 172 says why: *"Informational — actual schedule lives in crontab."* Allowlist it, with that reason as the entry's comment.
   - **`db_path` is equal in meaning, not in text.** The example sets `".palinode.db"` (line 23); the dataclass default is `None` (`config.py` line 583), a sentinel that resolves to `<memory_dir>/.palinode.db` (line 728) — the same file the example's relative path resolves to (line 617). Either normalize both sides to the resolved path, or allowlist the pair with that reason. A test that reports this as drift is wrong.

Verified on v0.17.0: those four leaves — two real, two equivalent-or-deliberate — are the complete set of scalar differences. The test should fail on the two values before the fix and pass after, with the other two handled.

**If you'd like to take this, please comment here first and wait to be assigned before opening a PR.**

title: An enforced contract on a SELECT * model can never be violated, because the columns come from the contract
body:
#87 added enforced-contract violation detection. On a `select *` model it cannot fire,
because the columns it compares against the contract are read out of the contract.

Measured on dbt-core 1.11.7 + dbt-duckdb 1.10.1:

```sql
-- models/dim.sql, contract enforced, declaring id + amount + tax
{{ config(contract={'enforced': true}) }}
select * from {{ ref('raw_src') }}
```

`raw_src` loses `tax`. `dim.sql` is not edited and its compiled SQL is byte-identical.

```
$ dbt-plan check
SAFE  raw_src (view)
  CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW
  Downstream: dim (1 model(s))
dbt-plan: 1 checked, 1 safe, 0 warning, 0 destructive
exit=0

$ dbt run
2 of 2 ERROR creating sql view model main.dim
Compilation Error in model dim (models/dim.sql)
  This model has an enforced contract that failed.
  Please ensure the name, data_type, and number of columns in your contract
  match the columns in your model's definition.
```

`dim` is listed as downstream and nothing is said about it.

### Why the check cannot fire

`cli.py:951-958` substitutes the manifest's `columns` for `["*"]` before `apply_contract`
runs at `cli.py:997`. For a contracted model the manifest `columns` *are* the contract. So
the produced set and the declared set are the same object by construction, and the
comparison at `predictor.py:982-987` can only ever agree.

`cli.py:1123-1128` then exempts contracted models from the "columns came from the manifest,
not the SQL" escalation — the one guard that would have said the answer rested on an
assumption.

`tests/test_contract_enforcement.py:230-234` pins this: a contracted incremental with
`sync_all_columns` doing `SELECT * FROM raw.orders` asserts exit 0 / `SAFE`.

The substitution itself is right — it is what #28 added, and it is what makes `select *`
models analysable at all. It is only wrong for the one comparison whose entire purpose is
to check the SQL against the contract.

### Shape

`apply_contract` needs the columns the *SQL* produces, not the columns after the manifest
fallback. Two ways, and the first is smaller:

1. Pass the pre-substitution value alongside, and have `apply_contract` refuse when it is
   `["*"]` — the refusal branch it already has at `predictor.py:964-980` and which the CLI
   currently only reaches for a parse failure or an `* except(` sentinel.
2. Resolve the star against the upstream model's real columns, which the relation index can
   already do (`cli.py:511`). That answers the question instead of refusing it, and it is
   the same machinery PR #128 used for cascade.

Refusing is the honest minimum and matches the project's first principle. Resolving is
better and is not much further, because the upstream here is a model in the same project.

### Second half, same measurement

The violation lands on a model whose own file did not change. Cascade already walks to
`dim` and lists it as downstream — it just has no contract check on the downstream pass.
An upstream drop that breaks a downstream *contract* is the same class as `BROKEN_REF`, and
worth reporting through the same channel.

### Evidence

`.context/audit/measurements/contract_star.txt`. Claim F3 of the gap audit's `fragile`
pile. Related: #28, #87, #103.

title: The published JSON schema rejects documents pysmi emits, and is not itself a valid schema
body:
Found by CodeRabbit on #197, verified. Two defects in `pysmi/codegen/schemas/jsondoc-v1.schema.json`, both mine from #193, and one gap in the test that was supposed to catch them.

## 1. `agentcapabilities` is missing from the class enum

`JsonCodeGen` emits `"class": "agentcapabilities"` for an AGENT-CAPABILITIES symbol. The schema's enum does not list it:

```json
"class": {
  "enum": [
    "objecttype", "objectidentity", "moduleidentity", "notificationtype",
    "textualconvention", "type", "objectgroup", "notificationgroup",
    "modulecompliance"
  ]
}
```

So any document containing an AGENT-CAPABILITIES symbol fails validation against the schema pysmi itself publishes:

```
path: ['capsCapability', 'class']
'agentcapabilities' is not one of ['objecttype', 'objectidentity', …]
```

There is no `byClass` branch for it either, so the `capabilities` and `variations` structures were undescribed.

## 2. `$defs/byClass/type` collides with the `type` keyword

The schema does not pass `Draft202012Validator.check_schema`:

```
SchemaError: {'if': {...}, 'then': {...}} is not valid under any of the given schemas
On schema['$defs']['byClass']['type']
```

`$defs/byClass` is itself validated as a schema, so a branch keyed `type` is read as the `type` **keyword**, whose value must name a simple type — not an object. Instance validation never noticed, because a `$ref` resolves the branch directly; only `check_schema` did. A consumer that validates the schema before using it — a reasonable thing to do — gets an error today.

## 3. Why the contract test missed both

`testTheSampleReachesEverySymbolClass` asserted one direction only:

```python
self.assertEqual(declared - reached, set())
```

Every class the schema *declares* is reached by the sample. Nothing asserted the converse — a class the generator *emits* that the schema does not declare. `agentcapabilities` sat in exactly that gap.

And it could not have been caught by widening `MODULES`: no bundled ASN.1 module declares AGENT-CAPABILITIES, only `SNMPv2-CONF`, which defines the macro. The sample has to carry a fixture.

Nothing ran `check_schema` at all.

## Fixed in #197

- `agentcapabilities` added to the enum, with a `byClass` branch, a `$defs/variation`, and a `$defs/variationAccess` — wider than `maxaccess`, because RFC 2580 section 6.5.2 admits `not-implemented`, which no OBJECT-TYPE can declare. Verified against both the description-only and every-field-at-once variation shapes, in both text modes
- `$defs/byClass/type` renamed to `typeSymbol`; both schemas now pass `check_schema`
- `testTheSchemaDeclaresEveryClassTheGeneratorEmits` asserts the converse; `testTheSchemaIsItselfValid` runs `check_schema` over both published schemas; a `CAPABILITIES_MIB` fixture joins the sample so the class is actually reached
- The stale `refinements` description in the schema — which still said an entry whose only payload is a DESCRIPTION is omitted without texts — corrected, since #190 changed that
- `docs/source/jsondoc-schema.rst` gains an `agentcapabilities` section

Both regressions verified: reverting the enum fails three tests, reverting the rename fails one.

## Note on the schema version

Neither change is a schema-version bump. Adding an enum member and describing a class that was already emitted make the schema accept documents it previously rejected — every document that validated before still validates. The rename is internal to `$defs` and changes no instance-visible behaviour.

title: Run-scoped OHLCV identity disagrees between the reader and the dashboards
body:
## Problem

#187 made run-scoped OHLCV reads join through the per-symbol source identity and removed the permissive run-wide path, but only in the Python reader. The generated Grafana price queries still filter with the old permissive expression that accepts a null or `multi` run-level source and otherwise compares against the run-wide value. The two surfaces now answer differently for the same run: for a `multi` run the dashboards return rows of any source for the symbol, while the reader returns only the routed one.

A second effect comes from the same change. The new column defaults to an empty object, so a run row written before the column existed, or backfilled by adding the column, expands to no rows in the lateral join. Because that join is inner, such runs read back as an empty frame rather than an error, and the chart helper then fails when it indexes the first symbol of an empty result. The removed permissive branch used to make these runs readable.

## Expected

One definition of run-scoped OHLCV identity, applied identically by the reader and by every generated dashboard query. A run whose stored identity is empty is either readable through a documented fallback or reported as an explicit error, never silently empty.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Dashboard price queries and the Python reader resolve the same rows for the same run.
- [ ] A run row with an empty source map produces an actionable error or a documented fallback rather than an empty frame.
- [ ] The chart helper does not raise when a run legitimately has no rows.
- [ ] Coverage that pins reader and dashboard agreement.

## References

- `librae/db/timescale_reader.py`
- `librae/app/grafana/generate_dashboards.py`
- `librae/db/charts.py`
- Introduced by #187, related to #193

title: Latitude Watching integration — fix loopback payload and keep media intent out of physical occupancy
body:
## Current status — reverified 2026-08-30 on `7107bda`

Both defects in this issue remain current after the August 30 sensing promotion:

1. `LaptopLoopbackCapture` still produces an obsolete `regions` payload while `/api/automation/screen-color` still validates top-level `r/g/b` via `ScreenColorReport`.
2. accepted Latitude media intent still writes synthetic `latitude_streaming` Couch presence into `PresenceFusion`.

The earlier `7db1d57` Watching/source-ownership work remains useful historical lineage, but it is **not the current canonical HEAD** and did not fix these two integration contracts. Current canonical baseline for this reconciliation is `7107bda`.

## Why

The context-lighting ownership work improved Latitude Watching source arbitration but left two cross-layer contract defects:

- the real laptop loopback producer cannot satisfy the current screen-color request schema;
- media/process ownership is still converted into fake physical occupancy even though HomeHub's source-qualified sensing contract says media evidence cannot establish a face/room.

These are separate from whether Watching itself is justified (#143), from Latitude camera/person reliability (#198), and from projector-safe nighttime lighting (#154).

## What the earlier ownership fix correctly established

Preserve the useful semantics introduced around the `7db1d57` lineage:

- accepted/fresh `process:latitude` Watching may own the laptop ScreenSync lane;
- loopback start/stop follows that ownership rather than raw browser/process presence;
- Watching resolves one authoritative ScreenSync source (`process:latitude` -> laptop, `process:desktop` -> desktop);
- desktop Gaming/Rust rejects laptop frames;
- status exposes authoritative ScreenSync source/reason/targets;
- automatic Watching no longer runs a competing Hue `glisten` effect.

The two defects below should be fixed without reverting those gains.

## Defect 1 — producer/consumer schema mismatch

Current `LaptopLoopbackCapture._loop()` builds a body shaped conceptually as:

```text
{
  "source": "laptop",
  "regions": {
    "left":  {"r": ..., "g": ..., "b": ...},
    "right": {"r": ..., "g": ..., "b": ...}
  }
}
```

Current `ScreenColorReport` requires top-level:

```text
r: int
g: int
b: int
```

The request is therefore rejected by validation before `receive_screen_color()` can perform the accepted source/target arbitration. Existing route tests construct valid `ScreenColorReport` objects directly and therefore do not cover the actual producer-to-request boundary.

The loopback must also treat persistent non-2xx responses as an observable failure instead of looking healthy merely because frame capture continues.

## Defect 2 — media intent leaks into physical occupancy

Accepted Latitude media ownership still creates a synthetic `PresenceReading` equivalent to:

```text
source="latitude_streaming"
face_present=true
zone="couch"
```

That can make `PresenceFusion.latest_zone()` return Couch and can count as strong physical presence for consumers such as navigation/path-light logic.

This violates the current product contract. Accepted media intent is strong **media/source ownership**, not evidence that the Latitude camera saw a person on the Couch.

## Product / technical contract

- Accepted `process:latitude` Watching may own the laptop ScreenSync source.
- Media/process evidence must not create `face_present`, physical zone, posture, or strong-presence authority.
- Latitude physical person/Couch authority comes from the YOLO-gated camera path under #198.
- Desktop physical Desk/Bed authority comes from the source-qualified Desktop camera path under #201.
- Source selection must not write synthetic physical evidence back into fusion.
- Losing automatic Latitude Watching authority stops/cancels only the loopback that automatic ownership started.
- Non-authoritative screen-source frames remain no-op writes as established by the current ownership contract.

## Implementation direction

1. Choose one current wire shape for laptop loopback and `/screen-color`; prefer the existing simple `ScreenColorReport` unless regional semantics are independently required.
2. Make the real producer emit a body that validates against that contract.
3. Treat non-2xx responses as bounded observable errors without log spam.
4. Add a producer-to-schema/route integration regression; do not rely only on hand-constructed route models.
5. Remove `latitude_streaming` as a physical `PresenceReading`; retain media/source ownership in Activity/ScreenSync context only.
6. Add regression coverage proving media playback alone cannot create Couch or strong physical presence in `PresenceFusion`.
7. Preserve current accepted-source arbitration, async lifecycle, Gaming/Rust rejection, and status observability.

## Acceptance

- A real `LaptopLoopbackCapture` frame is accepted by the current `/api/automation/screen-color` schema.
- Latitude-owned Watching can drive its intended ScreenSync targets end-to-end in a focused in-process/fake-Hue integration test.
- Persistent request rejection is observable.
- Desktop-owned Watching rejects laptop frames; Latitude-owned Watching rejects desktop frames.
- Desktop Gaming/Rust still rejects laptop frames before Hue/Rust writes.
- Accepted Latitude media playback creates **no** physical Couch/face/strong-presence evidence.
- Physical Couch authority continues to come from the Latitude camera path only.
- Production deployment/live Hue verification remains a separate explicitly authorized step.

## Boundaries / related

- #143 owns credible Watching/playback-intent detection.
- #198 owns deployed Latitude YOLO-gated physical authority and its remaining Couch acceptance.
- #201 owns deployed Desktop Desk/Bed physical localization acceptance.
- #154 owns nighttime projector-safe path-light/ScreenSync behavior once a valid stream exists.
- The earlier context-lighting ownership audit remains useful provenance, not current canonical state by itself.

title: supporter-loop: first live sweep fails closed — stargazers 403 under GITHUB_TOKEN + precondition (a) counts all repo runs past the 1,000 cap
body:
## 目的 (Why)

The first live weekly sweep (caty-ai/x-collector run 34100523613, schedule 2026-09-07 08:25Z) failed closed: `decide` emitted `sweep_gate=false` and `stargazers=[]`, so `act` reported `sweep preconditions (a)-(e) failed; all API cleanup skipped` and `alert` fired. Two independent defects, both measured with a throwaway probe (run 34107453239, branch deleted):

- **A — stargazers 403 under `GITHUB_TOKEN`.** `GET /repos/{source_repo}/stargazers?per_page=100` returns HTTP 403 "Resource not accessible by integration" for the workflow token even on a public repo (also with `--paginate --slurp`). decide line ~368 calls `pages "$GH_TOKEN" ".../stargazers"` → gate=false, empty list. Fix: read the star list with `SUPPORTER_LEDGER_TOKEN` (a fine-grained PAT reads public repos implicitly — contract §8.4 already names this platform property). Contract v1.11 (caty-ai/x-collector, sibling Issue) adds the one-sentence read-only exception to §0-4.
- **B — precondition (a) counts every run in the repo and hits the 1,000 cap.** `runs()` (decide ~353) lists `actions/runs?per_page=100&<query>` for the whole repository. With zero successful scheduled sweeps the fallback `runs ''` returns total_count 1691 (17 pages, 36 s) → the `.total_count<1000` check silently returns 1 → gate=false. Chicken-and-egg: it can never pass until a sweep has already passed. Fix: list `actions/workflows/supporter-loop.yml/runs?per_page=100&<query>` (measured: total_count 11, 1 page, <1 s, exit 0 with `GITHUB_TOKEN`). The `select(.path==...)` filter and the 1,000-cap fail-closed check stay.

Without this the sweep (unstar cleanup, expiry re-arm, SUPPORTERS.md regeneration) never runs and the owner gets a Telegram alert every Monday.

## 完了条件 (Done when)

- [ ] decide's stargazer listing uses `$LEDGER_TOKEN`, never `$GH_TOKEN`; `SUPPORTER_LOOP_TOKEN` still never appears in decide
- [ ] `runs()` queries `repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/workflows/supporter-loop.yml/runs` (per-workflow endpoint); the 1,000-cap and page-error fail-closed checks unchanged
- [ ] `supporter-loop/fixtures/workflow/test-interface.py` pins both: (a) the stargazers call is not made with `$GH_TOKEN` (b) `runs()` uses the per-workflow endpoint
- [ ] Header comment / README reference contract v1.11
- [ ] Local CI green: actionlint + shellcheck + yaml load + `check-decide-static.sh` + every `fixtures/workflow/test-*.py`
- [ ] GitHub CI green on the PR
- [ ] Five heterogeneous seats (permission-boundary risk): no open blocking finding
- [ ] Post-merge: next scheduled sweep (or a dispatch) reaches `sweep_gate=true`, stargazers non-empty, `act` success — recorded on this Issue

## 触るファイル / モジュール予測

- .github/workflows/supporter-loop-reusable.yml
- supporter-loop/fixtures/workflow/test-interface.py
- supporter-loop/README.md

## 想定スコープ

Do: the two credential/endpoint changes above, the test pins, version references. No permission boundary is widened: the ledger token gains no write path, the loop token stays act-only, `decide` permissions map unchanged.
Do not: add `workflow_dispatch` to the caller (separate owner decision), change the frozen `workflow_call` interface (inputs/secrets/descriptions), touch tier-1/2/3 event paths, or the #87 follow-up.

## 前提条件 (Blocked by)

Contract v1.11 in caty-ai/x-collector (sibling Issue, filed together); merge order: contract first, then this workflow.

title: The browser axe and reflow gates have never rendered right-to-left
body:
## What

`tools/a11y_browser/axe.spec.ts` and `tools/a11y_browser/reflow.spec.ts` set no
language anywhere. Neither file contains `locale`, `lang`, `dir` or
`Accept-Language`, and `playwright.config.ts` has a single project using the stock
`devices["Desktop Chrome"]`, which sends `Accept-Language: en-US`. So
`server._lang()` negotiates `en` on every request the browser gates make, and both
gates have only ever rendered `<html lang="en" dir="ltr">`.

ledger ships en/es/fr/ar. `i18n._RTL_LANGS` marks `ar` right-to-left,
`i18n.text_direction` derives the direction, and `render._page` threads it into the
document root. `docs/I18N.md` §"RTL & text direction (G10)" states that "the browser
mirrors the whole layout for an RTL reader with no per-element CSS."

That claim has never been checked by a browser. `tests/test_i18n_rtl.py` asserts
`dir="rtl"` against the *string* `_page()` returns, which cannot tell anyone whether
a 320px column still reflows or whether axe finds a violation once the layout
mirrors. The two gates that could answer it have been rendering the other direction.

## Evidence that it matters

Running the reflow gate with the layout actually mirrored fails immediately on every
page:

```
Error: about (/about) scrolls horizontally at 320px:
content is 9999px wider than the viewport (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 Reflow)
```

`web/static/app.css` parks `.skip-link` at `position: absolute; left: -9999px`, the
old off-screen idiom. Under `ltr` that is harmless, because a browser does not scroll
to reach content at a negative `left`. Under `rtl` the inline start edge is the right
one, so the link sits outside the scrollable origin and the document genuinely gains
9,999 pixels of horizontal scroll — on every page of the Arabic archive, for as long
as `ar` has shipped, with a required check green the whole time.

The element-level half of the same gate is blind here for a second reason: it tests
`box.right > limit` only, and a mirrored layout spills off the left.

## Scope

- A second Playwright project rendering the canonical pages right-to-left.
- An assertion that the loaded document really came back in the direction the run
  claims to be auditing, so a locale that fails to arrive fails the run instead of
  passing as a second English pass.
- The reflow element scan reading the inline **end** edge rather than the right one.
- The `.skip-link` declaration.

## Out of scope

- `keyboard.spec.ts`. Tab order follows DOM order, which mirroring does not change.
- Auditing es/fr, which are both `ltr` and add no direction coverage.
- RM6 captions.

## Relationship to #180

#180 (RM6/RM7, deferred, partly human) records the general RTL gap and says in terms
that "the existing axe and reflow gates would not surface [RTL], since the demo
content is left-to-right." This issue is the narrow, automatable half of that
sentence: making those two gates render the direction, and the one CSS defect doing so
uncovers. The rest of #180 — captions, and the human review of Arabic typography and
tone — is untouched and stays there.

*Filed with AI assistance.*

title: Observation.category: dual coding inside one category element violates JP Core / eCS category slicing (286k validator errors)
body:
## Problem

HAPI validation of the 2026-07-17 JP full export (437,669 resources) reports 286,168 category-related errors on Observations, introduced by the dual-coding normalization from #188/#190:

```
(A) 値は 'http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/observation-category' ですが、
    'http://jpfhir.jp/fhir/core/CodeSystem/JP_SimpleObservationCategory_CS' でなければなりません   182,662
(B) 値は 'http://jpfhir.jp/fhir/core/CodeSystem/JP_SimpleObservationCategory_CS' ですが、
    'http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/observation-category' でなければなりません              103,670
(C) Observation.category:laboratory.coding: 最大許容値 = 1、見つかった値 = 2                        31,172
```

Breakdown by resource-id prefix: (A) vs 151,490 / lab 31,006 / mb 166; (B) vs 103,670; (C) lab 31,006 / mb 166.

Current emitted shape (one category element, two codings):

```json
"category": [{
  "coding": [
    {"system": "http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/observation-category", "code": "vital-signs"},
    {"system": "http://jpfhir.jp/fhir/core/CodeSystem/JP_SimpleObservationCategory_CS", "code": "vital-signs"}
  ]
}]
```

## Spec (verified against StructureDefinition snapshots)

**JP_Observation_VitalSigns** (jp-core 1.2.0, `http://jpfhir.jp/fhir/core/StructureDefinition/JP_Observation_VitalSigns`): `Observation.category` is sliced by `coding.system` with `rules=open`; slice `first` (1..*) has `coding.system fixedUri = JP_SimpleObservationCategory_CS` + `coding.code fixedCode = vital-signs`; slice `second` (0..*) has `coding.system fixedUri = JP_ObservationVitalSignsCategory_CS`. A category element mixing HL7 + JP codings matches a slice but fails the slice's `coding.system` 1..1 fixedUri on the other coding — producing both error directions (A)+(B) when the HL7 base VitalSigns profile (auto-applied via magic LOINC codes) also demands its `VSCat` slice.

**JP_Observation_LabResult_eCS** (clinical-information-sharing 1.12.0): `Observation.category` is 1..1, slice `laboratory` has `coding` **1..1** with `coding.system fixedUri = JP_SimpleObservationCategory_CS` + `coding.code fixedCode = laboratory`. Dual coding directly violates coding max=1 (error C), and the HL7 coding violates the fixedUri (error A on lab/mb).

## Correct shapes

Vital signs — two category elements (HL7 element allowed by `rules=open`, satisfies base VSCat; JP element satisfies JP Core slice `first`):

```json
"category": [
  {"coding": [{"system": "http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/observation-category", "code": "vital-signs"}]},
  {"coding": [{"system": "http://jpfhir.jp/fhir/core/CodeSystem/JP_SimpleObservationCategory_CS", "code": "vital-signs"}]}
]
```

Lab / microbiology (eCS): single category element, single JP coding:

```json
"category": [{"coding": [{"system": "http://jpfhir.jp/fhir/core/CodeSystem/JP_SimpleObservationCategory_CS", "code": "laboratory"}]}]
```

Note the official JP Core example `Observation-jp-observation-vitalsigns-example-1` also uses two separate category elements (JP_SimpleObservationCategory_CS + JP_ObservationVitalSignsCategory_CS), never mixed codings.

## Fix

Rewrite `_normalize_jp_observation_category` (JP-only post-emit walker in `fhir_r4_adapter.py`):
- `vital-signs` → two category elements as above (HL7 first, JP second)
- everything else (incl. eCS lab) → single JP CS coding; drop the eCS dual-coding special case from #190
- keep: fabricated-URL normalization, foreign-system coding preservation, display omission, idempotency

Expected impact: −286k errors (validator feedback 2026-07-17 §【最優先 3】).

title: WS 那个 64 KiB 单帧上限形同虚设，1 MB / 10 MB 的 text 和 binary 帧都被服务端照单全收、json.loads + dispatch 跑全套
body:
WS 那个 64 KiB 单帧上限只挡得了 binary 挡不了 text，我刚把 1 MB 的 JSON 直接打进去被照单全收

我在测协议层硬上限那条路径——`backend/app/transport/websocket/handler.py:142` 上明明白白写着 `_max_frame_bytes = 64 * 1024`，`handler.py:310` 的 `_loop` 里也有：

```python
payload = raw.get("bytes") or raw.get("text") or ""
if len(payload) > self._max_frame_bytes:
    await _fail(self.ws, code="frame_too_large", close_code=4410, max_kb=64)
    return
```

文档协议层也是这么说的，audio 单帧 64 KiB、超了 4410 关连接。我想顺便看下普通 JSON 帧是不是也走这个闸，于是拿 `websockets` 库往同一条访谈 WS 上丢 text 帧，从 65 537 一路打到 10 000 000 字节：

```python
async with websockets.connect(
    f'ws://127.0.0.1:8000/ws/v1/interview/{sid}',
    subprotocols=[f'bearer.{TOK}'],
    max_size=100_000_000,   # 客户端不限
) as ws:
    await ws.send(json.dumps({'type':'hello', ...}))
    hello_msg = await ws.recv()  # → hello
    # 现在发超大 JSON
    big = {'type':'listen','state':'start','data':'x' * N}
    await ws.send(json.dumps(big))
    resp = await ws.recv()
```

跑出来的结果：

```
N=    100000 (msg 100048 B)  : processed → coaching.update
N=    500000 (msg 500048 B)  : processed → coaching.update
N=   1000000 (msg 1000048 B) : processed → coaching.update
N=   5000000 (msg 5000048 B) : processed → coaching.update
N=  10000000 (msg 10000048 B): processed → coaching.update
```

10 MB 的 JSON 帧被服务端 json.loads 解析 → `listen:start` 路径被正常触发 → 推了 coaching.update 回来，全程 0.33 秒结束。`frame_too_large` 那条岔路一次都没走过。

我又把 text 换成纯文本（`'X' * 65_537`）：依然收下。然后换成 binary audio（同样的长度）：**这条**被拦下来了——`{"type":"error","code":"frame_too_large","i18n_key":"ws.frame.too_large","i18n_params":{"max_kb":64},"message":"Single frame exceeds 64 KB","close":4410}`，连 `code=4410` 关掉。

行为不一致让我有点意外，于是我又把 binary 也加到 1 MB 重跑一遍，结果……1 MB 的 binary 也被服务端收了，没有 4410。我之前能看到 binary 被拦下来那次，是因为连接拿到的是 `connection.conflict`（pending 状态），跟是否超限没关系——那次走的是「handler 在 conflict 后直接 _loop 起手就把第一帧撞上 64 KiB」的偶然路径，不是真的拦下大帧。

所以两种帧型在握手成功后的稳态路径上都通——1 MB、10 MB 都是「JSON 解析 → dispatch」一路走完，64 KiB 那道闸从来不开。我看了一眼 `raw.get("bytes") or raw.get("text") or ""` 之后那个比较，最合理的解释是 Starlette/Uvicorn 的 `WebSocket.receive()` 在 socket 读侧做了定长缓冲（比如每次从 socket 拉 4 KiB），handler 里 `await self.ws.receive()` 每次只拿到一小块，导致 `len(payload)` 永远是几千字节，永远 ≤ 64 KiB。比较的是 Starlette 缓冲后的 chunk 而不是完整的 WS message，于是「单帧上限」实际上被 Starlette 的缓冲粒度给稀释掉了——binary 那次拦下来多半是因为某个边界 chunk 大小正好踩过了 64 KiB。

不管具体哪一层在稀释，行为事实就是：任何持有效 JWT 的人都能给自己跑的访谈 WS 喂无限大的 JSON 帧，服务端会同步 `json.loads` + 跑一遍 dispatch pipeline（`listen:start` 那条还触发 engine.first_compute + 重新推 coaching snapshot）。CPU 在单条连接上就够打满，连 100 个连接并发就能让 uvicorn 单进程卡住。我没往上压到 100 MB——担心触发 ASR 上游对端断开把后端进程一起带挂——但 10 MB 单条 0.33 秒吃下来已经能看出是线性增长，没有拦的迹象。

我以为的行为是：连接握手成功后，无论是 text 还是 binary，单帧超 64 KiB 直接 4410 关连接（注释里也明确这么写的）。实际是 text / binary 帧都能灌到 MB 级别、`frame_too_large` 几乎不会触发，只能靠 Starlette 自己的 message size 上限兜底——而项目里我看 grep 没设 `websocket_max_message_size`。

修法上我直觉是把闸挪到「整条 WS message」而不是「单次 receive()」，比如在 _loop 维护一个 `current_message` 缓冲，看见 FIN 帧或 chunk 大小合计 > 64 KiB 就 4410 关掉；或者更省事的：直接用 Starlette 的 `websocket_max_message_size=64*1024` 配置交给库来挡，省得自己维护缓冲。但我对 Starlette 这条配置项的覆盖粒度（是 message 维度还是 socket 读缓冲维度）没把握，如果需要我可以按这两条思路各跑一遍并发确认。

title: Historical Pathé confirmations (2009-2019, gmail archive) use 4 unconfigured domains and templates
body:
## Description

Ryan's real Pathé booking history goes back to 2009, but it doesn't live
in the mailbox `pathe-mail-import` already knows about. It's in
`alrayyes@gmail.com`'s "All Mail" (mutt's local Maildir sync exposes it
as `Archive`) - a completely different account from the `ryan@ryankes.eu`
one `extra_paths` (#188/#191) was built for.

Scanned it directly (read-only, no import run): **311 unique Pathé-related
messages, 2009-2019**, across four sender domains, none configured today:

| domain | count | era |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pathe.emsecure.net` | 119 | 2014-2018ish |
| `pathe.nl` | 99 | 2011-2013ish |
| `e.pathe.nl` | 57 | 2013-2016ish |
| `info.pathe.nl` | 36 | 2018-2019 |

**The template genuinely changed multiple times across that decade** -
this isn't one more domain to add to the existing chain list, it's at
least four structurally distinct confirmation formats:

1. `pathe.nl` (2012ish): a fully-inline, real plain-text body - no HTML
   part needed at all. Dutch, "Pathé - BEVESTIGING RESERVERING", date as
   `Za 8-9-2012 - 20:35`, seat as `rij 7, stoel 3`.
2. `e.pathe.nl` (2013ish, "Pathé Mobiel"): HTML-only real content behind
   a "your client doesn't support HTML" plain-text placeholder. Title,
   `Vrijdag 28 juni, 20:30`, `Zaal 4`, `Rij 7 Stoel 13`.
3. `pathe.emsecure.net` (2014ish, "Ticketbevestiging"): same
   placeholder-plus-HTML shape as #2, different wording and layout -
   `Rij: 11 Stoel: 10`, a `referentiecode`, a named greeting.
4. `info.pathe.nl` (2019, "Reservering \<title\> - Referentie: ..."):
   same shape again, different wording again - `Rij: 3 stoel: 14`, an
   empty/broken name greeting, a different customer-service phone format.

**Architectural point, not just "four more regexes":** every one of
these is Pathé changing their own email template over a decade, the
same way the three templates already found in the `ryankes.eu` mailbox
(#158, #163, #171) are three points on the same timeline. `pathe.py`
today is a flat `_parse_plain_text_shape` /
`_parse_html_derived_shape` pair, and every new era so far has meant
adding a new function and OR-ing it into `parse_pathe_email`. That
scales linearly in code but not in confidence - nothing stops a future
template from accidentally matching an older regex's partial pattern,
and nothing documents which era a given regex is even for. Worth
deciding, before adding a fifth and sixth shape, whether this wants a
small ordered registry of named, dated template matchers instead of an
ever-growing OR-chain - self-documenting ("this handles 2014-2018
Ticketbevestiging emails") and safer to extend.

**Confirmed a second, independent bug while building fixtures for
this**: `_extract_body`'s digit-based placeholder heuristic (#171) isn't
robust. All three HTML-behind-a-placeholder templates above (2, 3, 4)
have a "your client doesn't support HTML, click here" plain-text part
whose "click here" link contains a tracking ID with digits in it - so
the heuristic's actual test ("does the plain part contain a digit")
returns true for the *placeholder itself*, and `extract_envelope`
returns the useless placeholder text instead of falling through to the
real HTML. This isn't specific to these old domains; any chain whose
"view in browser" boilerplate happens to include a digit anywhere would
hit the same failure silently. Confirmed against current `main` with
all three fixtures below.

## Acceptance criteria

- A decision on the architecture question above, written down (registry
  of dated template matchers vs. continuing to OR new functions
  together), before more per-era parsing is added.
- `_extract_body`'s placeholder-vs-real-content decision no longer
  depends on "does it contain a digit" - needs a check that doesn't
  false-positive on a tracking URL's digits (e.g. matching the
  placeholder's actual boilerplate phrasing, or a minimum-real-content
  heuristic instead of a digit count).
- At least the `pathe.nl` 2012 and one HTML-behind-placeholder template
  parse correctly, proving the approach generalizes rather than being a
  one-off fix for a single sample.
- No change to how `ryankes.eu`'s already-working templates parse.

## Definition of done

- Redacted, real fixtures for all four templates (attached as follow-up
  comments) added as regression tests.
- A path to actually importing this history without blowing the OMDb
  daily budget in one run - out of scope for the parsing fix itself, but
  worth a mention/follow-up ticket once parsing exists, since 311
  historical entries dwarfs the ~354-call restore already run once for
  the existing 369-entry calendar.
- `docs/pathe-mail-import.md` documents that a project can span multiple
  mail accounts and mailbox *formats*, not just multiple folders of one
  account (#188's `extra_paths` only adds more `mbox` files to
  `MboxMailClient`). This archive is only reachable locally via mutt's
  Maildir sync (`~/.local/share/mail/gmail/Archive`, `mailbox.Maildir`
  format) - Thunderbird never synced this account's full history.
  `MboxMailClient` can't read it regardless of `extra_paths`, so this
  needs either a `MaildirMailClient` alongside the existing one, or the
  gmail account re-synced into Thunderbird's mbox format first (a
  Thunderbird-side workaround, not a code fix) - flag as a likely
  follow-up rather than assuming `extra_paths` already covers it.

title: fix: config.py のプレースホルダーデフォルト値が起動時に無音で 503 を引き起こす
body:
## 問題

`academic_paper/config.py` の `embedding_svc_url` デフォルトが `"http://<internal-host>:9092"`、`qdrant_url` が `"http://<internal-host>:6333"` という無効な URL になっている。env を設定し忘れた新規デプロイでは、起動は成功するが全インジェスト・全検索リクエストが 503 で失敗し続け、スタートアップ probe のログを見ないと原因が分からない。

## 場所

- `academic_paper/config.py` — `embedding_svc_url`、`qdrant_url` デフォルト値

## 提案

```python
from pydantic import field_validator

@field_validator('embedding_svc_url', 'qdrant_url')
@classmethod
def reject_placeholder(cls, v: str) -> str:
    if '<' in v:
        raise ValueError(f'Set {v!r} via environment variable before starting')
    return v
```

pydantic の `model_post_init` またはバリデータでプレースホルダー文字列を起動時に即座に拒否し、設定漏れを明示的なエラーで通知する。

title: Three gaps in the enterprise-reader exclusivity guard
body:
Found by automated review on #187. Three smaller findings against the same guard, all self-contained enough to fix without a live probe.

## 1. A reader group whose members may edit membership

`analysis/checks/_permissions.py` applies no guard when an enterprise-reader group sets `allow_members_edit_membership: true`, and the security phase reconciles that setting *before* the account is enrolled. The enrolled account can then add arbitrary principals to the group, so the one-account exclusivity check holds only for the duration of the deployment and the group's Read access can be propagated freely afterwards.

A validator rule refusing that setting on an enterprise-reader group closes it. Needs a test that makes it fire.

## 2. The already-enrolled path skips the post-write exclusivity re-read

In `_reader_enrolment.js.j2`, when the named reader is already present the code `continue`s without re-reading membership. If another administrator adds a principal after `before = await readMembers()`, the run reports success on a group that now holds a second reader. The post-write `strays` check added in this PR covers only the POST path and is bypassed here.

The fix is to perform the same final exclusivity read before continuing.

## 3. `--enterprise-reader` is accepted when the selected site role grants the group nothing

For a multi-role mapping whose default policy is scoped to `hq`, a build using `--site-role branch --enterprise-reader ...` passes validation as long as the group receives `Read` somewhere in `hq`. But `build_schema_json` emits only `branch` assignments and `permissions_for_entity` excludes the `hq` default — so the account is permanently enrolled, the run reports success, and it can read none of this site's lists.

Effective grants should be checked for the *selected* role, failing closed when that role grants the target group nothing.

Overlaps #194, which is the manifest-reporting half of the same confusion.

Related: #198, #199.

title: SELECT SQL 実行: nl2sql.profiles.manage 保持者の表スコープが無制限になる
body:
## 症状

`backend/app/features/nl2sql/router.py` の `_allowed_profile_ids_for_request` は `PROFILE_MANAGE_PERMISSION` を持つ principal に `None` を返し、`resolve_direct_sql_allowed_objects` はスコープ強制をしない。

`menu.glossary_rules` / `menu.global_rules` / `menu.ontology_build` / `menu.profiles` はこの権限を含意するため、たとえば用語管理者に `menu.direct_sql` を足すだけで `ALL_TABLES` を含む任意表(DeepSec 無効なら全データ)を SELECT できる。

`execute` route の docstring は「system admin / 認証無効時は request の allowed_objects のみ」としており、実装と一致していない。

## 修正方針

非 system admin の profile manager は「全(有効)プロファイルの許可オブジェクトの和集合」をスコープにする(`profile_ids` に全プロファイル id を渡す)。既存テスト `test_execute_route_keeps_request_scope_for_admin_and_unauthenticated` は admin / 認証無効のみを対象にしているので、profile manager のケースを追加する。

title: Busy-retry re-runs the whole impl function, duplicating non-idempotent operations
body:
Split out of #183. Found while investigating the freeze reports, but it is an independent, currently-live bug.

## Problem

The retry loop in `src/utils/com_wrapper.py:117-134` retries by re-invoking `func` — the **entire `_impl` function**, not the individual COM call that was rejected:

```python
for attempt in range(_RETRY_MAX + 1):
    try:
        result = func(*args, **kwargs)
```

The comment at `com_wrapper.py:26` says:

> Both mean the call was never started, so retrying is always safe.

That is true **per COM call**, and false **per impl function**. If `_add_slide_impl(count=5)` is rejected while creating the third slide, the retry starts from scratch and slides 1–2 are created a second time. The same applies to every multi-step or non-idempotent impl: bulk slide operations, table row/column insertion, shape duplication.

## Second, related defect: the retry budget exceeds the call timeout

- Worker side: up to `_RETRY_MAX = 5` retries with `_RETRY_INTERVAL = 3` s ⇒ **up to 15 s of `time.sleep`** plus six attempts' worth of actual COM time.
- Caller side: `execute()` gives up at 30 s (`com_wrapper.py:163`).

When the total exceeds 30 s the caller abandons the future and reports failure, while the worker keeps retrying and **eventually performs the operation**. The client sees an error; PowerPoint gets the edit. (Cancelling abandoned futures — #199, fix 1 — removes this particular path, but the budget mismatch is worth fixing on its own.)

## Proposed fixes

- Give the worker a deadline covering all retries, set below `execute()`'s timeout; and/or replace the fixed 3 s interval with exponential backoff (0.5/1/2/4 s) to compress the budget.
- Restrict retrying to idempotent operations — either an explicit flag on `execute()`, or push retry down to individual COM calls. The latter is the correct fix but a much larger change.
- At minimum, correct the misleading comment at `com_wrapper.py:26`.

## Note on `IMessageFilter`

The COM-standard answer to rejected calls is `CoRegisterMessageFilter` + `IMessageFilter::RetryRejectedCall`, which retries at exactly the right granularity. It is not an option here: pywin32 does not expose it (`hasattr(pythoncom, 'CoRegisterMessageFilter')` is `False`). It also would not help with hung calls (#199) — `RetryRejectedCall` only fires for `RPC_E_CALL_REJECTED` / `RPC_E_SERVERCALL_RETRYLATER`. The same granularity benefit is reachable without it, as described above.

Related: #198, #199

title: Auto-discovery drops every valid sitemap directive after the first
body:
# Auto-discovery drops every valid sitemap directive after the first


robots.parse_robots preserves all Sitemap directives, but crawl-site auto-discovery and site-audit select only index 0. Valid pages declared only by later independent sitemap files are omitted from crawl seeding, reconciliation, and bounded audit page selection.

## Version and affected interface

SEOHEAD Tools `3.0.0`, audited commit `cfda214c0c14a764f8f14fa270e765ccac2fe4ad`. The behavior was independently rechecked on `1e630bf5d619cc35ddaf90c39857a2b98781e890`.

Affected surface: `seohead/servers/handlers.py`, `seohead/audit/site.py`.

## Actual behavior

```text
Two valid directives were injected offline. Both the real crawl handler and site-audit invoked sitemap crawling only for https://example.test/sitemap-pages.xml; neither received https://example.test/product-b from the second sitemap.
```

## Minimal offline reproduction

Run from a checkout with the project dependencies installed. Save the script outside the source tree, then run `PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python /path/to/reproducer.py`. It uses synthetic data or injected boundaries; no paid provider or live audit target is needed.

### `reproduce_auto_discover_drops_second_sitemap.py`

```python
"""Offline handler-level reproduction for sitemap auto-discovery loss.

The fixture contains two valid Sitemap directives in robots.txt, each with a
different declared URL.  No network calls are made: the robots reader,
sitemap crawler, and spider are replaced only at their external boundaries.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import seohead.crawl.spider as spider
import seohead.tools.robots as robots
import seohead.tools.sitemap as sitemap
from seohead.audit.site import PAGE_TOOLS, SITE_TOOLS, audit_site
from seohead.crawl.collect import PageRecord
from seohead.crawl.spider import SpiderResult
from seohead.servers import handlers


FIRST = "https://example.test/sitemap-pages.xml"
SECOND = "https://example.test/sitemap-products.xml"
calls: list[str] = []
seeds: list[str] = []


def fake_sitemap_crawl(url: str, concurrency: int = 3) -> dict:
    calls.append(url)
    return {
        "urls": [
            {"loc": "https://example.test/page-a"}
            if url == FIRST
            else {"loc": "https://example.test/product-b"}
        ]
    }


def fake_spider(*args: object, **kwargs: object) -> SpiderResult:
    seeds.extend(kwargs.get("seed_urls") or [])
    result = SpiderResult()
    result.pages = [
        PageRecord(
            url="https://example.test/",
            status_code=200,
            content_type="text/html",
        )
    ]
    result.seed_urls = list(kwargs.get("seed_urls") or [])
    return result


robots.check_robots = lambda url: {"sitemaps": [FIRST, SECOND]}  # type: ignore[assignment]
sitemap.crawl = fake_sitemap_crawl  # type: ignore[assignment]
spider.crawl_site = fake_spider  # type: ignore[assignment]

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    config = Path(directory) / "crawl.json"
    config.write_text(json.dumps({"sitemaps": {"auto_discover": True}}))
    result = handlers.crawl_site(url="https://example.test/", config=str(config))

output = {
    "robots_sitemaps": [FIRST, SECOND],
    "sitemap_crawl_calls": calls,
    "seed_urls_received_by_spider": seeds,
    "reported_sitemap_url": result["discovery"]["sitemap_url"],
}
print(json.dumps(output, indent=2))

assert calls == [FIRST]
assert seeds == ["https://example.test/page-a"]
assert "https://example.test/product-b" not in seeds

# The bounded site-audit has the same loss: it selects only the first directive
# before it invokes the real sitemap-crawl handler slot.  Skip its unrelated
# networked tools and page tools so this is also fully offline.
site_calls: list[str] = []
handlers.robots_check = lambda url: {"ok": True, "sitemaps": [FIRST, SECOND]}  # type: ignore[assignment]
handlers.HANDLERS["sitemap_crawl"] = lambda url: (  # type: ignore[assignment]
    site_calls.append(url) or {"ok": True, "urls": [{"loc": url + "/page"}]}
)
site_skip = [tool for tool in SITE_TOOLS if tool not in {"robots_check", "sitemap_crawl"}]
site_skip += list(PAGE_TOOLS)
site_result = audit_site("https://example.test/", skip=site_skip)
site_output = {
    "robots_sitemaps": [FIRST, SECOND],
    "sitemap_crawl_calls": site_calls,
    "selected_page_urls": [page["url"] for page in site_result["pages"]],
}
print(json.dumps(site_output, indent=2))

assert site_calls == [FIRST]
assert site_result["pages"][0]["url"] == FIRST + "/page"
```

## Cause locations

- [seohead/servers/handlers.py:111](https://github.com/PavloSEO/seotools/blob/cfda214c0c14a764f8f14fa270e765ccac2fe4ad/seohead/servers/handlers.py#L111)
- [seohead/audit/site.py:252](https://github.com/PavloSEO/seotools/blob/cfda214c0c14a764f8f14fa270e765ccac2fe4ad/seohead/audit/site.py#L252)

## Expected behavior and acceptance criteria

- Automatic discovery expands every robots Sitemap directive and seeds their de-duplicated URL union.
- Native reconciliation and discovery metadata use that same union and identify every source used.
- site-audit samples the combined sitemap result within its existing configured limit.
- Offline tests cover two independent robots sitemap directives for crawl-site and site-audit.

## Related work checked

#28, #124, #145, #146, #148, #152, #165. The listed issues cover the initial seeding/reconciliation feature, protocol limits, URL normalization, parse-failure accounting, gzip safety, MCP reachability, or uninvoked checks. This regression occurs when multiple ordinary valid Sitemap directives exist and consumers never load later sources.

This report describes one independently reproduced cause. Related manifestations are grouped above; it does not request a wholesale rewrite.

title: Agent loop: answer with what was gathered when the tool budget runs out
body:
When the turn loop runs out of tool iterations it discards everything it found. Asked to
find five book bloggers with contact details, Kasa searched for eight rounds, made sixteen
tool calls, and posted this:

```
프로필 URL을 찾았어요. 각 작가의 프로필 페이지에서 소개글·연락처를 확인해볼게요.

stopped after 16 tool call(s) without an answer — the model kept asking for tools.
Try a narrower question.
```

The visible sentence is not an answer. It is a leftover preamble: `kasa/core/agent.py`
keeps `text = response.text or text`, so the last non-empty text survives even though the
model was mid-plan when the loop cut it off. Several profiles had been found by then and
none of them reached the person who asked.

The cause is `kasa/core/agent.py:249`. With calls still outstanding on the last permitted
pass, the loop answers each `tool_use` with `"Tool iteration limit reached; stopping."`,
sets `stop_reason="max_iterations"` and breaks. The error results are correct — an
unanswered `tool_use` poisons every later turn — but nothing then asks the model to say
what it learned. The loop already allocates one extra pass (`max_tool_iterations + 2`);
that pass is only reached when the model volunteers a tool-free reply, never when it is
still calling tools, which is exactly the case that needs it.

Four profiles found is a good answer to "find me five". Nothing is a bad one, and the note
blames the question.

**Scope**
- On the final pass, re-call the model with `tools=()` rather than breaking. Both compat
  layers omit the key entirely when tools are empty (`kasa/llm/anthropic_compat.py:77`,
  `kasa/llm/openai_compat.py:84`), so the model has no tool to reach for and must write
  prose from the transcript it already has.
- The pending `tool_use` blocks still need their error results first, in the same order
  and before the final request — the transcript has to stay valid whether or not the last
  call succeeds.
- Say in that request that the tool budget is spent and this is the last word, so the
  reply summarises findings instead of announcing another plan.
- `AgentResult.note` should stop reading as user error. `max_iterations` with text now
  means "this is partial", not "try a narrower question".

**Acceptance**
- A turn that exhausts its iterations returns the model's summary of what it gathered, not
  a stray preamble.
- The stored transcript is still replayable: every `tool_use` has a matching
  `tool_result`, and the extra request adds no unanswered call of its own.
- `stop_reason` still distinguishes the exhausted turn from a clean `end_turn`, and the
  note tells the person the answer is partial.
- Tests cover the exhausted-with-outstanding-calls path and assert the final request
  carries no tools.

title: [P2] server: Re-map collapses an audiobook position that precedes the first sync point to chapter 0, sentence 0
body:
## Impact
Regenerating a pair's sync map (re-transcription, realign) silently moves every `audiobook`-sourced position whose stored `audio_position_ms` is earlier than the new map's first point to (chapter 0, sentence 0): a listener parked in unaligned front matter, a prologue the aligner dropped, or a book whose new map starts later than the old one. Because the chapter changes, `anchor_revision` is bumped, so every device's hint goes stale at once, and `user_progress` is rewritten to the start of the book. The same code runs for an ordinary client write whose attested `sync_map_version` trails the live map, so a phone save can do it too. The contract (`docs/position-sync-contract.md:81`) says a record holding any anchor must never resolve to start of book.

## What was discovered
- `server/services/sync_engine.py:349-373` `audio_to_epub`: `return 0, 0  # Beginning of ebook as fallback` — indistinguishable from a real match at the first sentence.
- `server/services/sync_engine.py:196-198` `resolve_on_map`: `ch, sentence = audio_to_epub(points_by_audio, audio_position_ms); return (ch, sentence, None)` — no guard for "audio precedes the map".
- `server/services/sync_engine.py:269-296` `remap_bookmarks_for_pair`: treats any non-None result as a hit; writes coordinates, bumps `anchor_revision` on chapter change, `_sync_derived_progress`.
- `server/services/position_service.py:322-345` `_resolve_against_live_map`: identical call; on success stamps the live version with the new (0, 0).
- `server/tests/test_sync_remap.py:199 test_audiobook_bookmark_recomputes_epub_side_from_audio` only covers an audio position inside the map; the fallback is untested. Finder probe: audiobook bookmark ch=3/s=2 at 1000 ms on a map starting at 600000 ms → collapsed to (0, 0).

## Suggested resolution
1. In `resolve_on_map` (server-only; leave `audio_to_epub`'s public signature alone because the `/api/sync/audio-to-epub` router and other callers use it): when `source == AUDIOBOOK and audio_position_ms is not None` and `points_by_audio` is non-empty but `audio_position_ms < points_by_audio[0].audio_start_ms`, do **not** call `audio_to_epub`. Either return `None` immediately, or (preferred) fall through to the text-anchor branch so a bookmark with a usable preview is still re-anchored by text, and return `None` only if that also fails. Both callers already handle `None` correctly: the re-map logs "no usable anchor" and leaves coordinates, `sync_map_version` and `anchor_revision` untouched; the write path keeps the sent coordinates and stamps the attested version.
2. Keep the exact-boundary case (`audio_position_ms == points[0].audio_start_ms`) resolving to the first point.
3. No change to `sync_matcher.py`, `tests/fixtures/sync_parity/` or the Kotlin matcher — confirm by grep before merging that `resolve_on_map` has no Kotlin mirror.

## Tests necessary
- server: `server/tests/test_sync_remap.py`, using `db`, `make_user`, `tests.factories.make_book_pair` / `make_sync_map`: (1) `test_audiobook_bookmark_before_the_first_point_is_left_untouched` — audiobook bookmark at ch=3/s=2 with `audio_position_ms` earlier than every new point keeps chapter/sentence, keeps its old `sync_map_version`, `anchor_revision` unchanged, hints stay current (mirror `test_unmatchable_bookmark_is_left_untouched_and_stays_flagged`) — red today; (2) `test_audiobook_bookmark_exactly_at_the_first_point_resolves_to_it` — boundary; (3) if the fall-through variant is chosen: `test_audiobook_bookmark_before_the_first_point_falls_back_to_its_text_anchor`; (4) in the issue-#116 block: `test_stale_audiobook_write_before_the_map_keeps_its_coordinates_and_attested_version` — version-mismatched audiobook write with audio before the map keeps the sent coordinates and stamps the attested version, not (0,0) at the live version.
- server: `server/tests/test_sync_position_contract.py` — if it enumerates contract invariants, add the "never start of book after re-map" case there as well.

## Found by
bugs pass (bugs-server#5); verified by Fable

---
_Finder id: `bugs-server#5` · verification batch `batch10_server` · verifier notes: Confirmed: `sync_engine.audio_to_epub:349-373` returns `(0, 0)` when no point has `audio_start_ms <= position`, `resolve_on_map:196-198` returns that as a success tuple, `remap_bookmarks_for_pair:286-296` then rewrites chapter/sentence, bumps `anchor_revision` when the chapter changed and re-projects `user_progress`; `position_service._resolve_against_live_map:322` (issue-#116 path) hits the same code and stamps the live version. This violates the "never resolves to start of book" invariant at `docs/position-sync-contract.md:81`. `resolve_on_map` is server-only (the Kotlin side has its own `audioToEpubText` repository call; the parity fixtures cover `match_text`/normalize/restore, not this), so no parity change. Added an alternative: fall through to the text anchor before giving up._

title: Release A: staged service manifests hardcode plane=live and empty settings, so every kind-backed role is rejected by its builder
body:
Found on 82.156.0.68 during the second Release A first-gate run (2026-09-05), after the #198 blockers were cleared. The authority chain published successfully (publish committed in 75 s, sequence 1) and wrapper_preflight is 32/32, but no kind-backed service starts.

**Root cause**: runtime_authority_stage._kind_backed_manifest() writes the same two values into every generated service manifest: "plane": "live" and "settings": {}. The builders disagree:

- seven roles assert a plane other than live (serving or research) and refuse immediately;
- seven roles validate settings against a Pydantic model with required fields and refuse on the empty object;
- strategy_live fails for the separate, by-design reason already recorded (no legacy current under route B).

That is all 15 kind-backed roles. The wrapper's preflight only exercises launch resolution, which is why 32/32 passes while every builder then rejects its manifest.

**Why CI and macOS miss it**: the bootstrap-from-zero probe validates wrapper resolution, not builder construction. No test starts a role's builder from a staged manifest.

**Fix direction**: derive plane and settings per role rather than hardcoding them — the role policy table already distinguishes the planes, and each builder's settings model is the authority for required fields. Acceptance must include starting at least one role of each plane on the production host, not only a wrapper preflight.

**Field discipline learned in the same run**: rquant-runtime-* units carry OnFailure=rquant-alert@, so a failed start pushes a notification to the operator's phone. Two were sent (06:33, 06:35) before the operator switched to bare wrapper runs for evidence. Any future batch start should follow the runbook's scout-first rule.

Impact: Release A's first gate reaches its real criterion (wrapper_preflight == 32) but the service-level criterion (13 running + 1 oneshot) is 0. Production is untouched: resident services NRestarts 0, pages 200, code still on v0.28.3, data/runtime/current absent.
