title: [agents] preexec_fn=pdeathsig raises on Windows — the whole delegation spawn path dies
body:
## 증상

Windows에서 **멀티에이전트 위임 스폰 경로 전체가 죽는다.** `preexec_fn`은 POSIX 전용이고, `subprocess`가 Windows에서 이를 거부한다.

## 사이트 (실측, `6ea4793`)

```
packages/aelix-coding-agent/src/aelix_agents/print_channel.py:970   preexec_fn=pdeathsig,
packages/aelix-coding-agent/src/aelix_agents/rpc_channel.py:438     preexec_fn=pdeathsig,
```

`pdeathsig`는 `aelix_agents/reaper.py:270`에 정의돼 있고, 부모가 죽을 때 커널이 SIGTERM을 보내도록 요청하는 POSIX 기능이다.

## 왜 지금까지 이슈가 없었나

`README.md:231`이 이미 "delegation is unsupported on Windows"라고 적어 두었고, `SLICE-STATUS.md`의 잔여 목록 1번이 이 항목을 **"다른 트랙 소유 — 명시적으로 범위 밖"** 으로 남겨 두었다. 즉 알려져 있었지만 **이슈로는 어디에도 등록된 적이 없다.** #110의 P7 폴리시 목록에도 없다.

## 재현

```bash
grep -rn "preexec_fn" --include=*.py packages/*/src/ | grep -v test
```

## 참고

같은 `aelix_agents/` 트랙에 `reaper.py:208`의 세 번째 raw SIGKILL 사이트가 있고 그쪽은 #105가 추적한다. 프로세스 그룹이 없는 Windows에서 자손이 고아가 되는 더 넓은 부류는 별도 이슈로 등록했다.

측정 근거: `.omc/specs/handoff-windows-roadmap-2026-08-22.md` §3 N-1, `.omc/specs/windows-support-prep-2026-09-03.md`

title: [Bug]: Electrolux dishwasher execute_command results in service error
body:
### What happened?

Environment
​Integration: Electrolux / AEG (Home Assistant)
​Appliance Type: Dishwasher (Model / PNC: DW-911472004 / 911472004_00)
​Home Assistant Version: Latest
​Describe the bug
For this specific dishwasher model, the integration does not expose individual button entities (like button.start), but instead exposes an execute_command switch (switch.keuken_afwasmachine_keuken_execute_command).
​When attempting to trigger this switch or send a start command via Home Assistant (e.g., using switch.turn_on), the action fails and returns the error: “De Electrolux-service is tijdelijk niet beschikbaar. Probeer het opnieuw.” (Electrolux service temporarily unavailable). However, operating and starting the dishwasher directly via the official smartphone app works completely fine without any errors, indicating that cloud connectivity and appliance status are valid.
​It seems the translation from the boolean Home Assistant switch state to the required string command (START) for this legacy/specific schema payload might be failing or rejected by the cloud endpoint.

### Steps to Reproduce (Optional)

To Reproduce
​Ensure the dishwasher is loaded, door is closed, and it is in a ready-to-start state.
​In Home Assistant, toggle switch.keuken_afwasmachine_keuken_execute_command to "On" or call switch.turn_on for this entity.
​Observe the error response from the Electrolux service API call while the official app successfully starts the cycle.

### Expected Behavior (Optional)

Expected behavior
Triggering the execute_command switch should successfully send the START payload to the appliance via the API, matching the behavior of the official mobile app.

### Home Assistant Version (Recommended)

Lastes

### Integration Version (Recommended)

3.7.6

title: Redactor misses prefixed env-style secrets (DB_PASSWORD=, OPENAI_API_KEY=, SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=) and common token prefixes
body:
## Summary

`redact_text` never redacts the most common secret shape in a coding session: an environment-style assignment whose key carries a prefix. `_ASSIGNMENT` and `_AWS_SECRET_ASSIGNMENT` anchor the key name with `\b`, and `_` is a word character, so `DB_PASSWORD=`, `OPENAI_API_KEY=`, `GITHUB_TOKEN=`, `MY_SECRET=` never match. Well-known token prefixes for Slack, Stripe, Google, and npm are not covered either.

## Evidence

```
kept     | 'DB_PASSWORD=hunter2'
kept     | 'export OPENAI_API_KEY=abcdef1234567890abcdef'
kept     | 'SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=xoxb-1234567890-abcdefghij'
kept     | 'MY_SECRET=topsecretvalue'
kept     | 'GITHUB_TOKEN=abc123notaghp'
kept     | 'STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live_abcdefghijklmnop1234'
kept     | 'AIzaSyA1234567890abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv'
kept     | 'npm_abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789'
REDACTED | 'password=hunter2'            -> 'password=[REDACTED]'
REDACTED | 'api_key: abcdef'             -> 'api_key: [REDACTED]'
```

## Where

- `src/iiwi/security/redactor.py:27-30` (`_ASSIGNMENT`), `:23-26` (`_AWS_SECRET_ASSIGNMENT`), `:21` (`_PROVIDER_KEY` only knows `sk-`).

## Impact

The same function guards every outbound path, so an unredacted value reaches:

- the written report (`services/report.py:266-270`),
- the narrative transcript handed to the narration CLI (`summarizers/transcript.py:96,109`), i.e. potentially a hosted model,
- the Quick Review compact index, whose `goal` is the first user message (`services/outcomes.py:124-131`).

README promises "Common secret patterns are removed before reports are written"; `.env` dumps and `export FOO_TOKEN=...` are the common case and slip through.

## Suggested fix

- Replace the leading `\b` with a lookbehind that allows an underscore-joined prefix, e.g. `(?<![A-Za-z0-9])(?:[A-Za-z0-9]+_)*(?:password|passwd|pwd|token|secret|api[_-]?key)(?:_[A-Za-z0-9]+)*` (covers `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`, `DB_PASSWORD`).
- Add known prefixes: `xox[abprs]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10,}` (Slack), `[sr]k_(?:live|test)_[A-Za-z0-9]{16,}` (Stripe), `AIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{35}` (Google), `npm_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}` (npm).
- Add a table-driven test in `tests/unit/security/` with every shape above so a regression is caught.

title: Nexus: новая задача со словом «напомни/дедлайн» внутри уходит уточнением в предыдущую задачу
body:
Гейт 5-мин окна уточнений (`nexus_bot.py` ~645) = `_last_task_get(uid) and _CLARIFY_RE.search(text)`. `_CLARIFY_RE` матчит «напомни» в любом месте строки, поэтому новая задача вида «<заголовок> напомни завтра в 14 дедлайн 13 сентября» распознавалась как уточнение и ставила напоминание на ПРЕДЫДУЩУЮ задачу (ответ «✏️ 🔔 Напоминание: …»), а новая задача не создавалась.

Fix: эвристика `_is_clarification_not_new_task` — у настоящего уточнения перед ключевым словом ≤2 значимых слова.

Связано (не в этом фиксе, pre-existing red): tests/test_reschedule_pending_non_text_inputs.py — voice/photo reply на reschedule-промпт создаёт задачу вместо переноса.

title: fin report 叙事捏造 'market breadth': 合成层改写漂移引入来源不存在的信号 (同文件 References 自相矛盾)
body:
## 现象 (外部全量审查 #1, demo 包不可放行 HIGH)

`financial-intelligence/report.md` **同文件自相矛盾**:Executive Summary (L12)、Key Findings (L16)、Recommendations (L22) 三处称 Joe Tigay 的信号是 "low **market breadth**" / "low **breadth**";但同文件 References (L51/L61) 与本域 digest、cross-domain 全部写 "low VIX, inflation shocks, and excessive AI spending"。

"market breadth" 是**来源中不存在的信号**,属叙事合成层的捏造/改写漂移——把来源的三个具体信号压缩成一个来源没有的抽象词,违背 README 声明的 no-fabrication("只依据来源内容")。

## 根因

- report 合成层有 #179 no-fabrication 全局约束(`output/__init__.py:8819-8824`),但 LLM 在 paraphrase 时把 "low VIX, inflation shocks, excessive AI spending" 改写为 "low market breadth" —— 约束只挡"编造团队/数字/方向",挡不住**对来源信号的改写漂移引入新词**。
- 无任何**叙事↔References 一致性检查**:Exec/KeyFindings/Recommendations 里出现的主题信号,没有断言"必须存在于同条目 References/摘要"。

## 修复方向

1. **合成约束加强**:Exec/KeyFindings/Recommendations 中出现的每个主题信号/关键词,必须能回溯到同条目 References 或摘要;来源没有的词不得以"聚合抽象"形式引入。
2. **确定性门禁断言(推荐,低成本)**:对 report/digest,抽取叙事段的信号词,与 References/摘要做字符串交集一致性检查(breadth 与 VIX/inflation 冲突即 FLAG)。参考审查者建议:加字符串一致性断言。

## 验收标准

- [ ] 重生成 fin report:全文不再出现 "market breadth"(Exec/KeyFindings/Recommendations 与 References 信号一致)
- [ ] 门禁新增叙事↔References 一致性断言,对含 "breadth vs VIX/inflation" 冲突的产物 FLAG
- [ ] 现有测试不回归

## 定性

中等(合成约束 + 门禁断言;含 LLM 行为,需重生成验证)

title: Inbox Favorite writes state nothing reads back: no star in the list, no favorites filter, no count, no sort — api.ts's own comment promises 'a star in the UI', and the Knowledge list implements all four for the same field
body:
Favoriting an inbox item persists, and then nothing shows it. The list has no star, no favorites filter, no count, and no sort. The only thing in the entire frontend that reads `favorited` for an inbox item is the button's own label. `api.ts:925` promises otherwise.

## Measured

Starred one item through the detail panel; it persisted:

```
GET /api/inbox -> favorited items: 4
  proposal_9e973ce7_…  | favorited: True | status: pending
  skills_digest_…      | favorited: True | status: dismissed
  needs_input_ed59b5…  | favorited: True | status: seen
  proposal_c0dc5dc1_…  | favorited: True | status: seen
```

Four items are starred on this instance and no surface distinguishes them from the other 40. One of them is `status: dismissed` — starred and dismissed at once, with nothing to reveal the contradiction.

Every frontend reference to `favorited` for inbox:

```
web/src/lib/api.ts:925-926        // P11: user-favorited (a strong engagement signal + a star in the UI).
web/src/lib/api.ts:2563           favoriteInboxItem(id, favorited)
web/src/pages/inbox/InboxDetail.tsx:44    api.favoriteInboxItem(item.id, !item.favorited)
web/src/pages/inbox/InboxDetail.tsx:200   <Star … className={item.favorited ? … : ''} />
web/src/pages/inbox/InboxDetail.tsx:201   {item.favorited ? 'Favorited' : 'Favorite'}
```

`grep -n favorit web/src/pages/inbox/InboxPage.tsx` returns **nothing**. The star at `:200` is inside the button the user just pressed, in the panel they are already looking at.

The API comment names the missing half:

```
// P11: user-favorited (a strong engagement signal + a star in the UI).
```

The signal exists. The star in the UI does not, unless "the UI" means the button's own label.

## The sibling did all of it

`web/src/pages/knowledge/KnowledgeListPage.tsx` implements every piece for the same field:

```
:342  favorites filter predicate      ? !!it.favorited
:354  favorites: base.filter((i) => !!i.favorited).length      <- a count
:575  context-menu toggle             it.favorited ? 'Remove favorite' : 'Favorite'
:616  list star with an accessible name
        {it.favorited && <Star size={12} … aria-label="Favorite" />}
```

Knowledge is the reference implementation; Inbox shipped the write and skipped the read.

## Honest bound

This is not fully inert. `handlers_inbox.py:539-540` records a `favorite` engagement signal, and `_rank_items` can use it — so the flag does feed ranking when `inbox.engagement_ranking_enabled` is on (it is **false** by default, and false on this instance). What is missing is any way for the user to see or use their own stars. The flag works for the ranker and not for the person who set it.

## Repro (UI-driven)

1. Inbox → open any item → **Favorite**. Label flips to **Favorited**.
2. Close the panel. The row is visually identical to every other row.
3. Open **Filter & sort**. The only section is **Show** (open / handled / classification). No favorites.
4. Reload. The star survives in the panel and is still invisible in the list.

## Suggested shape

Port the four pieces Knowledge already has: a star in the row (with `aria-label`, since #401 and #618 show this list is weak on accessible names), a `favorites` entry in the Show section with a count from `filterCount`, and the context-menu toggle so starring does not require opening the panel. `InboxPage.tsx:269-271` already builds a `menuItems` array with exactly one entry, so the toggle has a home.

## Environment

`origin/main` @ `af659c9`, validation home on `:10000`, 44 inbox items, 4 favorited, `engagement_ranking_enabled: false`.

title: Acceptance: the permission dialog never reaches the engine, and nothing on the hook path records why
body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Rewritten during triage on 2026-09-02. The original body claimed the `Connection lost`
line caused the missing `approval_id`; that claim was checked against the artifacts and
the code and is **disproven**. It is preserved under *Ruled out* below, with its evidence.

## Symptom

Across two real-machine acceptance runs, the engine never received the Session's
permission dialog. The `relay`, `approval`, `companion inbound` and `switches` steps each
ended `neither a verified effect nor an approval … within 360s`.

The engine knew a permission was pending — it just had no handle to answer it with. The
Stop Notice it published says so in its own words (run `20260902T002414Z`, Telegram 4155):

> `Write needs your permission: …/inbound.txt — answer it in the terminal; it cannot be answered from here`

That wording is what the engine emits when the roster row is in the PERMISSION state and
carries no approval handle. So the `PermissionRequest` hook never parked that dialog on
this engine.

Reproduced in `20260902T005521Z` (branch `worktree-187-187`, `53400b6`), same failure,
same wording (Telegram 4162: *"a tool needs your permission — answer it in the terminal"*).

## Why it cannot be diagnosed from the artifacts

**Neither side of the hook boundary records that a `PermissionRequest` hook ran.**

- The hook prints nothing by design — anything on its stdout that is not a verdict is read
  by Claude Code as a *denial*, so the never-deny rule is enforced by printing nothing at
  all — and it writes no log anywhere else.
- The listener logs a *question* when it parks one, but logs nothing when it parks a
  *permission*, nothing when the first line is not something it speaks, and nothing when it
  refuses a session it holds no registration for.

So these four outcomes are indistinguishable in a run's artifacts:

1. the hook never fired;
2. it fired and found no published address, so it exited before opening a socket;
3. it fired, dialed, and reached a different engine;
4. it fired, dialed this engine, and was refused.

Every candidate cause — including #202's — is currently unfalsifiable. **That gap is what
this issue asks to close first.**

## Ruled out

**(a) The `Connection lost` line. Not the cause, and not a failure.**

The original body read `an approval hook connection failed: Connection lost` as the dialog
being dropped 26 s before the relay. The timestamps say otherwise — it lands 1 ms after the
Session's registration, and 31 s *before* the dialog:

```
12:24:19,941  approval address published at …/engine/address.json
12:24:21,063  registration received for session_id=2ad74f3e… pid=43106
12:24:21,064  registered Session inbox agent=claude …
12:24:21,064  an approval hook connection failed: Connection lost
…
12:24:52,006  Session stopped: claude:2ad74f3e…:43106 waiting on permission (Write)   ← no approval line at all
```

Run `20260902T005521Z` shows the same shape: address published 12:55:26, `Connection lost`
12:55:27,230 — again at registration time, not at a dialog.

The cause is in the code and is by design. The `SessionStart` registration client sends one
line, calls `shutdown(SHUT_WR)` and closes the socket without waiting for a reply — its
module docstring states this outright (*"It never waits for an answer"*), because
`SessionStart` runs before the Session is usable and a blocking hook would delay every
Session on the machine. The listener shares one socket between registrations and approvals;
its registration branch then writes a `session_registered` acknowledgement and drains it
into a peer that has already gone. The resulting `ConnectionResetError` is caught by the
connection handler's outer `except` and reported as an **approval hook** failure.

Nothing failed. A registration was delivered and acknowledged into a closed socket, exactly
as designed, and the log called it a broken approval.

**(b) A stale hook binary. Ruled out.**

`~/.claude/settings.json` points both hooks at the installed app
(`/Applications/GPT-VoiceCoding.app/…/engine/bin/python3`), not at the acceptance bundle
under `.claude/worktrees/192-192/shell/.build/`. That looks suspicious but is not the
problem: the `SessionStart` hook from that same path *did* reach the acceptance engine
(the 12:24:21 registration), and `diff` of the installed app's `approval_hook.py` and
`approval.py` against the repo is **empty**. The wire versions match.

**(c) #202 (two engines racing over `address.json`) — does not fit this run.**

In `20260902T002414Z` the codex-lane engine published the address at **12:48:31**, after
the claude lane's entire failure window (12:24:19–12:45). Runs `20260902T005111Z` and
`20260902T005431Z` started at 12:51 or later. Nothing else republished it in between, and
the 12:24:21 registration plus the 12:30:49 `answer_relay` both prove the address was
reachable throughout. #202 remains a real defect and may explain other runs; it does not
explain this one.

## Legacy (ADR 0010)

**Hook-side observability existed in legacy and was dropped.** Every hook invocation wrote
one line naming its outcome — `registered` / `refreshed` / `skipped (<reason>)`, plus a
detail string — into a shared rotated log, best-effort, with a documented guarantee that a
log failure never affects the Session
(`legacy@1d32845:bridge/hook.py:96-109,257-277`). The rewrite **dropped** it; this issue
asks for it **ported**, adapted to the two hooks this generation has.

**The approval transport itself has no legacy counterpart.** Legacy detected a pending
permission and sent the user to the screen rather than carrying a verdict
(`legacy@1d32845:bridge/transcript.py:1633-1713`, `bridge/daemon.py:1901-2052`), so there
is no legacy behaviour for a parked dialog to cite — stated explicitly, as ADR 0010
requires.

## Evidence

- `~/Library/Application Support/GPT-VoiceCoding/acceptance/20260902T002414Z/` —
  `verdict.json`, `journal.jsonl`, `engine-claude/engine.log`, `engine-codex/engine.log`
- `~/Library/Application Support/GPT-VoiceCoding/acceptance/20260902T005521Z/` — second run
- Bundle `f2affaa`; claude 2.1.258; codex 0.152.1

## Related

- #191 rewrites the approval path on the same hook and is `ready-for-agent`. Read it first
  so the fix lands once. It retires `AwaitingApproval`, the budget, the sweep and the
  approval pipeline — but it does **not** touch the registration branch or the connection
  handler this issue changes, so the two do not collide.
- #202 — `address.json` is per-machine and last-writer-wins. Ruled out for these runs
  (above); still the first thing to re-check once the hook path leaves a trace.
- Observed in the same run and filed separately in spirit: an acceptance run and the agent
  crew share one roster and one hook installation, so the roster listed the crew's own
  Claude sessions (pids 72243, 76296, 77695, 79271) beside the acceptance Session.

## Routing

Workflow: tdd
Executor: claude
Model: claude-opus-5
Effort: medium
Review: codex gpt-5.6-sol high
Reasons: tdd because listener and hook tracing are new testable behaviour; non-core-complex because it crosses the hook and listener modules without changing a shared contract.

title: SolidSource-backed FootageItem.name does not persist after save
body:
## Environment

- py-aep 0.15.0 and current `main`
- Python 3.14
- target AEP version `26.3x87`

## Problem

Assigning `FootageItem.name` works in memory for a `SolidSource`, but the name is restored from
the Solid source after save and reparse. File-backed footage names persist normally.

## Minimal reproduction

```python
from pathlib import Path
import py_aep

output = Path("solid-rename.aep")
app = py_aep.new(version="26.3x87")
comp = app.project.root_folder.add_comp("Main", 200, 200, 1.0, 1.0, 25.0)
layer = comp.add_solid([1.0, 0.0, 0.0], "Original Solid", 40, 40, 1.0, 1.0)
footage = layer.source

footage.name = "Renamed Solid Item"
assert footage.name == "Renamed Solid Item"
app.project.save(output)

checked = py_aep.parse(output).project
solid = next(item for item in checked.footages if item.id == footage.id)
assert solid.name == "Renamed Solid Item"  # fails: "Original Solid"
```

## Expected behavior

Either `FootageItem.name` should persist for Solid-backed footage like other project items, or
the assignment should be rejected with an actionable error. Silently accepting a value that is
lost on save makes project-panel cleanup difficult to validate.

The binary appears to carry both an item display name and a Solid source name. It would be useful
to confirm whether the setter should synchronize both fields or whether Solid footage needs a
dedicated rename path.

title: Inspector Playwright specs fail on the first day of a month
body:
## Problem

Eleven inspector Playwright specs fail on the first day of a calendar month, on `main`, with no code change involved. `frontend-tests` went from green on 2026-08-31 to red on 2026-09-01; `backend-tests` is unaffected.

This blocks every PR opened on the 1st, and re-running the job does not help — it will keep failing until the clock moves far enough into the month, and it will recur on the 1st of every month.

## Reproduction

On a clean checkout of `main` (verified at `094e4c5`), on 2026-09-01:

```
npx playwright test tests/inspector-pill-chart-link.spec.ts -g "hovering a column lights its pill"
```

```
Error: expect(received).toContain(expected)
Expected value: "2026-09-16"
Received array: []
  at frontend/tests/inspector-pill-chart-link.spec.ts:89
```

## Cause

`mountInspector` builds its fixtures from the real system clock — `const today = new Date()` at `frontend/tests/support/inspector-aggregate-harness.ts:59`. Nothing in the harness fakes or injects a clock, so the fixture's shape depends on which calendar day CI happens to run.

The failing assertions take the **middle** column of the month being shown and require a day pill for it:

```ts
const index = Math.floor(keys.length / 2);
const wanted = keys[index];
expect(await dayPillDates(page)).toContain(wanted);
```

The aggregate chart draws a column for every day of the month, so on 2026-09-01 the middle column is 2026-09-16 — a date two weeks in the future. `dayPillDates` (`inspector-aggregate-harness.ts:330`) comes back empty. The specs implicitly assume a "today" far enough into the month that its midpoint is a day with history behind it, and the 1st is exactly where that assumption breaks.

Worth settling as part of the fix: whether the empty pill row on the 1st is *only* a bad test assumption, or whether the inspector itself should draw pills for a month whose days are mostly still in the future. The chart and the pill row disagree about the month's extent, and that disagreement is what the tests trip over.

## The eleven

From run [33495969606](https://github.com/Scarfsail/hass-helman/actions/runs/33495969606/job/99818126942) (11 failed, 4 skipped, 516 passed):

| Spec | Test |
|---|---|
| `inspector-aggregate-views.spec.ts:336` | a minutes stop opens the day picked at D |
| `inspector-aggregate-views.spec.ts:1100` | double-clicking a day column at D opens the day at the width last used |
| `inspector-aggregate-views.spec.ts:1173` | double-clicking a day pill at D opens the day |
| `inspector-pill-chart-link.spec.ts:81` | hovering a column lights its pill |
| `inspector-pill-chart-link.spec.ts:95` | hovering a pill lights its column |
| `inspector-pill-chart-link.spec.ts:108` | leaving a pill clears both |
| `inspector-pill-chart-link.spec.ts:168` | the browsed day and the selected column can be one pill |
| `inspector-pill-chart-link.spec.ts:651` | the day being read at 15/30/60 arrives at D already picked |
| `inspector-span-pills.spec.ts:339` | clicking the lit month pill keeps the day the reader came from |
| `inspector-span-pills.spec.ts:514` | a day pill picks the column, and a minutes stop opens it at the width last used |
| `render-discipline.spec.ts:236` | a re-render for an unrelated reason does not hand the pills a new historyDays |

`inspector-pill-chart-link.spec.ts:81` is the one reproduced against `main` locally and confirmed to be independent of any branch. The other ten are attributed by shape: every one is an inspector spec that goes through the same month-view/day-pill path, and all ten went red in the same run that `main` had been passing the night before. `render-discipline.spec.ts:236` presents differently — a 30s timeout on `page.waitForFunction(() => window.__pendingInspector() === 1)` at line 252 rather than an assertion — so confirm it shares this root cause rather than assuming it.

## Suggested direction

Give the harness a fixed, injected clock instead of `new Date()`, so the suite stops depending on the day CI runs. That is the durable fix, but it touches the shared harness and the date assumptions in several specs, so it wants doing deliberately rather than by pinning one test.

## Not caused by #198

Noticed there, and ruled out: the failure reproduces on `main` at `094e4c5` with an otherwise clean tree, and #198's only frontend change is a renamed constant's value in `frontend/cards/helman/power-device-info.ts`, which the inspector does not import.

## Notes
- `frontend/tests/support/inspector-aggregate-harness.ts:59` — `const today = new Date()`, the clock the fixtures are built from
- `frontend/tests/support/inspector-aggregate-harness.ts:330` — `dayPillDates`, which returns `[]` here
- `frontend/tests/inspector-pill-chart-link.spec.ts:84-89` — the midpoint-of-the-month assumption
- `frontend/cards/helman-solar-inspector/helman-solar-inspector.ts:1607` — `_dayPillsVisible`, which gates the row

title: Final report is half Turkish, half English — agent prose and gate codes are never translated
body:
### What happened

With the website language set to Turkish, the final report comes out mixed: the headings and standard sentences are Turkish, while large parts of the body are English. It should be fully Turkish.

### Why

The report is a Markdown document rendered once, inside the pipeline, and frozen into an artifact (`src/ads/pipeline/stages.py:646`):

```
markdown = render_markdown(evaluation).rstrip()
state.blackboard[FINAL_MARKDOWN_KEY] = markdown
```

Two separate problems fall out of that.

**1. Some content is never translated, only interpolated.** `render_markdown` (`src/ads/reporting/markdown.py:131`) wraps its own sentences in `_t(...)`, but drops several values in raw:

- `report.problem_description` (`markdown.py:156`) and `report.problem_title` (`:133`) — agent-authored prose, written in English (the planner is instructed "Use English for reply", `src/ads/api/service.py:2697`).
- `decision.verdict.value` and `decision.reason_code` in the decisions table (`markdown.py:122`-`:124`) — raw enum codes.
- `report.primary_metric.value` (`markdown.py:33`).

The frontend already translates exactly those codes — `verdictLabel` and `reasonLabel` in `web/src/lib/status.ts` — so the same gate verdict reads Turkish in the UI and English in the report.

**2. The report does not follow the website language at all.** The active language is a per-request `ContextVar` bound by the HTTP middleware (`src/ads/api/i18n.py:27`, `src/ads/api/service.py:6157`). `render_markdown` runs in the run's **background worker**, outside any request, so that ContextVar is never set and `_t` falls back to `DEFAULT = "tr"` (`i18n.py:26`).

The Turkish half is therefore an accident of the default, not a response to the language selection. The consequences both ways:

- An English UI still gets a Turkish report skeleton.
- Switching language after the run cannot change the report, because the text was frozen into the artifact at render time.

### What should happen

- Carry the run's language into the worker explicitly — capture it when the run is started and wrap the reporting stage in `i18n.using(...)` — so the report is rendered in the language that was actually chosen, instead of the ContextVar default.
- Better still, store the report in a form that can be rendered per reader (the structured `EvaluationReport` is already the artifact; the Markdown is a projection of it), so one run does not permanently commit to one language.
- Translate the values currently interpolated raw: verdict and reason codes should go through the same mapping the UI uses, not appear as enum text.
- Agent-authored prose (`problem_title`, `problem_description`, findings) needs the bilingual treatment the rest of the system already uses — `*_en` / `*_tr` pairs, as the planner artifacts do — rather than being emitted in English and dropped into a Turkish document.
- Identifiers that must stay untranslated — column names, metric ids, model class names, artifact ids — should stay exactly as they are; this is about prose and codes, not identifiers.

### Where in the product

Final report artifact (`src/ads/reporting/markdown.py`, rendered from `src/ads/pipeline/stages.py:640`).

Reported directly by the supervisor: "the final report is half turkish and half english if the website language is turkish, it should be fully turkish in this case."

title: [code-review] 一括発行違反 50% のうち 2 件が偽陽性 — waves_expected に式の版が無く旧式の値が残る / skeptic 控除が反証 wave の後ろで効かない
body:
## 対象プラグイン
code-review

## 説明

#192 で分母・呼称・是正先が直り、一括発行違反が **判定できた 16 件中 8 件（50%）** としてシグナルに出るようになった。この 8 件を payload から 1 件ずつ検算したところ、**2 件が偽陽性**だった。

母集団: このマシンの 10 本の `.claude/events.jsonl` を合算した `review:completed` **n=108**（2026-09-01 時点。`dispatch.waves` と `waves_expected` が揃い `agents-mismatch` で抑止されていない回が 16 件）。

| ts | `wave_sizes` | waves | payload の exp | 現行式で再計算 | 判定 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 08-24T02:34 | `[6,10,4,1]` | 4 | 3 | **4** | **旧式の偽陽性** |
| 08-28T00:28 | `[2,5,1,1]` | 4 | 3 | 3 | **skeptic 控除の取り逃し** |
| 他 6 件 | — | — | — | 一致 | 本物 |

### 1. `waves_expected` に式の版が無く、旧式の値が集計に残り続ける

08-24T02:34 は **#166 の meta 項（v2.87.1）が入る前に publish された回**で、現行式で再計算すると期待 4 本 ＝ 実 4 本で違反にならない。#172 の起票時に「偽陽性（meta 項追加前の版 ＝ #166 で解決済み）」と判定された回そのものが、**式が直った後も payload の旧値のまま違反として数え続けられている**。

`waves_expected` は publish 時点の式で固定されるが、**式の版マーカーが無い**。`dispatch.schema` は `measure-tokens.sh` が持つ版で、publish 側の式変更では上げない契約（コメントに「上げると出所が 2 つに割れる」と明記）。結果として、この計測フィールドだけが「版マーカーで層別する」原則の外にある。

再計算に必要な値（`agents` / `meta_reviewer.fired` と `findings_added` / `recall_skeptic.fired` / `wave_sizes`）は**すべて payload にある**ので、集計側で現行式に揃えられる。

### 2. #172 の「既知の残存限界②」の初実サンプルが出た

08-28T00:28 は `wave_sizes` の合計 9 が申告体数と一致する（explorer 2 + reviewer 5 + verify 1 ＝ 8、+ skeptic 1 ＝ 9）。並びは `[explorer 2][reviewer 5][1][1]` で、末尾 2 本はそれぞれ skeptic wave と反証 wave。**どちらも構造的に別 wave が要る**（skeptic は reviewer 完了後、反証は指摘確定後）。

skeptic 控除の条件は「`wave_sizes` の末尾が 1 かつ末尾以外に 1 が無い」なので、**後ろに反証 wave が 1 本付いた瞬間に効かなくなる**。これは #172 が既知の限界として予告していた形そのもの:

> ②fallback が走っても後ろに meta / 反証 wave が付く回では fallback wave は末尾に来ない。どちらも位置ヒューリスティックでは分離できず、構造的な解は `recall_skeptic` に起動経路を自己申告させること。

6 サンプルへの後付けという留保つきで導入されたが、母集団が 17 件になって実サンプルが出た形。

### 3. 結論は変わらないが、根拠の数字が違う

本物は **6/16 ＝ 38%**（報告値は 50%）。⚠️ シグナルの閾値 20% は依然超えるので**「一括発行が守られていない」という結論は変わらない**。ただし #192 で分母を直した直後で、この数字が打ち手の見積もりに使われる位置にある。

本物 6 件の内訳（`wave_sizes` と申告体数の突合による）:

- **explorer を 1 体ずつ発行**: 2 件（`[1,1,6,1]` / `[1,2,1,2,1]`）
- **reviewer wave の分割**: 4 件（`[2,2,4]` / `[2,3]` ×2 / `[2,5,1,1]` のうち reviewer 側）

## 期待する動作

1. **retro が判定に使う `waves_expected` を現行式で再計算する**（payload の値は残したまま、判定だけ揃える）。または式に版を持たせて層別する。**旧式のまま数え続けると、式を直すたびに過去の偽陽性が固定化する**
2. **skeptic 控除の取り逃しを埋める**。「末尾から連続する単独 wave のうち 1 本」に緩めるのが最小の変更だが、`[1,1,6,1]`（先頭の explorer 分割 ＝ 本物）を落とさないことが要件。#172 が示した構造的解（`recall_skeptic` に起動経路 — fallback 単独か reviewer 相乗りか — を自己申告させる）に進むなら、位置ヒューリスティック自体を捨てられる
3. **本物 6 件の内訳を是正の入口にする**。検知は #172 / #192 で整ったが、**違反そのものを減らす打ち手はどの issue も持っていない**。上の内訳は 2 型に割れており、explorer の 1 体ずつ発行と reviewer wave の分割では手当てする Step が違う

## 補足

- 再現: `bash code-review/scripts/review-retro.sh --logs <10 本の events.jsonl>` で違反 8 件を出し、各回の payload から `waves_expected` を現行式で再計算して突合する
- **「本物 6 件」は `wave_sizes` と申告体数の突合による推定**で、層の割り当てそのものは payload に無い（`publish-review-event.sh` の「層の同定はしない」という判断は維持されている）。断定できるのは 08-24T02:34（式の版で説明が付く）と 08-28T00:28（体数が一致し末尾 2 本の役割が構造から決まる）の 2 件
- 関連: #192（分母・呼称・是正先の修正）/ #172（WARN 化と skeptic 控除の導入 / 限界②の予告）/ #166（meta 項の追加）/ #154（`waves_effective` による再試行の除去）

title: Resuming into a fresh run directory crashes seeding the rolling window
body:
## The defect

`_RollingSaveMixin.on_train_start` seeds the rolling window from disk when a run resumes. Its
guard checks that `dirpath` is *set*, never that it **exists**:

```python
if self.monitor is not None or not trainer.ckpt_path or not self.dirpath:
    return
found = sorted(
    (int(match.group(1)), str(path))
    for path in Path(self.dirpath).iterdir()
    ...
```

Lightning creates a checkpoint directory lazily, inside its IO plugin, at the first save. So on a
resume into a run directory that has not saved yet, `iterdir()` raises:

```
File "sisr/training/callbacks.py", line 730, in on_train_start
    for path in Path(self.dirpath).iterdir()
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../checkpoints'
```

## When it fires

`fit --ckpt_path <ckpt>` where the *destination* run directory is new — i.e. resuming a run under
a different `version:` than the checkpoint came from. That is a legitimate and useful thing to do:
branching a run, or restarting a crashed run into a clean directory so the old one stays intact as
evidence.

Resuming in place is unaffected, because the directory already holds the checkpoint being resumed
from. That is why it has not been hit before.

## Severity

Crashes at `on_train_start`, so it fails fast and corrupts nothing — but it fails *after* model
construction, dataloader setup and the sanity-check pass, which on an adversarial config with
perceptual metrics is tens of minutes of work thrown away.

## Fix

Treat a missing directory the same as an empty one — there is nothing on disk to adopt, which is
exactly the state the seeding code would infer anyway:

```python
if self.monitor is not None or not trainer.ckpt_path or not self.dirpath:
    return
directory = Path(self.dirpath)
if not directory.is_dir():
    return
```

Same shape as the `artifacts.py` directory-creation fix: Lightning owns creating that directory,
and code outside its IO plugin cannot assume it has run yet.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Resuming into a fresh run directory reaches the first training step
- [ ] A test proves it, RED against current `main`
- [ ] Resuming in place still seeds the window from the files already there (the existing
      behaviour must not regress — there is already coverage for it)

title: hunting FaultSource selection is not wired into the production path - an empty POST /hunting is a vacuous pass
body:
## Overview

The hunting pipeline cannot run its own candidate selection: `FaultSource.select` (`attack/hunting/fault_source.py:256` - the deterministic typed applies-if predicate + the phase-1 enum-of-system-kinds tag + the LLM match) has **ZERO call sites** in the production hunting path. `POST /projects/{id}/hunting` with an omitted/empty `candidates` body runs `arun_orchestration` with an empty intake, which returns the vacuous "Empty pass (O1)" report - nothing is reasoned over. The candidate set MUST be supplied externally (the caller plays the FaultSource role). This forced the eval harness to fabricate candidates (placeholder witnesses, hardcoded "applies" verdicts) and bypass the selection entirely - which is why `enum_kinds`-requiring faults reached the gate despite zero linked systems (see #199/#197 for the downstream effects).

## Evidence

- `grep -rn "fault_source\|FaultSource\|\.select(" src/polymerhus/attack/hunting/*.py` -> only the module itself + the orchestrator docstring "Consumes the FaultSource candidate set (IA-1, spec 4.1)". No call site.
- `hunt_orchestrator.py` `arun_orchestration` (line ~915): `intake = normalize_candidates(candidates, known_faults)` then `if not intake.accepted: return OrchestratorReport(...)` - the empty pass (O1) with `pairs_processed=0`.
- `runtime.py` `start_hunting` passes `candidates or ()` straight into `arun_orchestration`.
- Observed: a launch with an empty batch produces a vacuous pass; the harness's fabricated batch (the eval driver) produced 75 `enum_kinds` candidates with `"verdict": "applies"` + placeholder witnesses, which `normalize_candidates` accepts (only prunes `does-not-apply` verdicts / no-llm-witness candidates).

## Expected

The platform should run its own selection when no candidates are supplied: `start_hunting`/`arun_orchestration` with an empty candidate set should invoke `FaultSource.select` over the live L1 (predicate + enum tag + LLM match), so an empty launch is a meaningful pass - and the deterministic stage prunes `enum_kinds` faults for units with no linked systems (the correct behaviour on an unenriched/unlinked L1). The candidates-rewrite spec 4.1 ("consumes the FaultSource candidate set") should state explicitly whether FaultSource is an internal stage or a caller contract.

## Found during

Eval-harness hunting stretch assessment, white-jotter (2026-08-28). The harness driver was retired because it could only fabricate candidates; this ticket is the prerequisite for an API-only, self-contained launch.

title: An interrupted turn is lost when the gateway exits
body:
Upstream HKUDS/nanobot `2cdfba38` keeps a turn that was interrupted by a gateway shutdown, so a restart resumes it rather than losing it; `c7e2a474` fixes where the recovered turn is routed, and `12029f88` puts the resume behind a user decision instead of doing it silently.

Ours diverged in both files the fix touches (`nanoinfra/agent/loop.py` shutdown, `nanoinfra/gateway/runtime.py`), so this needs a real read rather than a cherry-pick. The property is worth having on its own: a `docker compose up -d` costs about 15 seconds of downtime, and any turn in flight at that moment is currently gone with no record that it existed.

Two things to decide while porting, because upstream decided them after the first attempt:

- **Who resumes.** Silent resumption replays work the operator may no longer want; `12029f88` makes it a choice. With our gate that matters more, not less — a resumed turn re-enters the same approval path, and an approval answered before the restart is not answered after it.
- **Where it resumes.** `c7e2a474` exists because the recovered turn was routed to the wrong session.

Triage: `proposals/upstream-sync-triage.md`, second pass.

title: [OMEGA-220] Bug 7: Agent Generates False Bug Reports in Unsupervised Mode
body:
Describe the bug:
When left unsupervised (no user messages for several hours), the agent continues a "bug hunt" task but generates false positive bug reports. After correctly finding 2 real bugs in helper.py during a supervised session, the agent spent the night in autonomous mode and reported 3 additional bugs — all of which were false positives. The functions it claimed were "undefined" actually exist in the codebase.

To Reproduce:

Start a productive supervised session where agent finds real bugs

Send: "Nice now go and seek for more bugs"

Do not send any further messages for several hours

Review agent's autonomous bug reports upon return

Expected behavior:
Agent either finds real verifiable bugs, or reports that no additional bugs were found.

Actual behavior:
Agent sent 16+ messages overnight, eventually reporting 3 new bugs:

"memory.metta uses undefined swrite and read_file_tail"

Reality: swrite is defined via !(import_prolog_function swrite) in utils.metta

Reality: read_file_tail is imported in skills.metta via !(import_prolog_functions_from_file ... read_file_tail)

Agent claimed "grep confirmed these don't exist in codebase" — grep shows they do exist

"helper.py calls undefined normalize_string"

Reality: def normalize_string(x): is defined at line 200 of helper.py

Verified via server:

bash
grep -r "swrite\|read_file_tail" /PeTTa/repos/OmegaClaw-Core/src/
# swrite: defined in utils.metta
# read_file_tail: imported in skills.metta, used in memory.metta

grep -rn "def normalize_string\|normalize_string" /PeTTa/repos/OmegaClaw-Core/src/
# def normalize_string(x): at helper.py line 200
Pattern:

Supervised mode (with user feedback): 2 real bugs found in helper.py

Unsupervised mode (no user feedback): 3 false positives generated

Agent fabricates verification claims: "grep confirmed these don't exist"

Additional context:

OmegaClaw version: singularitynet/omegaclaw:main (build b7c00077)

Communication channel: Telegram

Model provider: ASICloud (minimax/minimax-m2.5)

title: fix(dev): stop shipping maintained Cloud SQL identifiers in the helper
body:
## Context

Parent epic: #151
Discovered while implementing #171, which removed the same two identifiers from the public Terraform module.

`scripts/cloud_postgres.py` is shipped by this public template, is retained in a generated project whenever the reader keeps the Cloud SQL helper, and hardcodes the maintainer's infrastructure:

```python
DEFAULT_PROJECT = "pisces-476117"
DEFAULT_INSTANCE = "sci-rag-dev"
```

Its module docstring repeats both, and `docs/run-postgres.md` documents `sci-rag-dev` as the value of `SCI_RAG_CLOUD_PG_INSTANCE`.

## Why it is separate from #171

#171 was a deletion: the Terraform variables had defaults, and removing them makes Terraform refuse before it can plan. This one is not a deletion. The helper needs somewhere else to read its configuration from, because this repository's own `.conductor/setup-cloud-workspace.sh` calls `cloud_postgres.py config` before any workspace `.env` exists, so the values cannot simply move into `.env` without a chicken and egg problem.

## Why it matters

`cloud_postgres.py` has `pause` and `resume` verbs, and ADR 0009 says plainly that they "affect every workspace using the shared instance". A downstream reader running `python scripts/cloud_postgres.py pause` with the shipped defaults is aiming a lifecycle change at the maintainer's instance. Their credentials will refuse, so the blast radius is smaller than the Terraform case, but a public template should not name somebody else's infrastructure as the thing its verbs act on.

It is also inconsistent after #171: the module that creates the instance now refuses to guess, while the helper that pauses it still guesses.

## Evidence

```console
$ git ls-files | xargs grep -ln "pisces-476117\|sci-rag-dev"
docs/adr/0009-cloud-dev-database.md      (addressed by #171)
docs/run-postgres.md
scripts/cloud_postgres.py
tests/unit/test_cloud_postgres_script.py
tests/unit/test_dev_database_terraform.py  (addressed by #171)
```

`tests/unit/test_cloud_postgres_script.py` asserts the defaults are present in four places, the same shape of guard #171 had to invert.

## Fix direction

Give the helper a configuration source that is not source code, and make an unconfigured helper say what to set rather than guessing. Options worth weighing during implementation: a git-ignored `.cloudsql/config.json` written by `terraform output -raw sci_rag_cloud_pg_config`, reading the same environment variables the Terraform output already emits, or a tracked example file the reader copies. Whatever the mechanism, `setup-cloud-workspace.sh` and every parallel Conductor workspace must keep working without a manual step per workspace.

## Acceptance criteria

- No tracked file names a maintained Google Cloud project or Cloud SQL instance, extending the check #171 added for Terraform to the whole repository.

title: pack init promises no patient data is kept, and writes patient data into the pack
body:
Found by functional verification of the packaging path. **Reproduced.** Raising this above the other `pack init` findings because it touches the PHI promise.

## What was measured

`src/anastomosis/packgen/infer.py:62` sets `_STATIC_FRACTION = 0.6`, and `:223-225` promotes any text recurring in `ceil(0.6 × N)` samples to "static template chrome". `README.md:234` describes the same step as *"recurring across **ALL** samples → static-text intersection"*.

Ran `anast pack init --from-samples <3 charts, 3 DIFFERENT patients> --name probe_pack`. Values printed to the terminal **and** written verbatim into `template.html` and `DRAFT.md`:

- a charted diagnosis display string
- a patient ethnicity value
- a rendering provider's full name
- a facility street line, and city/state/ZIP
- a phone number

Two of those — the diagnosis and the ethnicity — appear in only **2 of the 3** sample charts; the third contains zero occurrences of either. They are per-patient clinical data promoted to template chrome by the 60% rule.

The command's own confirmation prompt asks whether the samples are from different patients, and the header says "Analysis (PHI-safe — no values shown)". These samples *were* from different patients, and values were shown. `infer.py:596-603` correctly suppresses text for a 1-sample run; there is no equivalent guard for a value that is merely common.

Reproduce: `anast pack init --from-samples '<dir>/*.pdf' --name p --out-dir /tmp/p -y`, then grep the sample charts for each string listed under `static labels` in `/tmp/p/p/DRAFT.md`.

## Why 60% cannot be safe on its own

With 3 samples the threshold is 2, so any value shared by two patients — a common diagnosis, an ethnicity, a referring provider, a clinic address — is indistinguishable from a printed form label. The count of samples is doing work that only content can do.

## What to do

1. **Make the threshold and the documentation agree.** Either raise the rule to a true intersection, or change `README.md:234`. They should not describe different algorithms.
2. **A fraction is not a safety property.** Text that lands in a pack should have to look like chrome, not merely be common: appearing at a stable page position across samples, matching a label shape, being absent from the extracted clinical fields the same run already parsed. The run already knows which spans it mapped to patient fields — those should never be eligible for the static set, whatever their frequency.
3. **Say what the checkpoint actually covers.** The prompt asks about different patients, which implies the different-patient case is handled. Until (2) lands, the summary should say plainly that common values can be promoted, so the confirmation is an informed one.

## Related, from the same pass — the learned pack renders none of what it learned

Not a PHI matter, but it is the other half of the picture for this command.

`src/anastomosis/packgen/emit.py:298` dumps all learned static text into an HTML comment (`<!-- UNPLACED STATIC TEXT — position manually`, emitted at `template.html:36`). Rendering with the draft pack:

```
all 6 charts: text identical to generic_soap: True
```

Samples were 6-page charts, ~5.2–6.4k chars, 159–186 blocks, 34 section headings. Draft output: 1 page, 376–893 chars, 4–22 blocks. `DRAFT.md` reports **112 heading sections** cleared the confidence gate; **0** reach the page. The "recovers roughly 60-70% of a pack" line (`emit.py:693`, repeated in `DRAFT.md`) is not supported by what the pack produces — the recovered material is inert commentary. `DRAFT.md` does say fidelity is not claimed, so this is a claim-vs-output mismatch rather than a false promise, but the percentage should describe something the operator gets.

title: Env-driven roots make a silently-missing source reachable in the audit chain
body:
Round-1 review of PR #199.

Replacing the hardcoded absolute paths with `MEDIAINGREDIENTMECH_ROOT` / `KGMICROBE_ROOT` is what makes the chain runnable anywhere. It is also what makes a *wrong* root reachable for the first time: with a literal path, the file was either present or the script was obviously on the wrong machine.

Two things that only matter once the path can vary:

**1. `load_mediadive_unmapped` returned `[]` in silence.** A kg-microbe checkout that has the unified dictionary but not `mappings/mediadive_unmapped_ingredients_to_curate.tsv` produces a complete-looking audit whose unmapped-candidate count is short by a whole source, with nothing said. Measured against a checkout with only the dictionary: **190** candidates instead of **391**. The main dictionary is fine — `load_kgm_dict` already raises `SystemExit` with the regeneration command, verified by pointing `KGMICROBE_ROOT` at `/tmp`.

**2. A comment in the PR claimed a refusal that does not exist.** It credited `load_kgm_entity_index` with refusing a missing artifact. That function returns `{}`; the refusal lives in each caller's own `.exists()` check. A comment asserting a safety property the code does not have is worse than no comment — it sends the next reader looking in the wrong place.

**Fix (in #199)**: the absent MediaDive source prints a warning naming the path, what the count now covers, and `KGMICROBE_ROOT` as the knob; the comment is corrected to say where the refusal actually is. `tests/test_xref_chain_sources.py` pins both, plus the #147/#176 contract that importing any of the four chain modules requires no checkout.

title: Async decorator typing regression in 2.4.0 with mypy disallow_any_decorated
body:
## Summary

After migrating from `backoff==2.2.1` to `python-backoff==2.4.0`, applying `@backoff.on_exception` to an annotated async function fails with mypy when `disallow_any_decorated = true`.

Runtime behavior is unaffected. This is a static typing regression introduced by the decorator annotation changes in #182.

## Reproduction

`example.py`:

```python
import backoff


@backoff.on_exception(backoff.expo, ValueError)
async def fetch() -> str:
    return "ok"
```

`pyproject.toml`:

```toml
[tool.mypy]
strict = true
disallow_any_decorated = true
```

Run:

```console
mypy example.py
```

Result with `python-backoff==2.4.0` and mypy 2.3.0:

```text
example.py:5: error: Type of decorated function contains type "Any"
("Callable[[], Coroutine[Any, Any, str]]")  [misc]
```

The same example passes with `backoff==2.2.1`.

## Cause

Version 2.2.1 typed the decorator as an identity transformation over the complete callable type:

```python
_CallableT = TypeVar("_CallableT", bound=Callable[..., Any])

def on_exception(...) -> Callable[[_CallableT], _CallableT]:
    ...
```

Version 2.4.0 reconstructs the callable using `ParamSpec` and a return `TypeVar`:

```python
def on_exception(
    ...
) -> Callable[[Callable[P, T]], Callable[P, T]]:
    ...
```

Mypy represents an async function as `Callable[P, Coroutine[Any, Any, T]]`. After the new decorator transformation, `disallow_any_decorated` reports the two `Any` parameters of `Coroutine`.

This behavior is related to python/mypy#17171. However, the change in #182 makes `python-backoff` trigger the diagnostic where 2.2.1 did not.

There is also a separate problem in the internal async annotations. Both `_async.retry_exception` and `_async.retry_predicate` accept:

```python
target: Callable[P, T]
```

but then await the result:

```python
ret = await target(*args, **kwargs)
```

An arbitrary `T` is not awaitable. The returned async wrapper is also annotated as `Callable[P, T]`, although an `async def retry(...) -> T` returns a coroutine. These mismatches are currently hidden with `type: ignore`.

## Expected behavior

Decorating an annotated async function should:

- pass mypy with `disallow_any_decorated = true`;
- preserve its parameter and awaited result types;
- remain usable with APIs expecting a coroutine, such as `asyncio.create_task`;
- require no adapter or `type: ignore` in consumer code.

## Proposed approach

Keep the `ParamSpec`-based typing introduced in #182 inside the sync and async implementations, but expose the public decorator as an identity transformation over the complete callable type:

```python
_CallableT = TypeVar("_CallableT", bound=Callable[..., Any])


def on_exception(...) -> Callable[[_CallableT], _CallableT]:
    ...
```

The decorator preserves the callable's public contract, so retaining the complete callable type avoids reconstructing an async function as `Callable[P, Coroutine[Any, Any, T]]`.

This identity form is the exact public typing contract of 2.2.1, so consumer code that type-checked against 2.2.1 — including strict configurations with `disallow_any_decorated` — type-checks unchanged. It also gives up nothing that #182 delivered to consumers: an identity transformation preserves the complete callable type, so parameter and return checking at call sites stays at least as precise as with the reconstructed `Callable[P, T]` form, while the `ParamSpec` typing keeps doing its checking work inside the implementations. #182 states no rationale for reconstructing the public type, so no known requirement depends on that form.

Fixing this in the library also does not need to wait for python/mypy#17171: the identity annotation is accurate regardless of how mypy represents async callables, and consumers should not have to disable a strict flag that worked with 2.2.1.

An overloaded public protocol is not suitable here. Its async overload overlaps with the generic sync overload when a function has an unknown or unannotated return type. Pyrefly may therefore classify an unannotated sync function as async.

The internal implementations should retain `ParamSpec` and use separate sync and async contracts. The async implementation should accept a callable returning an awaitable or coroutine and declare that its wrapper returns a coroutine. The sync implementation should continue to use `Callable[P, T]`.

The same separation should be applied to `on_predicate`, `_async.retry_predicate`, and their sync counterparts.

Regression tests should type-check consumer code against the built package and cover:

- an annotated async function with mypy and `disallow_any_decorated = true`;
- preservation of the async function's parameter and result types;
- passing the decorated async call to `asyncio.create_task`;
- an unannotated sync function with pyrefly, ensuring it remains classified as sync.

## Environment

- Python 3.14
- mypy 2.3.0
- python-backoff 2.4.0

title: No SQLITE_BUSY handling: no busy_timeout, and write transactions BEGIN deferred
body:
Found during a full code review of the SQLite store.

## Problem

A repo-wide grep for `busy_timeout|busy_handler|SQLITE_BUSY` returns nothing, and `Transaction` (`src/cpp/store/sqlite_raii.hpp:154`) issues a plain `BEGIN;` rather than `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`.

Consequences when a second connection/process touches the DB (two builds racing, a stray sqlite3 shell, a future parallel consumer):

- any statement can fail instantly with "database is locked" (thrown from `step()`/`exec`) instead of waiting;
- a deferred write transaction can hit `SQLITE_BUSY` mid-transaction at its first write, after work has been done.

## Suggested fix

- Set `sqlite3_busy_timeout` (a few seconds) right after open in `Db`'s constructor.
- Use `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` for write transactions so lock acquisition happens up front and honors the busy timeout.

Same applies to the Python-side connections (`cache.py` / `store.py` — stdlib `sqlite3` has a default 5 s timeout, so the C++ side is the acute gap).

title: Setting both MCP tool filters crashes the server at startup
body:
Found while building #50, in released code.

`fastapi_mcp` **raises** when it is given both an include filter and an exclude filter. The gateway passes both through, so a deployment that sets `MCP_INCLUDE_TOOLS` and `MCP_EXCLUDE_TOOLS` together does not start at all.

Two things make this worse than a plain crash:

* It contradicts the settings' own documentation. `MCP_EXCLUDE_TOOLS` describes itself as narrowing `MCP_INCLUDE_TOOLS` — which is a reasonable thing for an operator to want, and reading the description is exactly what leads them into the crash.
* It fails at startup rather than at request time, so an operator who adds the second setting to a running deployment discovers it as an outage.

#50 fixed it in passing, because it needed the same code path to exclude the Ollama routes from the MCP tool surface: `mcp.py` now resolves the two filters itself and passes a single resolved set down, which also makes the documented narrowing behaviour real.

That fix is not separable — it is the same few lines the feature needed — so this issue exists to record the defect for the release notes rather than to carry its own commit. Users on 1.16 and earlier are affected.

Ref: `stdapi/mcp.py`, `MCP_INCLUDE_TOOLS` / `MCP_EXCLUDE_TOOLS` in `stdapi/config.py`

title: fix(turns): release DB connection during the hours-long diarize-api call in speaker_turns_dag
body:
## Problem

**Severity: HIGH** (on `origin/main`).

`congress_videos/speaker_turns_dag.py::_process_task` (~lines 183-215 on main) opens one DB connection for the entire per-chapter loop:

```python
with pg.get_connection() as conn:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        for chapter in chapters:
            result = run_chapter_turns(chapter, cur, ...)
```

`run_chapter_turns` extracts audio, parses the SRT, then calls `detect_turns(...)` → `api_diarize_fn` — an HTTP call to the diarize-api sidecar whose client timeout is **6 hours** and whose diarization runs ~4.6× realtime. The connection acquired at the top sits open for minutes-to-hours per chapter, on a shared server capped at `max_connections=100` with a documented starvation incident.

This violates "never hold a connection/lock across an external API call".

## Fix

Decouple: run the ffmpeg/SRT/diarize work with **no** open connection; acquire a short-lived connection only immediately before `_upsert_turns` + the `turns_detected_at` UPDATE, per chapter. Compatible with the per-chapter durable-commit design from #193.

Depends on / pairs well with the central `get_connection()` context-manager fix.

Source: full-repo audit, 2026-08-24 (DB agent, verified against origin/main ac24314).

title: fix(model): a violation regex containing a quote is either refused or silently dead
body:
## Bug Description

A `violation:` regex that contains a `"` character cannot survive a write/read round-trip. Depending on how the author quotes it, `scar promote` either refuses the scar outright or accepts a scar whose tripwire can never match. `scar lint` reports `0 errors` in the second case.

This matters because `violation:` is the only field whose whole purpose is to fire later, unattended. A silently-dead tripwire is worse than an absent one: `scar status` lists the scar as active, so the surface reads as protected when nothing is watching.

The identical defect was already found and fixed for `command_anchors` — `src/scar/model.py:152-153` strips both quote styles, with a comment naming the trap ("so the silently-dead single-quoted trap (daimon 0021) cannot recur for command anchors"). `violation` never received the same fix.

## Steps to Reproduce

Any HTML/JSX-oriented scar hits this, since attribute matching needs a literal quote. Real case: a fence forbidding `aria-live` on `<div id="state">`, needing to match both attribute orders.

**Path A — double-quoted with escapes:**

1. In a candidate, write:
   ```yaml
   violation: "id=\"state\"[^>]*aria-live|aria-live[^>]*id=\"state\""
   ```
2. Run `scar promote <slug>`
3. Promotion is refused:
   ```
   refusing to promote, lint errors: invalid violation
   /id=\"state\"[^>]*aria-live|aria-live[^>]*id=\"state\/: bad escape (end of pattern) at position 51
   ```

Cause: `src/scar/model.py:157` reads the field with `.strip('"')`. `str.strip` removes *every* leading/trailing `"`, so the trailing `\""` loses both quotes and leaves a dangling backslash — hence `bad escape (end of pattern)`. Nothing un-escapes the interior `\"` either.

**Path B — single-quoted (the dangerous one):**

1. In the same candidate, write:
   ```yaml
   violation: 'id="state"[^>]*aria-live|aria-live[^>]*id="state"'
   ```
2. Run `scar promote <slug>` — succeeds
3. Inspect the promoted file:
   ```yaml
   violation: "'id="state"[^>]*aria-live|aria-live[^>]*id="state"'"
   ```
4. Run `scar lint` → `lint: 6 file(s), 0 with errors`

Cause: the read at `model.py:157` strips only `"`, so the literal `'` characters stay in the value. The write at `model.py:77` then wraps that value naively:

```python
lines.append(f'violation: "{self.violation}"')
```

The stored regex now begins with a literal `'`, so it cannot match any real source line. The scar loads, lists as active, and never fires.

## Expected Behavior

A `violation:` regex containing `"` round-trips unchanged, and a regex that cannot round-trip is rejected loudly rather than stored dead.

## Actual Behavior

- Path A: a valid regex is rejected with a confusing error pointing at a position in a string the author never wrote.
- Path B: an invalid regex is accepted, serialized wrong, and reported clean by `lint`.
- `scar lint` does not validate the serializer's own output, so neither `promote` nor `lint` catches Path B.

## Suggested Fix

Two independent changes; the second is the one that closes the class of bug:

1. **Read side** (`model.py:157`) — mirror the `command_anchors` treatment so both quote styles are stripped:
   ```python
   violation=_field(front, "violation").strip('"').strip("'"),
   ```
2. **Write side** (`model.py:77`) — stop hand-rolling the quoting. Emit a YAML single-quoted scalar with `'` doubled, or block scalar, so a value containing `"` survives verbatim.
3. **Lint** — after serializing, re-parse and assert the recovered `violation` equals the in-memory one. That round-trip assertion would have caught this without knowing the specific quoting rule, and would also cover `condition:`, `pattern:`, and `- command:` which share the naive `f'... "{...}"'` shape at `model.py:64`, `:66`, `:73`.

A regression test worth adding: promote a candidate whose `violation` contains both `"` and `'`, then re-read it and assert the compiled pattern still matches the string it was written for.

## Workaround

Avoid quote characters in the regex entirely by matching the quote as `.`:

```yaml
violation: "id=.state.[^>]*aria-live|aria-live[^>]*id=.state."
```

This round-trips cleanly and matches both attribute orders, at the cost of precision.

## Environment

- scar-cli 0.16.2 (editable install)
- macOS 15.3 (Darwin 25.3.0)
- Python 3.13.7
- zsh

title: Bug: web_ui router PUT /snippets/{id} is dead - shadowed by snippets.router route collision
body:
## Summary
`app.py:54-56` includes `snippets.router` before `web_ui.router`, and **both** register `PUT /snippets/{snippet_id}` with no prefix (snippets.py:96, web_ui.py:130). FastAPI resolves the first match, so the web_ui handler is unreachable — every PUT to that path goes to the API router's handler forever.

This was discovered during the #198 fix (PR #199): the language-validation regression tests had to call the web_ui handler directly because it can't be reached over HTTP.

## Impact
- The web UI's own update endpoint (loose dict body, tailored response shape) never runs; whatever behavior it implements is dead code.
- Any future fix or change to web_ui's update path will appear tested (unit level) but have no effect in practice.

## Suggested options
1. Give `web_ui.router` a prefix (e.g. `/ui`) so its routes are distinct, updating the web frontend calls accordingly; or
2. Merge the web_ui handler's extra behavior into the canonical snippets router and delete the duplicate.

Option 1 preserves both surfaces; option 2 removes the duplication. Either way, add a test asserting each registered route has exactly one handler.

## Repro
```python
from snipcontext.web.app import create_app
for r in create_app().routes:
    if getattr(r, "path", "") == "/snippets/{snippet_id}" and "PUT" in getattr(r, "methods", set()):
        print(r.endpoint.__module__)
# -> prints only the snippets router module
```

title: [bug][registry] registry init produces a workspace add-catalog rejects; a registry cannot be bootstrapped through the CLI
body:
## Problem

`registry init` and `registry add-catalog` cannot be used together. A governed registry cannot be created through the CLI at all; the only working path is to hand-author the complete `registry.yaml` first, which is what `init` exists to avoid.

Three defects compound.

## 1. `init` does not create `registry.yaml`; `add-catalog` requires it

```
$ mint-oscal registry init --output /tmp/r1
exit=0
$ find /tmp/r1
  /tmp/r1/catalogs   /tmp/r1/packs   /tmp/r1/generated      # no registry.yaml

$ mint-oscal registry add-catalog --registry /tmp/r1 --id nist-800-53r5 \
    --file NIST_SP-800-53_rev5_catalog.json \
    --source-uri https://github.com/usnistgov/oscal-content \
    --release v1.5.0 --license NIST --authority NIST
error='registry.yaml does not exist: /private/tmp/r1/registry.yaml'
exit=2
```

The two sides disagree in the source, and the docstring states the intent that the code does not implement:

```python
# governance/registry_builder.py:44-45
def init_registry(output: str | Path) -> Path:
    """Create an empty registry workspace; Catalog import creates the YAML contract."""
    ...  # creates catalogs/, packs/, generated/ and returns

# governance/registry_builder.py:78-80
    registry_file = root / "registry.yaml"
    if not registry_file.is_file():
        raise RegistryError(f"registry.yaml does not exist: {registry_file}")
```

`init_registry`'s docstring says Catalog import creates the contract. `add_catalog` refuses to.

## 2. Validation requires three defaults that cannot exist yet

Hand-writing a minimal `registry.yaml` with `catalogs: []` does not help. `add_catalog` validates after writing, and validation requires all three defaults to resolve:

```python
# governance/registry.py
if document["defaults"]["catalog"] not in catalog_ids:
    raise RegistryError("default Catalog is not registered")
if document["defaults"]["profile"] not in profile_ids:
    raise RegistryError("default Profile is not registered")
if document["defaults"]["pack"] not in pack_ids:
    raise RegistryError(...)
```

Observed, with `defaults.catalog` forward-referencing the id being added:

```
$ ... add-catalog --id nist-real ...
error='default Profile is not registered'
exit=2
```

## 3. No verb creates a profile or a pack

```
$ mint-oscal registry --help
    list  show  validate  lock  verify  init  add-catalog
```

`add-catalog` is the only mutating verb. There is no `add-profile` and no `add-pack`, so `defaults.profile` and `defaults.pack` can never be satisfied through the CLI.

## Net effect

```
init  ->  add-catalog                       impossible (1)
init  ->  hand-write minimal yaml  ->  add-catalog   impossible (2, 3)
hand-write a COMPLETE registry     ->  add-catalog   works
```

Confirmed by building a full registry by hand with one catalog, one profile and one pack:

```
$ mint-oscal registry validate --registry /tmp/r2       EXIT=0
$ mint-oscal registry add-catalog --registry /tmp/r2 ...  EXIT=0
```

So `add-catalog` is sound. It just has no reachable starting state, and `init` produces a workspace no other verb accepts.

## Suggested direction

Either make `init` write a valid skeleton (empty `catalogs`/`profiles`/`packs`, `defaults` absent or nullable), or relax validation so `defaults` entries are optional until the registry is non-empty. The first is smaller. Whichever is chosen, `init_registry`'s docstring should match the code.

If profiles and packs are meant to stay hand-authored, say so in `init`'s output, and have `init` emit the skeleton with a comment naming what the author must add before `add-catalog` will accept anything.

## Acceptance criteria

- `mint-oscal registry init --output DIR && mint-oscal registry add-catalog --registry DIR ...` succeeds with no manual file editing.
- A test covers the init-then-add sequence end to end.
- `init_registry`'s docstring describes what it actually does.

## Environment

`origin/main` `2b5fa5a` (0.2.3), Python 3.14.6, clean `/tmp` copy, `uv pip install .`

title: GUI becomes unresponsive after installing prompted dependencies (Nobara)
body:
Raised in [discussion #17](https://github.com/loteran/Arctis-Sound-Manager/discussions/17) by @jsuvanto, on Nobara with an Arctis 7, installed from Terra (`python3-arctis-sound-manager`):

> I started the GUI immediately. After installing some prompted missing dependencies, the GUI was completely unresponsive. I forcibly closed it and ran `asm-setup`. After that the GUI worked.

## What is already in place

The suggested fix — running `asm-setup` on first launch — has been there since **v1.0.72**: `gui/first_run_dialog.py` runs it automatically when `.setup_done` is missing, streaming its output into the dialog. So the report is *not* the missing-setup case it looks like, and that is what makes it worth its own issue rather than a note in the discussion.

Which leaves the freeze itself unexplained. The sequence was: fresh install → GUI opened → a dependency prompt appeared → dependencies installed → the window stopped responding. Killing it and running `asm-setup` by hand fixed it for good.

## What would settle it

Untested guesses would be cheap here; what is missing is a reproduction. Worth asking the reporter, or anyone who hits this:

- whether the first-run dialog appeared at all before the freeze (it should have, on a machine with no `.setup_done`)
- which dependency prompt it was — the general dependency dialog, or the Clips one
- whether the daemon was running at the time (`systemctl --user status arctis-manager`)
- a bug report from the app afterwards, which carries the version and the journal

One candidate worth ruling out first: the first-run dialog runs `asm-setup` as a subprocess and streams its output. A subprocess that blocks waiting on something — a password prompt with nowhere to appear, a package manager lock held by the install that just ran — would present as exactly this, a window that stops responding while nothing is visibly wrong.

title: Incorrect line counting for pagination and counting rows on lists (Activity and Shows)
body:
The SQL queries used for counting rows and pagination are incorrect due to two reasons : 
- Because of joins on mark and favorite, there are some duplicated lines that should be filtered with the distinct instruction.
- ORDER BY instructions are not deterministic enough. Only with an ORDER BY on the requested field, the result can be random in case of ex-aequo. We must add a secondary sort key in order to be sure to have always the same result.
- Activity flow count only unioned only 3 of the 5 event sources. The union must be done on the whole event sources.

title: Make Specification structuring reliable for realistic To Spec sources
body:
## Problem

The closed Specification Structuring Agent cannot produce a complete `agileforge.spec.v2` candidate from a realistic registered To Spec source under the configured production model. The source is registered correctly and remains immutable, but every structuring attempt ends without a candidate.

## Reproduction

1. Use AgileForge commit `6f2a9c4e3209947e7ea6bd81bb88b31e65f60d42`.
2. Attach a clean repository and accept its Vision and Product Goal.
3. Register an 8,726-byte To Spec Markdown source plus a 1,297-byte root `CONTEXT.md`.
4. Run `agileforge specification structure` with the production `specification_structurer` role.

## Observed evidence

- The normalized structuring input is 17,465 characters.
- With the default 4,096-token setting, output validation reports incomplete JSON at column 20,069.
- With `VISION_INTERVIEWER_MAX_TOKENS=16384`, output validation still reports incomplete JSON, this time at column 19,713.
- Both attempts close durably as `SPECIFICATION_PRODUCER_FAILED` and create no candidate.
- `adapters/adk/agents/specification_author.py` currently obtains its limit from `get_vision_interviewer_max_tokens()`.
- Increasing that borrowed limit alone did not make the production provider return a complete object.

## Expected behavior

A realistic, fully resolved To Spec source can be transformed into one complete, schema-valid, source-faithful `agileforge.spec.v2` candidate without shortening or weakening the source.

If the configured provider cannot satisfy the required output contract, AgileForge fails with an actionable capacity or incomplete-output error rather than the generic `SPECIFICATION_PRODUCER_FAILED`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Specification structuring has a dedicated, explicit generation budget rather than borrowing Vision configuration.
- The effective generation configuration participates in attempt provenance and recovery identity.
- An integration fixture comparable to the observed 8,726-byte To Spec source successfully produces and validates the complete canonical candidate under the supported production-provider contract.
- A length-limited or incomplete provider response creates no candidate and exposes a specific durable failure code and message.
- Recovery does not silently truncate source content, omit accepted clauses, or require the human to weaken the Specification.
- Exact source hashes, Vision/Product Goal lineage, closed-schema validation, and human review remain unchanged.
- Focused tests and `uv run --frozen pyrepo-check --all` pass.

## Manual-test evidence

- Registered source fingerprint: `sha256:9d98bbdb4b8b688a9e4172805513a8d613344e1e1daa1bc8ae3fc9c859c9aa32`
- Repository revision: `1594e28671d247d711558a66495df1a53d1d2d1b`
- Failed workflow attempts: 20 and 21 in the isolated acceptance profile.

title: [Bug] Responses API raw CoT: ThinkingPart.content 为空，_normalize_thinking_event 未作用于最终 ModelResponse
body:
## 问题描述

使用 OpenAI Responses API + raw CoT provider（如 `svc/kimi-k2` via vLLM/litellm）时，`ThinkingPart.content` 为空字符串，导致：
- OTel 捕获的模型请求中 thinking 内容为空
- 下一轮请求中 thinking 内容丢失
- 模型无法看到之前的推理内容

## 根因

### pydantic-ai Responses API 的两种 reasoning 事件

| 事件类型 | `ThinkingPart.content` | `provider_details` |
|---|---|---|
| `ResponseReasoningSummaryTextDeltaEvent` (标准) | ✅ 有内容 (`chunk.delta`) | 无 |
| `ResponseReasoningTextDeltaEvent` (raw CoT, gpt-oss/vLLM) | ❌ 空字符串 | ✅ `raw_content` 有内容 |

`svc/kimi-k2` 走的是 **raw CoT** 路径（`openai.py:3732-3738`），reasoning 内容存在 `provider_details['raw_content']` 里，`ThinkingPart.content` 是空的。

### agentpool 的 _normalize_thinking_event 只作用于流式事件

`event_mapper.py:224-253` 的 `_normalize_thinking_event()` 能从 `provider_details['raw_content']` 提取内容填充到 `ThinkingPart.content`。**但这个归一化只作用于流式事件**（给 ACP 转换器用），**不作用于最终存储的 `ModelResponse`**。

```
流式事件 → _normalize_thinking_event() → ACP 日志有内容 ✅
                                          ↓
最终 ModelResponse → parts manager 构建 → ThinkingPart.content="" ❌
                                          ↓
                              存入 message_history → 下一轮请求 → OTel 捕获到空内容
```

### 为什么 Chat Completions API 不受影响

Chat Completions API 用 `reasoning_content` 字段，`_map_thinking_delta()` 直接把内容存入 `ThinkingPart.content`，不经过 `provider_details`。

## 影响范围

- 所有使用 Responses API + raw CoT 的 provider（vLLM, LM Studio, litellm bridge, gpt-oss via OpenRouter）
- 不影响 Chat Completions API
- 不影响标准 Responses API（使用 summary text 的 provider）

## 复现方式

1. 配置 model 为 `openai:svc/kimi-k2`（走 Responses API）
2. 运行 2 轮对话
3. 检查第 2 轮的 OTel 捕获或 `/tmp/real-llm-req.json`
4. 观察 `ThinkingPart.content` 为空字符串

## 修复方向

在最终 `ModelResponse` 构建后、存入 `message_history` 前，对 `ThinkingPart` 做归一化：从 `provider_details['raw_content']` 提取内容填充到 `content` 字段。

可选方案：
1. **agentpool `after_model_request` hook** 中归一化 `ModelResponse`（推荐，改动最小）
2. **pydantic-ai `_finish_handling`** 中归一化（上游修复，影响面更大）

## 关键代码路径

- `pydantic-ai/models/openai.py:3732-3738` — `ResponseReasoningTextDeltaEvent` 只传 `provider_details`，不传 `content`
- `agentpool/orchestrator/event_mapper.py:224-253` — `_normalize_thinking_event()` 只作用于流式事件
- `agentpool/orchestrator/event_mapper.py:89,93` — 调用点

## 验证

- 切换到 `openai-chat`（Chat Completions API）后问题消失 ✅
- 纯 pydantic-ai FunctionModel 测试中 ThinkingPart 内容正确保留 ✅
- agentpool native agent + FunctionModel 测试中 ThinkingPart 内容正确保留 ✅

title: Section 7's package savings are modeled on the household's current plan, and the switch is not priced
body:
Surfaced by adversarial review on #196, then again by Codex review. The **labelling** half was fixed in #196; this issue is the **modelling** half that remains.

## What #196 fixed

§7 previously opened *"All packages keep **{{BEST_PLAN}}**"* — which reads as advice in a decision section. For a household ranked second in `plan_results.csv`, §0 says "a cheaper rate plan exists" and §3 quantifies the gap, while §7 presented every package's savings and projected bill computed on the losing tariff with no indication the two were on different footings.

#196 made that sentence standing-aware: §7 now states the modelling basis rather than a recommendation, and says the plan comparison is §3's and the switch is not included in the savings shown.

## What remains, and it is a real analysis question

**No committed artifact prices switching plans.** `data/package_results.json` models every package on the household's current tariff. So a household on a second-best plan can read what each package saves *on the plan it is on*, and separately read what a different plan would cost — but nothing combines them, and the zero-cost switch never appears as a package component.

This is the more useful number for exactly the household #196 exists to serve.

## The question that must be settled before anyone implements it

**What is the baseline?** The packages' savings are deltas against the household's ACTUAL bills, which were billed on the current plan at the tariffs in force then. Re-basing them onto a different plan changes what the baseline means.

CLAUDE.md §1 and §9 both bite here:

- *"never subtract current-rate model deltas from prior-year actual bills to project a future bill — that mixes tariff vintages"*
- *"one pipeline per package figure: composite results come from a single integrated simulation re-billed end-to-end, never by adding numbers from different models and subtracting an overlap estimated in a third"*

So the wrong implementation is easy to reach: take each package's modelled saving, add the plan-switch delta from `plan_results.csv`, and publish the sum. That adds two deltas from two models on two baselines. The right implementation re-bills the package's modified year on the recommended plan, end to end.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A committed script prices at least one package on a plan other than the household's current one, re-billed end-to-end rather than by summing deltas
- [x] The baseline is stated explicitly in the report — what the savings are deltas against, on one rate vintage
- [x] §7 presents the switch as available to a household the ranking beats, or states why it is not modelled
- [x] A test renders the full template for a household ranked second and asserts the package figures and the plan comparison are on a stated common footing
- [x] This household is sole cheapest, so its published §7 output is byte-identical

Related: #196 (the chrome and the labelling), #178 (§4's row), #177 (the matrix rounds to whole dollars, which is what settles the ranking these packages would be re-based on).
