title: Implement native Codex identity, registration, and strict worktree ownership
body:
## Outcome
Ship the native runtime layer that lets independent Codex sessions declare their wave roles and exchange validated, attributable state transitions.

## Wave
Parent: #192; program: #189.

## Scope
Adapt the shared CPP registration/registry/mailbox protocol through the supported CxPP source bridge. Implement explicit native thread/process-generation mapping, declared capabilities, durable acknowledgements, validated transition recording, and the proved delivery strategy. Preserve shared helper semantics while making CxPP-owned adaptations explicit and reproducible.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Atomic registration handles worker-first startup, duplicate owner registration, live-owner conflict, stale replacement, and policy-revision rebrief.
- [ ] Messages bind to the intended wave, assignment, role, and generation; unknown provenance cannot gain gate authority.
- [ ] Liveness and delivery readiness are separate and visible; timeouts do not declare a process dead.
- [ ] Automated contract tests cover stale/duplicate messages and recovery with no live production sessions.
- [ ] No Claude-only address derivation or codex:auto capability fence is used as the native Codex identity contract.

## File lane and coordination
native runtime adapters plus adopted flow-register/registry/mailbox/lexicon helpers and their tests; serialize shared-source regeneration

## Execution constraints
Installed plugin packaging is delivered by the separate packaging child; this issue must not claim install acceptance early.
The coordinator reviews the concrete implementation plan and exact PR head. User authorization covers scoped delivery after planning; no repeated human approval is needed for routine implementation choices.

Blocked by: #196, #197

<!-- cxpp-native-platform:native-register -->

## Refined component boundary
This issue owns the native identity adapter, role registry, process-generation/liveness evidence, capability declarations, and binding to worktree claims. Durable message/event storage is #205; production queue/wake dispatch is #206. Define the shared API from #197, and coordinate any common files. Do not duplicate those implementations.

title: [UI] Lobby mode buttons do not read as tabs and the panel heading repeats them
body:
Parent: #156

## Observed

The lobby renders `New game`, `Continue game` and `Join game` as three full-width filled buttons in a card. Selecting one swaps the panel below, whose heading repeats the same label ("New game" button above a panel titled "New game").

## Impact

The three controls behave as a tab bar but are styled as primary actions, so clicking one appears to do nothing except retitle a section further down. The repeated heading reinforces the impression that nothing happened.

## Proposal

Style them as tabs with a selected state, or keep them as buttons and drop the duplicated panel heading. Either way the selected mode should be visually obvious without reading the panel below.

## Acceptance criteria

The active lobby mode is identifiable from the control itself, and its label is not repeated as the heading of the panel it reveals.

title: Every test that runs a workflow shell re-derives how to find bash
body:
## Description

The knowledge that a test must resolve `bash` through `PATH` before running it
is duplicated at every site that runs a workflow shell block, with no shared
helper:

```
tests/test_coverage_comment_workflow.py:138:        [shutil.which('bash'), '-c', script], cwd=workdir, env=child_env,
tests/test_coverage_comment_workflow.py:144:    bash = shutil.which('bash')
tests/test_coverage_comment_workflow.py:419:    bash = shutil.which('bash')
tests/test_ci_workflows.py:69:    bash = shutil.which('bash')
```

Each of those is correct on its own. Nothing carries the reason, and nothing
makes a new site inherit it, so the requirement has to be remembered
independently every time a site is added.

It was not remembered on the most recent addition. A new helper invoked the
shell by the bare name `bash` instead, and all four `windows-latest` cells of
the `suites` job failed on a single test while all eight Linux and macOS cells
passed. On Windows a bare program name is resolved by searching the system
directory before `PATH`, so it selected the Windows Subsystem for Linux
launcher rather than the Git for Windows `bash` that the other sites select.
WSL then reported that it has no installed distribution, and it reported it in
UTF-16, so the failure text does not match a plain search for an error in a
job log.

This is the second failure of this shape on the same branch. An earlier test
that reached a shell also passed every local suite and all eight Linux and
macOS cells before failing all four Windows cells.

## Expected Behavior

A test that needs to run a shell block obtains it from one shared helper that
resolves the executable through `PATH` and explains why, so a new call site
inherits the behaviour instead of re-deriving it, and getting it wrong is not
possible without editing the helper.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Add a test that runs a shell block by passing the bare name `bash` as the
   first element of a `subprocess` argument list.
2. Run the suites on Linux and macOS; they pass.
3. Run them on a `windows-latest` runner; the test fails with a UTF-16 message
   from the Windows Subsystem for Linux.

## Environment / Context

Only the `windows-latest` legs are affected. The behaviour follows from
`CreateProcess` searching the application directory, the current directory,
the system directory and the Windows directory before `PATH`, while
`shutil.which` searches `PATH` in order.

## Discovered During

Pull request #170, after all four Windows cells failed on a newly added shell
helper. The specific defect is fixed on that branch; this issue is about the
duplication that allowed it, which predates the branch.

## Suggested Fix

Unverified. Move the resolution into one helper the shell-running tests share,
have it fail loudly and name the program when the executable cannot be
resolved, and keep the reason in a comment there rather than in each caller.

title: Re-verify the launch copy in #57 against current releases and modern-di 3.x
body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Split out of #57, which is `ready-for-human` because launching is a one-shot judgment call. This
part is not: re-verifying factual claims against published sources is mechanical, and doing it ahead
of time means the maintainer is not doing archaeology on the morning of the launch.

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Re-verify every factual claim in #57's inlined launch copy against current published sources, correct the copy in place, and record what changed.

**Current behavior:**

#57's body carries the full ready-to-post copy for Show HN, r/Python, Lobsters, the org-story
announcement, the awesome-list one-liners and the social posts. Its header states the facts were
checked **2026-07-13** and must be re-checked before posting. A spot-check on 2026-09-06 found the
numbers stale and, more importantly, `modern-di` across a major version boundary:

| Claim in the copy | 2026-09-06 |
|---|---|
| `modern-di` 2.28.0 | 3.4.0 |
| `modern-di` 116 releases | 127 GitHub releases (PyPI lists 98 versions) |
| `modern-di` 58 stars | 66 stars |
| `that-depends` 4.0.2 / 251 stars | 4.1.0 / 253 stars |
| `httpware` 0.15.1 | 0.16.0 |
| `faststream-outbox` 0.10.5 | 0.13.1 |
| `lite-bootstrap` 1.2.3 | 1.4.0 |

That table is a starting point, not the work. Re-derive every figure at the time you run, rather than
trusting the right-hand column.

**Desired behavior:**

#57's body holds copy whose every factual claim is true as of a stated check date, and a comment on
#57 records what changed. Where a claim can no longer be made honestly, it is corrected or removed
rather than softened: the copy's own credibility strategy is the honest "when *not* to use this"
framing, so an overstatement is worse here than a missing boast.

**Sources of truth, in order:**

- Version, release count, licence, runtime dependencies: PyPI and the project's own repository.
- Star counts: the GitHub API, for both our projects and the ones compared against.
- Behavioural and design claims: the project's current documentation and source, never the copy's
  own prior wording.

**Numeric claims to re-derive:** the versions and star counts above, plus `modern-di`'s zero runtime
dependencies and MIT licence, `faststream-outbox`'s first-commit date and release count, Dishka's
star count (the copy says "~1.2k stars to my ~60", and both halves move), and `httpware` building on
**httpx2** rather than httpx.

Pin what "releases" means. GitHub releases and the PyPI version count disagree (127 vs 98), and the
copy currently cites one number without saying which.

**Design claims to re-verify against `modern-di` 3.x.** These were written against 2.x and a major
version may have moved any of them. Do not renumber them; re-read the current docs and source:

- "13 official integrations", and the list given. The copy names twelve frameworks and then adds the
  pytest plugin separately, so the count and what it includes need reconciling.
- Providers are plain class attributes on a `Group`, with no `@provide` decorator and no string keys.
- No DI decorator needed in the FastAPI, Litestar, FastStream and taskiq integrations.
- Exactly seven integrations still need an `@inject`: Starlette, Flask, aiohttp, Celery, arq, aiogram
  and Typer. Verify both the count and the membership.
- The FastAPI boundary still names the provider in the `FromDI(...)` form the copy shows.
- The resolve path is synchronous and `resolve` never awaits, while the container is an async context
  manager supporting async finalizers.
- Scopes run APP → REQUEST with build-time cycle and scope-violation checks.
- Async resources are constructed in the framework lifespan and injected by type via a
  `ContextProvider`.
- The docs pages the copy links or refers to still exist: the async-lifespan recipe, the comparison,
  the "design decisions" page, and the "do you even need a DI container?" page.

Every URL in the copy must resolve, including the ones inside the org-story draft.

**Where the corrected copy goes:** edit #57's body in place, and update its "Facts checked" header to
the date you ran. A single source avoids the failure mode where a corrected copy sits in a comment
while the stale body stays above it and gets posted by mistake. GitHub retains body edit history, so
this is reversible.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] Every numeric claim listed above re-derived from PyPI or the GitHub API, with the value in the copy matching
- [ ] Every design claim listed above checked against current `modern-di` docs or source, and corrected where 3.x changed it
- [ ] The integration count and the integration list agree with each other and with the project
- [ ] The `@inject` count and membership verified, not assumed
- [ ] "releases" cites one source, and the copy says which
- [ ] Every URL in the copy returns 200
- [ ] #57's body updated in place, with a "Facts checked <date>" header reflecting the run
- [ ] A comment on #57 lists each claim changed, with old value, new value and the source used
- [ ] Any claim that could not be verified is called out explicitly rather than left standing

**Out of scope:**

- **Posting anything anywhere.** Do not submit to Hacker News, Reddit, Lobsters, dev.to, Hashnode, any newsletter, any awesome-list, or any social account. This issue ends at corrected text sitting in #57. Posting is #57's own work and is human-only for a reason.
- Rewriting the copy's voice, structure, argument or ordering. Correct facts, leave the writing alone.
- The launch schedule, and which project leads.
- Newsletter and syndication work (#59) and the podcast pitches (#72).
- Re-verifying on the posting date. That still has to happen, and #57's brief already requires it. This pass exists to make that final check cheap.

title: feat(store): the artifact records the environment that produced it
body:
Gap 2 of [`docs/self-describing.md`](../blob/main/docs/self-describing.md): the
retention argument is that a polygon may be discarded because it is a
deterministic function of the row and four numbers in `meta`. Issue #175
measured that the function is the **platform's** — tables captured on one
architecture differ in their last bits on another. The artifact records
`reg_version` and an envelope-parameter digest, and records nothing about the
environment that produced it.

So an auditor who recomputes and disagrees cannot tell *wrong machine* from *the
geometry moved*. Those are opposite findings and the file cannot separate them.

This issue **records** the environment. Acting on it — refusing to recompute off
the recording environment — is the issue that depends on this one, deliberately
split: writing the data and using it are different work.

## REGROOMED 2026-09-05 against `prior-art.md` §27

The sixth pass (issue #199) found that **gap 2 is solved practice with a name and
a file format**: the Reproducible Builds project defines reproducibility
*relative to a stated environment*, and records that environment in a
**buildinfo**. `limitations.md` §1 and issue #175 are not a discovery about this
project — they are the first thing that field says. Three consequences, and they
change what this issue asks for:

1. **Adopt the content list; do not derive one.** The four fields this issue
   originally named were reasoned from scratch. The practice's own advice is to
   **minimise** the recorded set to what the build actually depends on rather
   than enumerate the world. Take the list from §27, cite it, and justify each
   field by what would change the geometry — a list derived here would be the
   same list with no provenance and nobody maintaining it.
2. **Putting it in `meta` is a deviation and must be stated as one.** A buildinfo
   is deliberately *a separate build product*, so an archive can distribute it
   separately. This project has a reason the practice does not — Claim 2 says the
   file answers with no access to anything else — and that reason goes in the
   text on the pattern §5's PROFIsafe deviation uses. Unstated, it reads as
   unfamiliarity with the practice.
3. **Do not write the word *attributable* unqualified.** See #201, which carries
   that correction.

## The decision, so it is not taken in the PR

**`SCHEMA_VERSION` is bumped**, and the reason is `reg/store.py`'s own stated
criterion: a bump is for what a previous reader would be *confidently wrong*
about. A reader that meets a file recording its environment, ignores it, and
recomputes a discarded polygon anyway returns a region it believes is the one in
force. The file contains what would have prevented that. That is the bump's
case, and it goes in the version note beside the others.

## Acceptance criteria

- `meta` carries the environment as a **buildinfo for a geometry computation**,
  with the content taken from `prior-art.md` §27 and cited there. The fields this
  issue previously named — shapely version, `shapely.geos_version`, platform
  (enough to separate x86_64 Linux from arm64 Darwin), Python version — are a
  starting point and not the specification: each surviving field is justified by
  what would change the geometry, and anything that would not is left out per the
  minimise principle. Read from the running interpreter, never passed in and
  never defaulted.
- **The deviation is stated in the text**: the practice puts a buildinfo beside
  the artifact and this project puts it inside, because Claim 2 says the file
  answers alone. Stated on §5's PROFIsafe pattern — the departure, its reason,
  and what it costs.
- `SCHEMA_VERSION` bumped with its note, in the form the existing notes take —
  what a previous reader would be confidently wrong about.
- **The figures are re-measured**, `python -m reg.bench --resolution --seed 0`,
  on this branch and on `origin/main`. If they moved, every document naming them
  is republished in the same change and the PR body carries the attribution; if
  they did not, the PR body carries the measurement showing it. Include the
  control-rate rungs CI does not pin — the lesson of #181.
- The eleven fixtures still build and `reg.query` still answers over them.
- **The negatives ship with it:** an artifact whose environment keys are absent
  is a could-not-evaluate and not a pass; an artifact built twice on the same
  machine records the same environment; and no environment value is ever
  synthesised when the interpreter cannot report one — it fails loudly naming
  what is missing.
- `docs/lossiness.md`'s recomputation clause states that the environment is now
  recorded and what that does and does not buy — recording it makes a
  disagreement attributable; it does not make recomputation portable.

## Notes for the implementer

Do **not** add a dependency to read the versions. `shapely.__version__`,
`shapely.geos_version` and the standard library's `platform` and `sys` are
enough. `docs/plan.md`'s no-new-dependencies rule is binding.

This issue does not change any recompute path. `reg.graph.envelope_at` behaves
exactly as it does today.

## Affected areas

- `reg/store.py`
- `reg/graph.py`
- `tests/test_graph.py`
- `docs/lossiness.md`
- `docs/self-describing.md`

## Verification

`pytest`

Depends-on: #199

title: Wire signal analysis into the Chart Analysis panel
body:
## Background

PR #143 added a general **Chart Analysis** sidebar panel (`chart_analysis_panel.py` / `AnalyzeChartSeriesCommand`) that runs derivative, integral, arc-length, smoothing, and interpolation on any chart series — a plotted data series or a fitted curve — and writes the result to a new dataset.

In review, [@dpluscec suggested](https://github.com/Youth-Research-Center/PandaPlot/pull/143#issuecomment-5189593493) generalizing analysis this way, and also floated supporting signal analysis through the same panel. The author agreed and [asked in the PR thread](https://github.com/Youth-Research-Center/PandaPlot/pull/143#issuecomment-5208791644) if @KlaraMlinaric could pick this up — signal analysis already exists as its own standalone feature (`signal_analysis_command.py` / `SignalPanel`, added in #90), but it isn't wired into the new Chart Analysis panel yet.

## Task

Extend the Chart Analysis panel (or `AnalyzeChartSeriesCommand`) so signal-analysis operations (FFT/PSD/STFT etc., per the existing `pandaplot/analysis/signal` engine) can be run against a chart series/fit the same way derivative/integral/smoothing/interpolation are today — consistent source picker, segment support, preview, and apply-to-new-dataset.

## Scope notes

- Reuse the existing signal analysis engine/methods under `pandaplot/analysis/signal/` rather than duplicating logic.
- Out of scope for this issue: the merge-conflict fixes and the two automated-review fixes on PR #143 were already handled separately (see [this comment](https://github.com/Youth-Research-Center/PandaPlot/pull/143#issuecomment-5386792155) and [this one](https://github.com/Youth-Research-Center/PandaPlot/pull/143#issuecomment-5388120449)) — this issue is just the signal-analysis integration follow-up.

title: [Enhancement]（持久化记录上次执行时间）保留调度任务最近执行记录
body:
## 背景

当前调度器最近执行结果保存在 Bot 进程内存中的 `_job_run_results`。Bot 重启后，这些记录会全部丢失；Web Admin 的“上次执行”因此重新显示为空，无法反映重启前的实际运行历史。

## 需求

为纳入调度器监控的任务持久化最近一次执行信息，至少包括：

- `last_run`
- `last_status`
- `last_error`（如有）

Bot 启动、任务重新注册和 Web Admin 读取时，应保持记录与当前任务 ID 的一致性；已删除任务不应继续出现在监控快照中。

## 设计约束

- 继续通过 Bot 进程写入、Web Admin 跨进程只读的状态边界。
- 使用原子写入，避免 Web Admin 读到半截状态文件。
- 明确时间格式与时区，保持现有带时区 ISO 8601 语义。
- 任务从未执行时仍应能明确表示“暂无执行记录”。
- 记录持久化失败不得阻塞实际调度任务执行，但应留下告警。

## 验收

- Bot 重启前后，同一任务的最近执行时间和状态能够恢复。
- 成功、失败、任务删除、任务重新注册场景均有测试覆盖。
- 与调度器监控页的“上次执行”展示联调验证。

请在 v1.14.0 正式版发布前完成。当前页面缺少部分任务执行结果记录的问题另见对应 Bug Issue；任务名称可读化见 #179。

title: Add a tts-eval bench skill over the engine registry
body:
## Task

Add a `tts-eval` bench so evaluating a new TTS model is a repeatable command, not a throwaway harness: register the model as an engine in `render.py`'s `ENGINES` table, run the bench, read one HTML report. The bench renders a fixed corpus through the registry's own adapter (never a re-implementation of the TTS call), always re-renders the current production engine as the control, computes a fixed metric set, appends a dated ledger entry, and writes a self-contained HTML report with side-by-side players.

## Context

On 2026-09-04 Breeze-TTS-2 was evaluated against Qwen3-TTS for Surface Tension with a scratch harness (eval_tts.py / analyze.py / report.py, discarded). It found objective parity, 4× slower rendering, a non-commercial license, and a ~1-in-5 derailment rate on takes past ~35 s that the speech-rate gate cannot see. Cory wants to evaluate new models regularly and use features Qwen3 lacks. The engine registry (spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-04-tts-engine-registry-design.md`, slice 1) makes "write the adapter" the way a model is evaluated; this issue is slice 2, the bench that exercises it.

## Motivation

As the operator of three shows, I want one command that tells me whether a new model is better than what ships, with the same lines and the same metrics every time, so that the next evaluation costs an adapter and a run rather than a day.

## Pointers

- `skills/daily-podcast/render.py` — `ENGINES`, `EngineSpec`, `render_segments(..., engine=)`, `_render_take` (after the registry PR). The bench calls these; it does not call mlx-audio itself.
- `skills/daily-podcast/bloopers.py` — the precedent for a sibling maintenance CLI that imports `render` (calls `render.run`, keeps the seam patchable). Follow it.
- `skills/surface-tension/refs/{ryan,aiden,ethan,chelsie}.{wav,txt}` — the cast clips; the bench's clone corpus.
- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-04-tts-engine-registry-design.md` — "Measurements that shape the design": the metric set and the derailment definition (whisper WER > 0.15, non-ASCII in transcript, heard/script word ratio outside 0.9–1.1).
- `tests/test_st_skill_md.py` — drift-test pattern if the bench ships a SKILL.md with tables.

## Constraints

- The bench renders through `render.render_segments` / `render.ENGINES`. Re-implementing the generate call defeats the purpose.
- The production engine (`qwen3`) is re-rendered as the control on every run; never compare against a stored baseline (mlx-audio upgrades move it).
- Fixed corpus in the repo: 3 lines per cast voice (short/medium/long), one 8-turn four-voice scene, a vocal-events probe, a direction probe; fixed metrics: WER (mlx-whisper large-v3-turbo), speaker similarity to own clip (resemblyzer or equivalent), nearest-clip identity, median f0, chars/s vs the clip's own, leading/trailing silence, RMS, × realtime, load time, peak memory, and the derailment flag.
- License is a first-class column, read from `EngineSpec.license`.
- Ledger lives in user state (`~/.config/daily-podcast/evals/<date>-<engine>.json`), not the repo; the report is one self-contained HTML file with base64 audio.
- Analysis dependencies (mlx-whisper, librosa, jiwer, speaker-embedding lib) are a `bench` extra in `pyproject.toml`, never runtime deps.
- No change to `render.py` behaviour. Tests must not load a real model (fake the adapter the way `tests/test_lines.py`'s `fake_tts` does).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `python3 skills/tts-eval/bench.py --engine breeze` renders the corpus on `breeze` and on `qwen3`, writes the ledger entry and the HTML report, and exits 0.
- [ ] Adding a third engine to `ENGINES` with no other change makes it benchable.
- [ ] The report flags a derailed take by the spec's definition, verified with a fixture transcript containing non-ASCII.
- [ ] A test proves the bench never calls `mlx_audio` directly (grep-level or import-seam test).
- [ ] SKILL.md for the bench documents the corpus, metrics, and the ledger path, with a drift test on any table.

## Out of scope

- Deciding which engine a show uses; changing `render.py`; the daily-show derailment guard (separate issue); sweeping quantization or temperature (a later bench feature).

## Cross-references

- Registry spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-04-tts-engine-registry-design.md`
- https://github.com/schmug/clodcast/issues/169 (bloopers bin: the sibling-CLI precedent)
- https://github.com/schmug/clodcast/issues/89 (speech-rate gate: what the derailment metric complements)

title: plugins+docs: complete the doberman.detectors extension seam (example + docs/EXTENDING.md)
body:
## What
Doberman's plugin registry (`src/doberman/engine/registry.py`) declares **11** entry-point groups — `doberman.rules`, `doberman.detectors`, `doberman.policy_sources`, `doberman.auth_providers`, `doberman.audit_sinks`, `doberman.drift_observers`, `doberman.cost_observers`, `doberman.algebra_adapters`, `doberman.adjudicators`, `doberman.egress_brokers`, and `doberman.async_challenge_backends` (lines 38–68) — each with a working interface (a duck-typed protocol/shape check). Ten resolve through a `discover_*()` function; the eleventh, `doberman.async_challenge_backends`, resolves through `active_async_backend()` instead, and the docs page should flag that difference. Only **one** group, `doberman.rules`, has a runnable worked example (`examples/plugin-guardrail/`, with its own installable package + `tests/test_example_rule.py::test_entry_point_is_discoverable_after_install`), and there is no single doc page enumerating all 11 seams for a contributor deciding where to plug in. Complete the closest sibling seam, `doberman.detectors` (structurally identical to `doberman.rules` — both discover `Guardrail`-shaped objects, per `discover_detectors()`'s own docstring, lines 166–174): add a second example package mirroring `examples/plugin-guardrail/`'s shape but registered under `doberman.detectors`, with its own install-based discoverability test, and add `docs/EXTENDING.md` documenting all 11 groups (one short paragraph each: what shape is required, how it resolves, and a link to the one worked example).

## Difficulty: level-6
Completing an extension seam end-to-end: the interface and registry already exist and are proven correct (`discover_detectors`, `tests/unit/test_registry.py`), and there's a worked example to mirror — the work is producing a second, real, installable example that proves the pattern generalizes beyond `doberman.rules`, an install-based test for it (mirroring `examples/plugin-guardrail`'s), and the docs page that ties all 11 seams together for the next contributor.

## Safety constraints (do not weaken these)
- The new example detector must be genuinely raise-only, like `ExampleRule` (`examples/plugin-guardrail/src/example_plugin/rules.py`) — PASS or AUTH only, never BLOCK from a tutorial plugin, and it must never put a raw path, argument, or payload into its `explanation`.
- `docs/EXTENDING.md` must state the same defensive-loading guarantee `registry.py`'s module docstring already documents (a broken/hostile plugin is logged and skipped, never crashes core, and can only ever add risk via `combine()`) — do not describe or imply a stronger contract than the code actually provides.
- Do not wire the new example into CI's default `testpaths` (mirrors #194's constraint) — keep it self-contained under `examples/`, installed only by its own test/instructions.

## Starting files
- `src/doberman/engine/registry.py` — `discover_detectors()` (line 166), `DETECTOR_GROUP` (line 39), the full list of 11 groups (lines 38–68) for the docs page.
- `examples/plugin-guardrail/` — the pattern to mirror (`pyproject.toml` entry-points block, `src/example_plugin/rules.py`, `tests/test_example_rule.py`).
- New: `examples/plugin-detector/` (package name e.g. `doberman-example-plugin-detector`, entry point under `[project.entry-points."doberman.detectors"]`).
- New: `docs/EXTENDING.md`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `examples/plugin-detector/` is a real, installable package registering an example under `doberman.detectors` (not `doberman.rules`).
- [ ] Its own test proves real (non-monkeypatched) discovery, mirroring `plugin-guardrail`'s `test_entry_point_is_discoverable_after_install`.
- [ ] `docs/EXTENDING.md` documents all 11 entry-point groups from `registry.py`, each with: required shape, how it resolves (`discover_*()`, or `active_async_backend()` for `doberman.async_challenge_backends`), and a link to the one worked example (rules or detectors).
- [ ] Neither new example is added to CI's default `testpaths`.
- [ ] Existing behaviour unchanged (no test weakened, no output format broken)
- [ ] `ruff check . && ruff format --check .` and `lint-imports` pass
- [ ] `pytest` passes

## How to validate
```
pip install -e examples/plugin-detector
pytest examples/plugin-detector/tests -v
pip uninstall -y doberman-example-plugin-detector
```

## Out of scope
- Do not build an example for any of the other seams in this issue — `doberman.detectors` only; a follow-up can cover the rest.
- Do not modify `examples/plugin-guardrail/` itself.
- Do not add `examples/` to CI's default `testpaths`.

## Notes for contributors
New here? Start with [CONTRIBUTING.md](../blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). Issues are labelled `level-1` (docs only) through `level-10` (new subsystem) — pick one at your level and climb. Comment to claim an issue before starting.

title: [Polygon Contract] Öffentlichen Assignment-Command für modulare Area-Zuordnungen bereitstellen
body:
## Kontext

Blocker für:

- `oklabflensburg/ocp-module-analysis-areas#5`
- #184

Der historische Analysis-Areas-Sync aktualisierte nach Änderungen an Analysegebieten auch Polygon↔Gebiet-Zuordnungen. Ein externes Modul darf dafür weder `user_polygons` direkt lesen noch fremde ORM-Modelle importieren.

## Ziel

Einen kleinen öffentlichen Polygon-Domain-Command bzw. Service-Port bereitstellen, mit dem ein Modul seine Area-Zuordnungen anhand eines stabilen DTO-/Geometry-Vertrags aktualisieren lassen kann.

## Leitprinzip

```text
analysis-areas owns area state
polygon domain owns user_polygons and assignment mutation

analysis-areas
→ public PolygonAssignmentCommand
→ polygon domain performs assignment atomically
```

Keine Foreign-ORM-Imports.

## Anforderungen

1. Keine `UserPolygon` ORM-Instanzen über Modulgrenzen.
2. Keine direkte SQL-Abfrage von `user_polygons` aus externen Modulen.
3. Stabile, versionierte DTOs/Protocol.
4. Command muss einen klar abgegrenzten Scope unterstützen, z. B. betroffene Area(s) oder vollständigen Rebuild, ohne Analysis-Areas-spezifische Host-Sonderlogik.
5. Geometry-Input über generischen öffentlichen Geometry-/Feature-DTO oder vorhandenen öffentlichen Port.
6. Transaktionsverhalten explizit: Command arbeitet entweder in übergebener Session/Unit-of-Work oder dokumentiert klar seine atomare Boundary.
7. Idempotent bei wiederholter Ausführung.
8. Bestehende Tabellen/Relationen weiterverwenden.
9. Keine parallele Assignment-Tabelle allein für die Modularisierung.
10. Observability mit stabiler Operation/Modul-Korrelation, keine hoch-cardinalen Labels.

## Tests

- kein ORM-Type im öffentlichen Contract
- initiale Assignment-Erzeugung
- Update bei Geometrie-/Area-Änderung
- idempotenter zweiter Lauf
- Entfernen/Neuberechnen veralteter Assignments entsprechend historischem Verhalten
- Transaktions-/Rollback-Verhalten
- externe Test-Implementierung kann den Command ohne private Imports konsumieren

## Nicht-Ziele

- kein Polygon-Domain-Redesign
- keine neue Geometrie-Engine
- keine Analysis-Areas-Fachlogik im Host
- kein Remote/Microservice-Zwang

## Akzeptanzkriterien

- [ ] Öffentlicher Polygon Assignment Command/Port existiert.
- [ ] Keine fremden ORM-Modelle überschreiten die Boundary.
- [ ] Externe Module benötigen keinen direkten Zugriff auf `user_polygons`.
- [ ] Assignment-Verhalten ist idempotent und transaktional klar definiert.
- [ ] Bestehende Datenstruktur bleibt erhalten.
- [ ] Contract-/Architecture-Tests sind grün.

Parent/coordinates: #184, oklabflensburg/ocp-module-analysis-areas#5
Architecture principle: Runtime klein halten. Komplexität an Systemrändern lösen.

title: Auth-required pages redirect silently with no explanation and no return path
body:
## Summary

Logged-out visitors to `/moderation` or `/account` are silently bounced with zero explanation. Confirmed live (no-redirect-follow request): both routes return a bare 302 to `/` — `pages/moderation.astro`/`pages/account.astro` use a plain `Astro.redirect("/")`, no query param, no flash message, and no `next` preserved to return the user after login.

## Context

Found during a 2026-09-03 independent frontend review. A moderator whose session expired and who reopens a bookmarked `/moderation` link lands on the homepage with no indication anything happened, and has to manually re-navigate to moderation after logging back in — the header's own login links do carry a `next` param, but only for whatever page they're clicked from, which by then is already `/`, not the page the user actually wanted.

## Scope

- Redirect through the login flow with `next=/moderation` (or `/account`) preserved, so a successful login lands the user back where they were headed.
- Show a one-line explanation if landing on the homepage anyway (e.g. via a query param triggering a small banner).

## Out of scope

- Any broader auth-flow redesign.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Visiting `/moderation` or `/account` while logged out and then logging in returns the user to the originally-requested page
- [ ] Some visible indication exists of why the redirect happened

title: feat: proper characterisation for Nebula, Star Cluster, and Anomaly environment types
body:
## Summary

When `unusual_stars=True` and the primary-type roll produces a Nebula, Star Cluster, or Anomaly result from the WBH p.219 Unusual column, the current implementation falls back to generating a Giants-class star and recording the environment type in `Star.special_notes` only. No bespoke physical characterisation is applied.

## Current behaviour

`_generate_peculiar_star()` routes Protostar to `_generate_protostar()` (full WBH p.219 characterisation), but Nebula, Star Cluster, and Anomaly all call the Giants branch, resulting in a G/K/M Ib/II star with `special_notes = "Peculiar environment: <type>"`.

## Expected behaviour

Each environment type should receive appropriate physical values and orbit-generation treatment per the WBH rules (p.219+):
- **Nebula** — ambient environment, no stellar luminosity driving an HZ in the normal sense; consider how MAO, HZCO, and world-count rolls should behave
- **Star Cluster** — multiple background stars, distinct from a single-star or binary system
- **Anomaly** — referee-defined; may need a placeholder/stub characterisation with extension hooks

## Impact

A seed that generates a Nebula (e.g. seed 2689 with `unusual_stars=True`) currently produces a G Ib supergiant with a special note rather than a dedicated environment object.

## Related

- Deferred-features row: "Post-stellar special circumstances (Phases 2–4)" — this issue covers the environment sub-types within Phase 1 that were left as stubs.
- `_generate_peculiar_star()` in `traveller_stellar_gen.py`
- WBH pp. 219+

title: feat: implement Star Cluster generation (WBH pp.219+)
body:
## Summary

Implement Star Cluster generation as a special system type, triggered by the Peculiar column in Unusual Star generation (issue #21 Phase 1 uses a Giants+special_notes placeholder for this result).

## WBH rules (pp.219+)

### What is a star cluster?

A dense conglomeration of stars — either an open cluster (recent star formation, same nebula origin) or a globular cluster (billions of years old, gravitationally bound). Key characteristic: all stars in the cluster have the same age.

### Single-hex cluster

A single-hex cluster contains **2D+5 star systems**, all of the same age.

### Multi-hex cluster

Larger clusters are circular, **1D+1 hexes across**. Each hex beyond the centre has **DM−2** to the number of star systems.

### Cluster age

Age = **1D × 1D × 50 million years**. Normally less than 1 billion years.

- If cluster age < 200 million years: apply **DM+1** to the Star Type Determination table (p.15); treat any roll of 2 as Unusual column.
- If the Unusual column result is another Star Cluster → treat as **BD (brown dwarf)** instead.
- Anomaly results may also be treated as brown dwarfs.

### Merged stars

If a star's mass would have caused it to leave the main sequence before the cluster's age, it is instead a **merged star** (collision of two less massive stars). Its planetary system applies:
- **DM−2** to all rolls for planet existence and quantity (DM+2 for the default gas-giant absence check)
- **DM+2** on the eccentricity table for all orbits

### Hex spillover

Each hex adjacent to the cluster hex (except the original rolled cluster hex) has a chance equal to the normal stellar density probability of containing a regular system that the cluster has "spilled into".

### Jump restrictions

Unless the jump is to a directly adjacent star within the cluster, or from outside to a star on the outer edge:
- All jumps suffer **DM−1D** to Astrogation and Engineer (j-drive) checks.
- This DM is rolled once per jump and changes on a daily basis.

## Scope

- Extend the Peculiar column handling in `traveller_stellar_gen.py` (Phase 1 placeholder) to generate a proper star cluster system.
- Add cluster-level data to `TravellerSystem` (age constraint, merged-star flag, cluster size/hex count).
- Modified planet existence and eccentricity rolls for merged-star systems in `traveller_orbit_gen.py`.
- Extend FastAPI and gen-ui to expose cluster data.

## Dependencies

- Issue #21 Phase 1 must be complete (introduces the Peculiar column and the Giants+special_notes placeholder this feature replaces).

## Notes

- The Peculiar column result "Star Cluster" currently sets `special_notes = "Star Cluster"` as a placeholder. This issue replaces that placeholder with real generation.
- Anomaly (also a Peculiar column result) may remain as a named special note, or get its own minimal treatment; decide when implementing.

title: No repository-level screen: the gates that reject a candidate target are still a hand pass
body:
## Impact

Every gate that decides whether a *repository* is worth running against is applied by hand, in conversation. `mailman check-target` works one level down: it reads a recorded duplicate search and answers whether an *issue* is claimed. Nothing screens the repo, so the same GitHub queries get re-typed for every candidate and the result is never recorded.

## Evidence, 2026-09-03

Screening finance and agent-framework candidates by hand produced this, none of it reusable:

| repo | stars | last outside human merge | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `OpenBB-finance/OpenBB` | 72.6k | 2026-07-24 | fails the two-week bar |
| `microsoft/qlib` | 48.2k | 2026-07-23 | fails |
| `AI4Finance-Foundation/FinRL` | 16.2k | 2026-07-12 | fails |
| `polygon-io/client-python` | 1.5k | 2026-04-10 (bot) | fails |
| `freqtrade/freqtrade` | 54k | 2026-09-02, but every outside merge for three years is one collaborator | effectively closed |
| `hummingbot/hummingbot` | 19.8k | 2026-09-02 | Cython core, no local compiler |
| `ccxt/ccxt` | 43.8k | 2026-09-02 | Python is generated from TypeScript |
| `pydantic/pydantic-ai` | 19.7k | 2026-09-03 | 100+ open PRs, maintainer bot already working issues, assignment required |
| `openai/openai-agents-python` | 29.1k | 2026-08-28 | passes |

## Gates the screen should apply, in this order

1. Most recent merged pull request from someone other than a maintainer, within 14 days, excluding bots and excluding a single recurring collaborator.
2. A CI workflow that actually runs tests, not just publish and lint.
3. Pure Python: no Cython or Rust workspace member in the dev install, and source not generated from another language.
4. Contribution and AI policy permits a disclosed AI-assisted pull request.
5. Whether the issue tracker is saturated by AI pull requests: ratio of open PRs to issues, and median time from issue open to first PR.
6. Stars, last.

## Next action

Add `mailman screen-target OWNER/REPO` that runs these against the GitHub API, prints a pass/fail line per gate, and writes the record next to the run data so a rejected candidate is not re-screened. Gates 1, 2, 3 and 5 are answerable from the API alone; gate 4 needs the contributing file read.

Related: #34 records the same shape of gap for assignment protocol.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Distill verdict defects into class-level amend briefs in Orchestrate
body:
## Problem

The strongest empirical finding of the SeaTwirl Fast Track run concerns the amend path's information quality, not model strength. Ticket #85 spent two amendments at Sol xhigh and failed both; a standalone repair of the same ticket at the same model and effort then succeeded on the first attempt. The difference was the brief: the repair worked from a distilled failure report — every verdict defect quoted verbatim with file/line anchors, marked fixed-then versus still-open across both verdicts, a pinned contract, and the explicit instruction to audit *all* steps for each defect class rather than only the cited instances. Across the whole run, six of six standalone repairs built on such distilled briefs succeeded first-try, while eight of sixteen tickets exhausted their amendment budgets on the engine's amend path.

The pattern held on the failing side too: #85's verdict 2 repeated a defect class (substring-only contract test) that verdict 1 had already named — the amending builder had fixed the cited instances but not the class, exactly what a distillation step's "audit all steps for this class" instruction exists to prevent.

## Desired behavior

The engine's amend path feeds the amending builder a distilled defect brief instead of raw verdict text:

- an inexpensive distillation step (a cheap model suffices; the SeaTwirl repairs used one) transforms the verdict into: each defect verbatim with its anchors, its status across prior verdicts, the defect *class* it belongs to, and the instruction to audit the entire owned surface for that class;
- the pinned ticket contract and the preserved attempt's exact commit history ride along, so the amendment starts from the same complete picture a standalone repair would;
- the distillate is stored in the run's durable state beside the verdict, so a later escalation (budget exhaustion → standalone repair) reuses it instead of re-deriving it.

## Acceptance criteria

- An amendment prompt contains the distilled defect list with classes and audit-the-class instructions, not only raw verdict prose.
- The distillate is durable in the state directory and referenced by the failure report when the budget is exhausted.
- Verdict independence is untouched: distillation summarizes the judgment, it never re-judges.

## Out of scope

Changing the two-amendment budget or verdict authority.

title: 【部署】匿名只读复用 Console 壳，仅权限不同
body:
## 背景

#155 为避免把 Console 的 mutation 和 private 数据放到公网，匿名面做成了独立的极简 HTML。实际效果是首页只有英文 “Public documents” 和一个 Search 链接，没有工作区卡片、没有阅读壳，和本机 Console 完全不像，匿名读者几乎无法使用。

## 目标

匿名只读部署使用与本机 Console 同一套前端壳与阅读路径；可见内容仅限 `public-read.json` 已声明的 public 根，写操作与未公开对象不可达。

## Stories

### S1. 匿名打开即见 Console 工作区壳并读到公开文档

- **角色**：用户
- **前置**：remote 上 current 含合法 public-read 快照，且至少有一个 public 根。
- **操作**：打开 public-read 首页，看见公开工作区卡片，点进工作区，打开已公开 target 正文。
- **闭环结果**：页面使用 Console 的仪表盘/工作区布局与样式；只出现已公开工作区；正文为该 public 根内容。
- **定量**：公开工作区卡片数 = public-read 快照中出现的 workspace 数；未公开 workspace 卡片数为 0。

### S2. 未公开与写操作同形拒绝

- **角色**：用户
- **前置**：同一 public-read 进程，磁盘上另有未出现在快照中的 workspace。
- **操作**：访问未公开 workspace URL；提交新建工作区或 Run 等写请求；观察页面上的写入口。
- **闭环结果**：未公开 URL 与不存在同形拒绝；写请求不成功且不改变磁盘；页面无新建/删除/Run/添加参考等写入口。
- **定量**：写请求成功次数 0；磁盘字节与请求前一致。

## 范围

- In：public-read 进程的 HTML 壳改为复用 Console 模板与 `/` `/w/{slug}` 读路径；列表与文档按 public-read 快照过滤；写路由在 public-read 下不可用。
- Out：登录、远程写入、改变 #118 的 locator/Permit 判定、TLS。

## 复现 / 依据

本机 Console 首页是工作区卡片网格；115 public-read 首页是英文空壳加 Search。#155 §5.1 放弃改造 Console 导致可用性失败。

## 验收标准

- [ ] **S1**：public-read 首页为 Console 仪表盘壳，仅列出公开工作区，可进入并读到公开正文。
- [ ] **S2**：未公开 URL 同形拒绝；写请求失败且磁盘不变；页面无写入口。

## 关联

- #155
- #118


## 设计

- 状态：L1 **Approved**（[L1 提案](https://github.com/xforce-io/kairo/issues/200#issuecomment-5475724501)；用户明确推翻 #155 §5.1）。
- L2：[`docs/design/200-console-public-read.md`](https://github.com/xforce-io/kairo/blob/feat/200-console-public-read/docs/design/200-console-public-read.md)
- public-read 复用 Console 壳与 `/` `/w/{slug}` 阅读路径；仅快照内根可见；写方法与未公开 URL 同形拒绝。

experiment: validate source-grounded relation seed retrieval
body:
## 目的

固定Git sourceから根拠付きrelationを取得し、query内で参照されたsource documentをrelation seedとして拾うretrieval candidateが、現行NGR defaultよりrelation path retrievalを改善しながらdirect / semantic / negative cohortsを維持できるか検証する。

## 前提

- Issue #197 / PR #199のv23 developmentでは、Homeからmigrationへの固定edgeが存在してもHomeがrelation seedに選ばれず、migrationはlexical hitとしてrank 3へ返るだけで期待path provenanceを持たなかった。
- v23のdocument path / text / content hashは固定Git commit由来だが、relation edgesとquery / goldはfixture-authoredであり、実repository dependency discoveryを測っていない。
- intent-aware cross-encoderはprefilterが持たないrelation pathを復元できないため、重いreranker比較より前にretrieval入口を検証する必要がある。
- 既存anchored graph experimentはrelationを改善した一方、direct / negativeを退行させた。relation改善だけで採用しない。

## 制約

- v23 protocol / fixtures / raw packets / evidence / resultsを変更、再実行、performance evidenceとして再利用しない。
- relation sourceは固定commitのMarkdown link、import、または同等のsource-visible referenceから決定論的に取得し、source path、target path、edge type、取得方法、content hashを固定する。根拠のないfixture-authored edgeをsource-groundedと呼ばない。
- fresh query / goldをdevelopment / holdoutへ結果観測前に分離し、既存caseのコピー、言い換え、近接変形を拒否する。
- workerはgoldへ接触しない。source acquisition / identity / leakageをprotocol validityとして評価し、現行baselineのrelation失敗は性能結果としてcandidate gateと分離する。
- original / full-query NGR defaultをbaselineにし、relation-source anchoring candidateを別armとして比較する。
- candidateはrelation path completenessとrelation cohort MRR / hit@5を厳密に改善し、direct / semantic per-case、cohort MRR / hit@5、negative forbidden countを退行させない。
- まずretrieval-onlyの安価なprotocolで検証し、cross-encoder再評価はretrieval candidateが全gateを通った場合だけ別successorで行う。
- fresh protocol / SQLite、deterministic replay、exactly-once、retry 0、shared DB不変、append-only evidenceを維持する。
- passing resultでもNGR default、MCP config、physical integrationを自動変更しない。

## 対象ファイル

- source-grounded relation acquisition
- relation seed retrieval candidate
- 新しいresult-free protocol / runner / fixtures / tests / docs
- shared observation engineは必要な最小extensionだけ

## 関連

- #197
- PR #199
- #129
- docs/anchored-bm25-graph-hybrid-experiment.md

title: test(backend): detect virtualenv drift from requirements.txt at test-session start
body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Problem

Nothing detects when a developer's virtualenv has drifted from `backend/requirements.txt`. Test results from a drifted environment are indistinguishable from real application defects.

This is not hypothetical. It already cost real work: #190 was filed reporting 15 integration-test failures "against the pinned dependency set", including an `AttributeError` in the request path of `GET /roles` and `GET /users` that was reasoned about as a probable production bug. The venv was in fact **64 packages** out of date:

| Package | Pinned | Was installed |
|---|---|---|
| `fastapi-pagination` | 0.15.16 | 0.13.1 |
| `fastapi` | 0.141.1 | 0.139.1 |
| `fastapi-async-sqlalchemy` | 0.7.1.post3 | 0.6.1 |
| `bcrypt` | 5.0.0 | 4.3.0 |

Rebuilding the venv from `requirements.txt` made the `AttributeError` disappear entirely. The endpoints were healthy the whole time. The issue's acceptance criteria asked for a "fix" that would have broken correct, working code — see the triage notes on #190 for the full mechanism.

The cost of this drift was a wrong diagnosis, an issue written around it, and a fix that would have caused the outage it was trying to prevent.

## Why CI cannot catch this

Backend CI installs from `requirements.txt` into a fresh environment on every run, so CI never drifts. The drift is purely local, and its damage is done locally — a developer or agent draws a false conclusion from a misleading test run and files or fixes based on it.

A guard therefore has to run on the developer's machine, and the highest-value moment is **the start of a test session**, because that is exactly when a drifted environment starts producing misleading output.

## Recommended design

A session-scoped check in the backend test configuration (`backend/conftest.py` already exists) that compares installed distribution versions against the `==` pins in `requirements.txt` and reports any drift before tests run.

- Compare exact pins; report the count plus the first N offenders with pinned vs installed, so the message is actionable rather than a wall of text
- Name the remediation command in the message
- Provide an environment-variable escape hatch, so someone deliberately testing an upgrade is not blocked
- Keep it fast — it should read already-available metadata, not shell out to the network

`.pre-commit-config.yaml` exists and is an alternative home, but it is the wrong moment: drift causes misleading *test runs*, and not every test run follows a commit.

## The open question

**Should drift fail the test session, or warn loudly and continue?**

Failing is the only option that reliably prevents the #190 scenario, because a warning in a long pytest header is easy to miss — and in that incident the misleading output was believed over several rounds of analysis. Failing is also obstructive for anyone mid-upgrade, though the escape hatch covers that case.

Warning preserves the current workflow exactly and costs nothing when someone is deliberately off-pin, but it only works if the person reads it.

My recommendation is **fail with an escape hatch**: the failure mode it prevents is expensive and hard to spot, and the opt-out makes the obstruction a one-time cost for the rare deliberate case. This is a developer-experience call, though, which is why it is not yet specified.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A drifted backend venv is detected at test-session start, before any test executes
- [ ] The report names the drift count and shows pinned vs installed for the worst offenders
- [ ] The report names the command that fixes it
- [ ] A documented escape hatch allows a deliberate off-pin run
- [ ] A matching venv produces no output and no measurable slowdown
- [ ] Packages installed but absent from `requirements.txt` do not trigger it — only pinned packages at the wrong version
- [ ] Tests cover a matching environment, a drifted one, and the escape hatch

## Out of scope

- Adopting a lockfile or changing dependency management (`requirements.txt` stays the source of truth)
- Frontend dependency drift
- Auto-installing or auto-repairing the environment; the guard reports, the developer fixes
- The corrupted `~mails` / `~json` distributions and the pre-existing `safety` version conflicts in the current venv — unrelated environment rot

title: [Feature]: Use tiling, aspect preservation, and interleaved placement at inference
body:
### Component

Model (Python)

### Problem statement

The model has a high-resolution understanding path and never uses it at inference.

`model/modules/vision_encoder.py:56-121` implements `ImageTiler`, which splits a
high-resolution image into encoder-sized tiles plus a global thumbnail, with bicubic position
embedding resampling so one encoder accepts any tile shape. `model/framer.py:220`
`encode_image_tiles()` is the tiling-aware entry point. Its only callers are
`model/framer.py:382`, `model/training/contrastive.py:28`, `model/eval/image.py:18`, and
`model/eval/video.py:24` - training, contrastive pretraining, and evaluation.

Inference takes a different route. `model/serve.py:348-350` handles the `understand` op by
calling `_load_image()`, and `model/serve.py:127-134` resizes unconditionally to a
`config.image_size` square, so aspect ratio is discarded and a tall page becomes a squashed
square. `model/generate.py:115-123` then calls `model.forward_vision()`, and
`model/framer.py:323-333` runs the plain encoder with no tiling. A 2000-pixel-tall page is
therefore seen at 256 pixels square, which is well below the resolution at which rendered text
is legible.

Placement has the same problem. The configuration supports `mm_token_placement="interleaved"`
with an `InterleavedSequenceBuilder`, but `model/framer.py:287-289` concatenates
`prefix_embeds` ahead of the text, so at inference an image always sits before the whole prompt
instead of at the position where it was mentioned. With several attachments in one message,
their relationship to the surrounding text is lost.

### Proposed solution

- Preserve aspect ratio in `model/serve.py:127`: resize to fit the tile grid rather than to a
  fixed square, and let tile count carry the resolution.
- Route `model/generate.py:115` through `encode_image_tiles()` so the inference path gets the
  same tiles plus thumbnail that training and evaluation already use, honouring the existing
  `vision_tiling`, `vision_max_tiles`, and `vision_thumbnail` settings at
  `model/configs/model_config.py:53-62`.
- Honour `mm_token_placement="interleaved"` in `model/framer.py:287` on the generation path, so
  encoded modalities are written into placeholder positions instead of prepended.
- Keep the current behaviour reachable when `vision_tiling` is off, so the laptop-scale presets
  are unaffected.

### Alternatives considered

Raising `image_size` instead of tiling. Rejected: attention cost is quadratic in patch count, so
a larger single image raises cost everywhere, while tiling keeps cost per tile and lets
effective resolution grow with tile count.

Tiling only for documents. Rejected: a photograph of a whiteboard or a screenshot has the same
problem, and a second code path would drift from the first.

### Additional context

Feeds the dense-text recognition work, which cannot reach a usable character error rate while
every page is downsampled to a fixed square. Closes when the inference path reports the same
tile count as the evaluation path for the same image, with a test at `framer-tiny` scale.

title: Extend the now line across the whole time grid and open it at the current hour
body:
## Summary

Two changes to the Calendar mode's time grid — the component shared by the `Week` and `Day` ranges. First, the current-time line is drawn **once across every day column** instead of inside today's column, and it is drawn **in every displayed range**, not only the one containing today. Second, the grid's opening scroll anchors on the **current hour minus one** rather than on the first event of the day, and it stays current: the line repositions on a 5-minute tick, and the grid re-anchors when the date rolls over at midnight. The line remains a hairline in `--ink` — never a fill — and today's column keeps its existing `is-today` treatment. Month and Agenda are unaffected.

---

## Motivation

**The line stops at the edge of one column.** `.calendar-timegrid-now` is appended to today's `.calendar-timegrid-col`, so in `Week` it reads as a marker *on Thursday* rather than as the horizontal time reference the component is built to give. The whole point of a time grid is that a shared vertical axis lets you compare columns by eye; the one element that names your position on that axis refuses to cross it. Scanning "what is everyone doing right now" — the wall tablet's single most common question — means holding a horizontal line in your head across six columns that do not have one.

It also disappears entirely the moment you navigate. Look at next week and there is no time reference at all, so a 3 PM block next Tuesday has nothing to read against; the grid gives you no sense of where in a day that sits without counting hour labels.

**The opening scroll optimizes for the wrong thing.** The grid currently opens an hour ahead of the day's earliest event, capped at 7 AM — 6 AM in practice. That was the right default when the failure being avoided was "the first event is scrolled off the top," but it means the grid always opens at the *start* of the day regardless of when you are looking at it.

> It is 4:30 PM. You open Calendar to check whether anyone is free before dinner. The grid opens at 6 AM, ten hours of empty morning above the part of the day you actually asked about, and you scroll past all of it — every time, on a device you are usually standing at rather than sitting at.

The morning-scroll cost is paid on every visit; the early-event case it protects against is rare and self-correcting, because the all-day band and the day are both still one scroll away.

---

## Proposed Behavior

### The now line

- Draw **one** line per time grid, spanning **all** day columns, in both the `Week` and `Day` ranges.
- Draw it **whenever a time grid is rendered**, regardless of which week or day is displayed. A grid showing next month still shows the line at the current time.
- The line looks **identical in every case** — the same 1px `--ink` hairline whether or not today is in the displayed range. It is a reference to the time axis, not a claim about the displayed date, and today is already marked structurally by `is-today` on the day label and column.
- It spans the **day columns only**, not the hour gutter. The time axis stays clean, and the gutter keeps reading as labels rather than as a cell the line passes through.
- It stays non-interactive (`pointer-events: none`), so it never intercepts a tap meant for an event block underneath it.

### Keeping it current

- The line's position refreshes on a **5-minute** tick. Rally lives on a wall tablet that is left open all day; a "now" line frozen at whenever the page happened to load is worse than no line, because it is confidently wrong.
- When the tick crosses **midnight into a new date**, the grid re-anchors its scroll position as if freshly rendered, so the panel is showing the new day's early hours rather than yesterday's evening.
- The tick moves the line only. It does **not** re-anchor scroll on any other beat — a scroll position yanked out from under someone mid-read is a worse bug than a stale one.

### Opening scroll

- The grid opens with **the current hour minus one at the top of the scrollable area**, in both `Week` and `Day`.
- This **replaces** the earliest-event rule entirely. Whether the day contains a 5 AM event no longer affects where the grid opens.
- The anchor is computed from the **wall clock**, not from the displayed date — every week opens at the same place, so navigating between weeks does not make the grid jump.
- It applies on **every render**, matching current behavior: page load, arrow navigation between weeks, and switching between `Day` and `Week`.

### Edge cases

- **Between midnight and 1:00 AM**, the anchor clamps to the top of the grid (00:00). There is nothing above it to show.
- **Late evening** anchors normally — at 11:40 PM the grid opens at 10 PM, which puts the line near the top with the grid scrolled as far down as it goes. No special handling; the scroll container simply bottoms out.
- **Month** and **Agenda** render no time grid and are untouched by either change.
- **Timezone.** Both the line and the scroll anchor read the **browser's** clock, as `todayIso()` and the `is-today` rule already do. This is a known discrepancy with the install's configured timezone, which is what push notification times are rendered in. The two disagree only for someone viewing from another zone; **we are deferring to the tablet-on-the-wall scenario**, where the browser and the family's zone are the same machine and the same place. Reading the configured zone here would mean plumbing it into a component that currently needs no server state at all, for a case the primary device never hits.

---

## Proposed UI

### Time grid (`Week` and `Day`)

**Position:** the line moves out of `.calendar-timegrid-col` and becomes a direct child of `.calendar-timegrid-body`, which is already `position: relative`. Column-scoped is not merely a stylistic choice today — `.calendar-timegrid-col` sets `overflow: hidden` (so a 30-minute body on an 11:50 PM event does not paint past the bottom of the day), which means a line inside a column *cannot* escape it no matter what its `left`/`right` are.

As a child of the body it can span the grid's day tracks and stop at the gutter:

> `left: var(--timegrid-gutter); right: 0;` — the same token the body's `grid-template-columns` uses for its first track, so the line's start and the gutter's edge cannot drift apart.

**Appearance:** unchanged from the current `.calendar-timegrid-now` — `border-top: 1px solid var(--ink)`, `pointer-events: none`. One hairline, one weight, one color, in every range and on every date.

**No new controls.** Neither change adds a toggle, a setting, or a label. The grid opens where you need it and the line says when now is; both are defaults, not preferences.

---

## Example

> It is **4:30 PM on a Wednesday**. You walk up to the wall tablet and open Calendar in `Week`.
>
> The grid opens with **3 PM at the top**. A hairline runs straight across all seven columns just below the 4 PM label. Wednesday's column is shaded `--surface-sunken` as it already is, so you can see at a glance that the line is in *today's* column as well as everyone else's — but the line itself is what tells you the time, and it crosses Thursday, Friday and the weekend at the same height, so the 4 PM soccer practice on Thursday reads immediately as "this time tomorrow."
>
> You press the forward arrow to look at next week. The grid opens at 3 PM again — no jump, no re-scroll — and the line is still drawn at 4:30 PM, so next Wednesday's 4:15 PM appointment sits just above it and you can see without counting that it lands in the same slot as the thing you were just looking at.
>
> The tablet stays on the counter. At **4:35** the line has moved down a notch; by **7:00** it sits below the evening blocks. Just after **midnight** the grid re-anchors itself, and Thursday morning is on screen when someone walks past it at 6 AM.

title: [Tool Submission]: IDPFold - Conformational Ensemble Generation for Intrinsically Disordered Proteins
body:
**Platform Source:** GitHub  
**Category:** Structure Analysis  
**Parent Node / Genealogy:** AlphaFold 2 / Intrinsically Disordered Proteins  
**Target Tags:** `idp`, `intrinsically-disordered`, `conformational-ensembles`, `alphafold`, `polymer-physics`  

---

### 📌 Description & Context
IDPFold is a deep learning system specifically designed to generate realistic, diverse conformational ensembles for intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) and disordered regions (IDRs), matching SAXS and NMR data.

### 🔗 Key Links & References
- **Primary Link:** [https://github.com/Junjie-Zhu/IDPFold](https://github.com/Junjie-Zhu/IDPFold)
- **Reference / DOI:** [https://github.com/Junjie-Zhu/IDPFold](https://github.com/Junjie-Zhu/IDPFold)

### ✨ Key Features & Innovations
- Overcomes AlphaFold's single-conformation bias on disordered polypeptide chains.
- Generates ensembles that reproduce experimental radius of gyration ($R_g$) and NMR chemical shifts.
- Captures transient secondary structure elements and polyampholytic chain compaction.

### ⚖️ Strengths & Limitations
- **Strengths:** Accurate statistical mechanics description of disorder without multimillion-step atomistic MD.
- **Limitations:** Optimized primarily for disordered regions rather than rigid globular domains.

### 📋 Suggested Action Items for Alphafoldology
- [ ] Add tool entry to `tools_data_updated.json` / `tools_data.json` under `Structure Analysis`.

title: chore(metric-semantics): unify scattered and inconsistent metric semantics into a single authoritative contract
body:
## Context

Metric semantics in this repo are not unified. There is no single authoritative contract that says, for a given metric, what its role is (primary/secondary), which direction is better, what its unit/scale/precision are, and how it is aggregated. Interpretation is currently spread across several modules as hardcoded constants that have already drifted out of sync, and at least two real inconsistencies have been hit during leaderboard investigation (#151/#165/#177).

This is the largest piece of "hidden debt" in the repo: how a metric is interpreted should not be a guess, but today it often is. EvalScope solves this with `MetricSemantics` (contract) + `MetricCatalog` + `MetricResolver` and R1-R5 validation rules; we currently have none of these.

## Evidence: semantics are scattered, not centralized

- `src/vllm_hust_benchmark/perfgate.py` L36-L46: hardcoded `METRICS` tuple that only encodes **direction** (`throughput_tps` higher_is_better, `ttft_ms`/`tbt_ms` lower_is_better) plus a `DISPLAY_NAMES` dict. No unit, scale, precision, or role.
- `src/vllm_hust_benchmark/perfgate_measurement.py` L28-L38: a *second*, independent set of lists — `PRIMARY_METRIC`, `SORT_DIRECTION`, `SELECTED_RUN_METRICS`, `PERFORMANCE_METRICS`, `PER_RUN_METRICS` — duplicating the same metric names without any link to a catalog.
- `src/vllm_hust_benchmark/leaderboard_export.py` L23-L28: `REQUIRED_METRIC_KEYS` again re-declares the metric names; L346-L394 "derives" values via fallback chains that *guess* the semantics (e.g. `avg_latency * 1000` treated as `mean_ttft_ms`; `mean_tpot_ms → mean_tbt_ms → tpot_ms → tbt_ms`).
- `scripts/analyze_issue_151_regression.py`: metric thresholds and `metric_definitions` are local, and `metric_definitions` in reports are human-readable strings only (not machine-checkable).
- `scripts/generate_pr_measurement_block.py`, `scripts/analyze_issue_146_regression.py`: metric direction/semantics live in comments/docstrings.
- There is **no** `schemas/*metric*.json` and no catalog/resolver module.

## Evidence: real inconsistencies this debt has already caused

1. **Naming drift — `tbt_ms` vs `tpot_ms`.** `perfgate.py` and `leaderboard_export.py` use `tbt_ms`; issue reports and constraint keys (`typical_tpot_reduction_pct_vs_baseline`, `long_context_tpot_p95_ms`, see `docs/国产芯片大模型推理关键指标与基线评测方案.md`) use `tpot_ms`. The fallback chain in `leaderboard_export.py` L352-L357 exists precisely because raw result payloads have used different names over time.

2. **Aggregation conflict — mean vs median.** The leaderboard derives/compares `mean_ttft_ms` (mean), while the #165/#177 retest contract is **median-based** with 3 interleaved reps per side. `reports/issue_177_remaining_jumps_report.json` L415 already documents this:
   > `metric_config_contract_note`: "Original mean_ttft_ms vs original ttft_ms are not directly comparable (per #165 report)."
   
   The same metric name means different quantities in different places, and it is documented in a human-readable note rather than enforced by a contract.

3. **Workload/mode-dependent semantics are not encoded.** `docs/国产芯片大模型推理关键指标与基线评测方案.md` defines TTFT/TBT/Throughput and states that in offline "throughput" mode TTFT is not measured, and in `random-latency` `avg_latency` is end-to-end TTFT including all generated tokens. `leaderboard_export.py` L386-L394 implements this by nulling metrics per `benchmark_type`, but the "which metric is meaningful in which mode" rule is nowhere in a structured contract.

## Required work (following the EvalScope approach)

- Introduce a `MetricSemantics` contract capturing for each metric: `name`, `role` (primary/secondary), `direction` (higher_is_better/lower_is_better), `unit`, `scale`, `precision`, `aggregation` (mean/median/p99...), and applicable workload/mode.
- Introduce a `MetricCatalog` as the single source of truth and a `MetricResolver` to resolve any metric name → full semantics.
- Add validation rules (R1-R5) for consistency: unique definitions, resolvable names, no direction/unit drift, no duplicate declarations, mode-applicability rules.
- Migrate all scattered definitions (`perfgate.py`, `perfgate_measurement.py`, `leaderboard_export.py`, issue scripts, measurement-block generator) to read from the catalog, and generate report `metric_definitions` from the catalog instead of hand-written strings.
- Resolve the `tbt_ms`/`tpot_ms` naming and the mean/median aggregation ambiguity explicitly in the contract.

## Acceptance criteria

- One source of truth for metric semantics; no hardcoded direction/display/unit strings left outside the catalog.
- All existing modules consume the catalog through the resolver with identical behavior for current data (no regression in perfgate/measurement/leaderboard/tests).
- Reports emit `metric_definitions` generated from the contract.
- CI runs the R1-R5 validation rules so future drift fails loudly.
- Existing suites (`tests/`) stay green.

title: Zredukować powtarzane zapytania .count() w silniku osiągnięć dla wielopoziomowych tierów
body:
Część przeglądu wydajności backendu — patrz #192.

## Kontekst

`suchar_overflow/achievements/engine.py:37-86` (`SucharCountRule`, `VoteFunnyCountRule`, `VoteDryCountRule`, `VoteCastCountRule`) — każda reguła w `evaluate()` wykonuje osobne `.count()` na tej samej relacji dla **każdego kandydującego osiągnięcia** przekazanego jej przez `check_achievements()` (`engine.py:229-233`).

Przy seriach wielopoziomowych (np. tiery "Królowa/Król Sucharów" — kilka progów tej samej metryki `COUNT_SUCHAR`) `check_achievements()` woła np. `user.suchary.count()` osobno dla każdego nieodkrytego progu tej samej metryki — to samo zapytanie SQL powtórzone N razy (N = liczba progów tej metryki jeszcze nieosiągniętych przez użytkownika) zamiast policzone raz i porównane z wieloma progami.

Silnik jest wołany **synchronicznie**, w ścieżce `post_save` na `Suchar`/`Vote` (`achievements/signals.py`) — czyli ten koszt dotyka bezpośrednio czasu odpowiedzi na każdy dodany suchar/oddany głos.

## Do zrobienia

1. W `check_achievements()` pogrupować kandydujące osiągnięcia po `metric` przed wywołaniem `evaluate()`.
2. Dla każdej unikalnej metryki policzyć wartość (`.count()`/agregację) **raz**, a następnie porównać ten sam wynik z progami (`threshold`) wszystkich kandydatów tej metryki, zamiast wywoływać `evaluate()` osobno per kandydat z powtórnym liczeniem.
3. Upewnić się, że refaktor nie zmienia kolejności przyznawania osiągnięć w ramach jednego wywołania (jeśli kolejność ma znaczenie dla istniejących testów/zachowania — np. przyznawanie od najniższego do najwyższego progu).

## Testy

- Test liczby zapytań (`assertNumQueries`) na scenariusz z użytkownikiem blisko kilku progów tej samej metryki jednocześnie (np. tuż przed 2 kolejnymi tierami "Królowa/Król Sucharów") — przed poprawką liczba zapytań rośnie z liczbą nieodkrytych progów, po poprawce jest stała (1 na metrykę).
- Regresja: wszystkie istniejące testy `achievements/tests/test_engine.py` przechodzą bez zmiany zachowania (te same osiągnięcia przyznawane w tych samych warunkach).

## Kryteria akceptacji

- [ ] Liczba zapytań w `check_achievements()` zależy od liczby unikalnych metryk wśród kandydatów, nie od liczby kandydujących progów.
- [ ] Test liczby zapytań pokrywający scenariusz wielu progów tej samej metryki.
- [ ] `pre-commit run --all-files` i `just test` przechodzą bez błędów.

title: Native uint64 cell IDs for S2
body:
## Background

Follow-on to #198 (shared `--cell-id` infrastructure + A5 as the reference implementation). Adds native `uint64` cell ID support for the S2 backend — the largest per-call-site diff of the three capable backends, and the one most exposed to the dtype hazards #197 hardens against, so it's sequenced last.

## Implementation

`S2CellId` already supports both forms: `.id()` returns the native uint64 (as a Python `int`), `S2CellId(int)` constructs from one; `.ToToken()`/`S2CellId.FromToken(str)` remain for string mode. Mechanical substitutions in `s2vectorindexer.py` (following #198's "always compute natively" architecture — the int form is used internally whenever the backend is capable): `S2.S2CellId.FromToken(x)` → `S2.S2CellId(x)`, `cell.ToToken()` → `cell.id()`, at every construction/stringification site (`secondary_index`, `tokens_from_polygon`, `tokens_from_linestring`, `compact_tokens`, `get_resolution`, `children_at_res`, `token_to_child_token`, `cell_to_point`/`cell_to_polygon`). A small private helper pair (`_cell_from(x)`/`_cell_id(cell)`, dispatching on the indexer's cell-id mode) is worth using at every site rather than duplicating the branch inline each time.

## The S2-specific hazard: cell IDs above 2^63

Confirmed live and via raster2dggs's own regression test (`s2sphere.CellId.from_face_pos_level(5, 0, 4).id() > 2**63`, in manaakiwhenua/raster2dggs#97's `tests/regression/test_uint64_cell_ids.py`): S2 cell IDs on faces 4–5 legitimately exceed the signed 64-bit range. Any place a cell ID is used to filter/compare against a PyArrow dataset (e.g. reading back a specific parent partition) needs an explicitly-typed scalar — `pa.scalar(value, type=pa.uint64())` — since a bare Python int silently overflows PyArrow's default int64 type inference for values in that range. This needs its own dedicated regression test using a face-4/5 cell, mirroring raster2dggs's `test_s2_face5_parent_survives_the_store_round_trip`.

## Notes

Reuses #198's shared plumbing (CLI flag, partitioning-schema type-awareness, string-conversion boundary) and #197's compaction/merge dtype-safety hardening — this issue is the backend-specific diff plus S2-specific tests, including the face-4/5 high-value-cell regression test above.

title: core.__all__ names three symbols it never imports, so 'from core import *' raises
body:
Found by accident while building #19 — an `__all__` entry was added without its import, and the
check for that turned out not to exist. It already did not exist for three names on `main`.

## The defect

```python
>>> from srd_rules_engine.core import *
AttributeError: module 'srd_rules_engine.core' has no attribute 'DeathSaves'
```

Three of 159 `__all__` entries resolve to nothing:

| Name | Lives in | Claimed by `ENGINE_SHAPES` as |
|---|---|---|
| `DeathSaves` | `core.state` | `stable` → `core.state.DeathSaves.stable` |
| `adjust_roll` | `core.d20` | `die-applied-to-a-roll` |
| `override_to_success` | `core.d20` | `failed-test-overridden-to-success` |

## Why it matters more than a broken star-import

`core/__init__.py` exists to be R34's re-export surface: "Nothing outside `core` imports a `core`
submodule. Outer layers use what `core` re-exports, so 'the adapters are built over the same
contract' is checkable rather than aspirational."

All three names are **claimed as implemented capability** in `ENGINE_SHAPES` and **named in the
re-export surface**, and an outer layer that follows the rule cannot reach any of them. The
inventory says the engine resolves those shapes; the import rule says an adapter may only reach
them one way; and that way does not work.

`tests/test_layer_boundaries.py` checks the *direction* of imports and cannot see this — a name
missing from a re-export is not an import at all.

## What closing it needs

1. Import the three names in `core/__init__.py`.
2. A guard: every entry in `core.__all__` resolves. One line of `hasattr`, and it is the check
   whose absence let this sit — `__all__` is 159 entries maintained by hand.

Worth proving red first by removing an import, per `AGENTS.md`: the guard is trivial enough to be
wrong in the direction of inspecting nothing.

## Not urgent, and not nothing

Nothing in the tree does `from core import *`, so no test catches it and no consumer has hit it.
The first one to follow R34 for these three shapes will.

title: feat(wearables): derive provider-level capability catalog from active data sources
body:
## 대목표

HealthMes는 사용자가 실제로 연결하고 보유한 웨어러블 provider와 data source에 대해서만 해당 provider-specific wearable capability를 Decision Agent에 제공해야 한다. Open Wearables 전체 source가 ON이라는 이유만으로 WHOOP만 연결된 사용자에게 Garmin/Polar 전용 capability를 노출해서는 안 된다.

현재 PR #199 / Issue #196은 Open Wearables source-level `disabled`, `unconfigured`, `disconnected`, `available`, `degraded`, `unavailable` 상태와 전체 wearable capability catalog 차단을 구현한다. 이 이슈는 그 다음 단계인 provider/data-source 단위 capability catalog를 다룬다.

## 현재 문제

현재 availability resolver는 Open Wearables의 active connection 또는 data source가 하나라도 존재하는지 확인해 Open Wearables 전체를 usable로 판단한다. 따라서 다음을 구분하지 못한다.

```text
WHOOP 연결됨
  -> WHOOP recovery/health-score capability만 사용 가능해야 함
  -> Garmin/Polar 전용 workout capability는 숨겨야 함

Garmin 연결됨
  -> Garmin이 실제로 제공하는 metric/workout capability만 사용 가능해야 함

연결은 됐지만 특정 기간에 행이 없음
  -> capability는 ON인 상태로 유지하고 no_data를 반환해야 함
```

`no_data`는 provider가 없다는 뜻이 아니다. 연결/coverage metadata가 없는 상태와 정상적인 빈 기간을 분리해야 한다.

## 목표 구조

```text
통합 Input Settings
  + Open Wearables connections
  + data_sources
  + provider coverage metadata
  + verified metric inventory
          |
          v
Provider-level availability resolver
          |
          v
owner-scoped, session-frozen capability catalog
          |
          +-- provider/capability available -> expose
          `-- absent, revoked, unsupported, unverified -> omit/deny
          |
          v
Hermes -> HealthMes MCP search_wearable(capability=...)
```

## 구현 범위

- Open Wearables `connections`, `data-sources`, `meta/coverage`, user inventory metadata를 provider/data-source별로 정규화한다.
- provider family, connection ID, data-source ID, supported metric family와 capability mapping을 stable canonical identity로 만든다.
- `wearable.health-scores(category=day_strain)`처럼 capability parameter가 특정 provider coverage를 요구하는 경우 provider-level availability를 평가한다.
- provider-specific workout, timeseries, sleep/session capability에 대해 실제 source coverage가 확인된 경우에만 session catalog에 포함한다.
- session 시작 시 provider-level catalog와 source-policy revision을 freeze하고, 각 tool call 전후 및 snapshot commit 전에 provider/data-source binding을 다시 검증한다.
- provider가 사라지거나 연결이 revoke되면 stale result/source_refs를 폐기한다.
- 연결된 provider에 해당 기간의 행이 없으면 capability를 끄지 않고 명시적인 `no_data`/coverage limitation을 반환한다.
- source-level `source_enabled`, domain-level `decision_access_enabled`, retention, ETag/If-Match 설정 계약을 그대로 유지한다.
- 기존 WHOOP recovery/day-strain cycle linkage, vendor semantics, provenance와 Open Wearables route-to-capability manifest를 보존한다.

## 책임 경계

- LLM은 필요한 domain/capability를 의미적으로 선택한다.
- HealthMes MCP는 하나의 `search_wearable` surface만 노출한다.
- Provider는 provider-specific endpoint/row/filter/pagination/dedup/source_refs를 결정론적으로 처리한다.
- Provider availability resolver는 capability를 실제로 제공할 수 있는지 판정한다.
- LLM에는 Open Wearables REST URL, raw SQL, credentials, arbitrary provider route를 노출하지 않는다.

## 완료 조건

- WHOOP만 연결된 fixture에서 Garmin/Polar-only capability가 catalog에 나타나지 않고 직접 호출도 upstream 접근 전에 거부된다.
- Garmin과 WHOOP이 함께 연결된 fixture에서 각 provider의 실제 coverage에 맞는 capability만 노출된다.
- provider 연결 revoke, data-source 삭제, source OFF와 OFF->ON revision race가 stale payload/source_refs를 저장하거나 fallback하지 않는다.
- 연결됐지만 요청 기간에 데이터가 없는 경우 capability는 유지되고 `no_data`와 coverage/freshness 정보가 반환된다.
- 서로 다른 provider의 동일 metric은 source/provider identity와 provenance를 보존하며 중복 합산하지 않는다.
- 동일 capability의 서로 다른 기간/필터 조회는 허용되고, 완전히 같은 effective query만 duplicate로 거부된다.
- focused tests만 실행하며 전체 CI/CD는 이 이슈 범위에서 요구하지 않는다.

## 의도적으로 하지 않는 것

- Open Wearables MCP를 Hermes에 직접 추가하지 않는다.
- 모든 provider 운영/auth/sync route를 Wellness capability로 만들지 않는다.
- provider가 없는 것을 LLM 추론으로 판정하지 않는다.
- 단순히 특정 기간에 행이 없다는 이유로 provider를 자동 OFF하지 않는다.

## 연결

- 기존 source-level capability 구현: #196 / PR #199
- 통합 Settings Hub 및 원클릭 연결/동기화 UX: #197
- 미래 선택적 retrieval subagent: #193
- 단일 HealthMes wellness runtime: #138 / #163 / #169
