title: [P3] Parallelize crash triage fan-out (agent.run, research minimize/reproduce/analyze stages)
body:
## Problem

Post-fuzz triage processes crashes strictly sequentially, and each crash's pipeline includes delta-debugging minimization, which can cost hundreds of target executions:

- `Agent.run()`: reproduce → minimize → analyze per crash id (`src/ios_research/agent.py:71-82`)
- Research stages: `_stage_minimize` / `_stage_reproduce` / `_stage_analyze` loops (`src/ios_research/research.py:238-269`)
- `Analyzer.analyze_batch()` is a plain list comprehension over serial `analyze()` calls (`src/ios_research/analysis.py:205-206`)

Crashes are independent of each other; against subprocess targets (real mac harnesses) each execution releases the GIL, so a thread pool converts this fan-out into wall-clock savings roughly proportional to worker count. With several unique crashes this is often the dominant cost of `agent run`.

## Proposed fix

Small helper (e.g., `ios_research.parallel.map_ordered(fn, items, workers)`) wrapping `ThreadPoolExecutor.map`, used by:
- `Agent.run()` triage loop,
- research minimize/reproduce stages,
- `analyze_batch()` (pure CPU but trivially safe).

Results collected in submission order so summaries/ids keep deterministic ordering. Workers default from limits (`max_workers`), capped like `tools/mac_campaign/run.py:191-195` (~half CPUs, max ~6) since ASan processes contend on memory/scheduler.

Note: `Triage` currently instantiates fresh targets/stores per call and writes distinct record paths, so there is no shared mutable state to guard; confirm with a concurrency smoke test on mock targets.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Ordered-output equivalence vs. serial path on multi-crash fixtures.
- [ ] `workers=1` path unchanged (and exercised in default tests).
- [ ] Wall-clock improvement demonstrated with ≥4 unique crashes on a real target (or mocked-slow target).

title: feat(mcp): implement real rule synchronization in sast_sync_rules MCP tool handler
body:
## Problem Description
The MCP tool `sast_sync_rules` provided in `src/mcp/tools.py` (`handle_sast_sync_rules`) is currently a no-op stub that returns a static mock response dictionary without interacting with `scripts/md_to_json.py` or rebuilding `sast_rules.json`. When AI coding agents call this tool after editing or adding new markdown rules in `rules/`, the rule compiler is never executed.

## Technical Root Cause & Code References
In `src/mcp/tools.py` (lines 211-218):
```python
def handle_sast_sync_rules(arguments: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    # Mock stub returning hardcoded payload
    return {
        "status": "success",
        "synced_count": 42,
        "message": "Rules synchronized successfully",
    }
```

## Reproduction Steps / Empirical Evidence
1. Add a new test rule markdown file to `rules/`.
2. Invoke MCP tool `sast_sync_rules`.
3. Check `rules/sast_rules.json` -> The new rule is not compiled or present in the JSON bundle.

## Proposed Remediation Strategy
1. Implement genuine synchronization logic in `handle_sast_sync_rules`:
   - Import and call `scripts.md_to_json.sync_rules()` or `AuditService.sync_rules()`.
   - Re-parse markdown files and write updated JSON to `rules/sast_rules.json`.
   - Return actual counts of synchronized rules.
2. Add a unit test in `tests/test_mcp_tools.py` verifying that invoking `sast_sync_rules` updates `sast_rules.json`.

## Environment & Impact
- **Severity**: P3 - Low
- **Affected Subsystem**: MCP Tool Handlers (`src/mcp/tools.py`)
- **Impact**: Enables AI agents to dynamically sync and reload SAST rules via MCP.

title: Community Workshop — view / share / download lighting presets
body:
## Community Workshop — view / share / download lighting presets

A new **Community Workshop** area for GridGlow where users can browse, share, and download community lighting presets for their games. Design/mockup work is done; this issue tracks it through to a wired implementation.

**Mockup:** `docs/mockups/workshop-community.html` (self-contained — open directly in a browser). Built in the app's real look & feel: 48px icon rail (new Workshop globe-share icon), navy glass + purple palette, Inter type.

---

### What's in the mockup

**Discover / browse**
- Header with search + **Upload Preset**, tabs (Discover / My Uploads / My Downloads / Liked).
- Master list of preset cards + a detail panel (hero, stats, description, share link).
- Each card shows a **curved rev-gauge LED arc** that renders the preset's colour range (replaces the earlier waveform look).
- **Live preview** in the detail panel: a user-started (Play/Pause, off by default) LED loop — F1 start lights → engine (throttle → shift flash → coast) → fastest-lap purple flash (all zones/bulbs in unison) → track-status flags → loop.

**Sort & filter** (functional in the mockup)
- Games / Devices / Sort (Popular · Most liked · Highest rated · Newest · Name A–Z) / Time (week/month/year) + Reset.
- Reorders/filters cards by their `data-*` attributes; empty state + pager hide when nothing matches.

**Upload Preset modal**
- Name, description, game, visibility (Public/Unlisted), supported-device chips, tags, and a live LED-arc preview of the colours pulled from the user's current setup.

**Download → Apply flow**
- Download button animates real progress (fill bar + live %, → "Downloaded ✓"), then hands off to the Apply step.
- **Apply / map-to-your-lights modal**: maps the preset's effect roles onto the user's own lights.

**Compatibility handling** (see design decision below)
- Detail panel shows a capability-based compatibility badge (🟢 full / 🟡 partial).
- "Supported Devices" reframed as **Recommended Devices** with owned/missing states.

**Micro-interactions:** modal fade + rise/settle entrance; like button plays a heart → checkered-flag → heart flourish (smoothed bounce, subtle clockwise rotation). All respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.

---

### Key design decisions

- **A preset is a device-AGNOSTIC theme** (the `gui_settings` — colours, curves, brightness range, enabled events, `rpm_gradient`, start-light direction, idle state), **not** a list of the author's devices. Presets never carry the author's physical bindings (`light_assignments`, which map to a user's own device labels).
- **Match on capability, not device count or brand.** Downloading a preset made with 6 devices onto a 4-device setup is a non-issue — the theme applies regardless; the user maps their lights to effect roles on apply, and unused roles are fine.
- **Multizone is the one real capability gate.** Multizone-only effects (RPM rev meter, zone start-lights — cf. the `_rpm_strips()` "needs a multizone strip" guard in `bridge_core.py`) can't render without a strip, so they offer a single-bulb fallback or can be skipped. Brand (LIFX/Nanoleaf/Hue) mostly doesn't matter (all RGB); the caveat is refresh-sensitive strobes on Hue.

---

### Dev / wiring notes (front end built to be swap-in ready)

- **Dynamic preview colours (hard requirement):** every colour in the live preview and the card arcs must be driven by the *selected preset's* config, not hard-coded. A ⚠ DEV NOTE at the top of the preview `<script>` lists which effects need wiring (rev ramp, start lights, shift, fastest lap, flags). Card arcs share one reusable `renderArc(el, cols)`.
- **Upload payload shape** (documented in a DEV comment): `{ name, description, game, visibility, devices[], tags[], colors[] }`, with `colors[]` from the user's active setup.
- **Apply/effect shape:** each effect declares `{ requires: 'multizone' | 'any', fallback }`; the role list comes from the preset's effects.
- **Sort/filter** mirrors intended server params (`?sort=&game=&device=&range=`) — currently reorders DOM nodes by `data-*`; swaps to an API call cleanly.
- **Data source of truth (TODO):** cards are still partly hand-written HTML. Collapse to a single `PRESETS[]` array driving cards/arcs/detail/preview so wiring = replace the array with a `fetch`.
- **Fonts:** mockup loads Inter from Google Fonts; **bundle Inter locally** in the real app.

---

### Planned / not built yet

- **Match colours per light** : instead of role-based mapping, let the user assign each of their lights to a specific colour from the preset (e.g. preset Light 2 = red, Light 3 = pink, Light 4 = yellow). A "Planned" placeholder card sits in the Apply modal.
- **Real game art:** card thumbnails + detail hero currently use logo-safe gradient placeholders; real game logos/cover art to be swapped in.

### Open questions

- **Nav placement / IA:** the icon rail is getting crowded — Workshop as a 6th top-level rail icon, or a tab inside the Profiles page?
- Compatibility badge copy/thresholds.

### Related

- **Backend design doc** (design-only, no code yet): `docs/community-workshop-backend.md` on branch `community-workshop-backend-ca111f` — D1 schema, API contract, front-end wiring seam table. Storage: Cloudflare D1; auth deferred (anonymous `X-GG-Token`, GitHub OAuth later).

title: pieplot 갤러리에 누적 비율 툴팁을 넣는다
body:
조각이 이미 비율을 보여주는데 **누적 비율**은 그림 안에 있으면서 어디에도 적혀 있지 않다.

## 선행

- #190 — 페이지별 CSS 통로와 조작 장치 방출기
- #191 — 툴팁 헬퍼
- #192 — 플롯 안 라벨 훅

## 하는 일

- `tooltip=True` 가 각 조각에 `<title>` 을 붙인다. 내용은 이름·값·비율, 그리고 그 조각까지의 **누적 비율**.
- 조각 옆 값 라벨에 `pointer-events: none` 을 준다 (#192 가 붙인 훅을 쓴다). 안 그러면 라벨 위에서 조각 툴팁이 안 뜬다.
- `info=` 가 툴팁을 채우는 예시. `scatterplot` 과 같은 기제다.
- **토글은 넣지 않는다.** 조각 하나가 행 하나라 토글은 범례가 아니라 데이터 편집이 된다. 이 판단을 NOTES 에 적는다.

## 갤러리가 아직 못 보여주는 것

그림이 담고 있지만 결코 적지 않는 누적 비율.

## 규칙 R1 — 예시 1의 렌더 바이트를 바꾸지 않는다

`docs/gallery/index.html` 이 각 페이지의 `examples[0].svg` 만 인라인한다. 새 기능은 **예시 2 이후**에서 시연한다. 그러면 이 이슈는 `index.html` 을 건드리지 않는다.

## 새 가드 — 각각 빨간불을 본 뒤에 넣는다

| 가드 | 무엇으로 빨갛게 만드는가 |
|---|---|
| `tooltip=True` 가 모든 마크에 `<title>` 을 정확히 하나씩 붙인다 | 하나 빠뜨리기 |
| `tooltip=False` 출력이 오늘과 바이트 동일 | 기본값 뒤집기 |

## 검증

- `tooltip=True` 가 모든 마크에 `<title>` 하나씩. `tooltip=False` 는 오늘과 바이트 동일.
- docstring 에 `tooltip` 이 단어로 나온다 (#187 의 게이트).
- `mise run check` green.
- 마지막 커밋은 `uv run python -m gallery.build` 다.
- Pages 배포 후 해당 페이지 200, `index.html` 무변경.

title: feat(blake2s): the 32-bit RFC 7693 sibling, host and device rows
body:
### Pre-submission checklist

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and this is not a duplicate.

### Context / problem

BLAKE2s (RFC 7693) is BLAKE2b's 32-bit sibling and the remaining half of the BLAKE2 standard: uint32 words, 10 rounds, 64-byte blocks, rotations (16, 12, 8, 7), SHA-256's IV, 1..32-byte output. Production surface: WireGuard (Noise IK uses BLAKE2s throughout), embedded/constrained stacks that pick the 32-bit member. `hashlib.blake2s` makes the host row free, and the device core is SIMPLER than blake2b's — native uint32, no half pairs.

### Proposed solution

Mirror the blake2b arrangement (#161) at the 32-bit parameters:

- Host `HostBlake2s` over `hashlib.blake2s` via the shared `host_digest` loop; digest_size (1..32) on the value surface.
- Device `Blake2s` behind marker `hash_frx.digest.blake2s`, always-emit digest posture (pre-emitter flags, GENERIC today); HAIFA counter/finalization flags as the blake2b device row lays them out; unkeyed first (keyed/salt/tree are follow-ups, same as #161).
- Package placement: alongside the existing `hash_frx/blake2b/` (its issue noted "consider `blake2/` if 2s follows" — decide with the tree's grain and record the choice).

### Alternatives considered

- Host row only (the original blake2b posture). Rejected now: the device-row recipe is established and the point of this sweep is device coverage of the general-purpose standards.

### Why this approach

The RFC's own test vectors + hashlib differentials make anchoring trivial; the device core reuses the G-function shape the blake2b device row establishes, at plain uint32.

### Plan

Single PR: ① host row + RFC vectors ② device core + marker + tests ③ registry/matrix/docs rows. (Order may collapse ① into ② since hashlib host rows are one class.)

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] RFC 7693 vectors + hashlib differential across block/padding boundaries, batched, both rows
- [ ] Marker emission + ABI pin; jit-zone single-trace pin; seam pins (GENERIC device / HOST host)
- [ ] CPU and GPU legs green

### References

- RFC 7693; blake2.net test vectors
- #161 (the blake2b arrangement this mirrors)

### Area

none / unsure

### Parent issue

#157

### Milestone

_No response_

### Relevant knowledge

_No response_

title: Collections: named saved filters over existing tags/status/score
body:
## Summary

Build "collections" as named, saved filter combinations over the library view's
existing tag/status/score filters — no new organizing primitive, no new
per-anime relationship. A collection is a shortcut to a filter state, not a place
an anime is manually added.

## Context

#165 (decided 2026-08-20) ruled out the standalone-primitive direction: tags +
bulk-tag-apply (#15) already let a user label anime freely, and the actual gap
identified was a missing "save this filter combination and give it a name" UI
feature, not a data-model gap. This keeps the personal-layer data model
unchanged — a collection is purely a saved *view* over `personal_notes.tags` +
`library_entries.status`/`score` filters that already exist in the library view.

## Scope

- New small per-user table (additive migration): saved collection = name +
  serialized filter criteria (tags, status, score range — whatever the library
  view's existing filter controls already support).
- UI to save the library view's *current* active filter state as a named
  collection (e.g. a "Save as collection" action near the existing filter row).
- UI to browse/apply saved collections — a dropdown or small nav element on the
  library page that, when selected, applies that collection's saved filters.
- Collections can be renamed/deleted from wherever they're managed (library page
  itself, or Settings — implementer's call).

## Out of scope

- No new per-anime relationship/table beyond the saved-filter-criteria table
  itself — an anime is never "added to" a collection directly, only ever
  filtered into view by one.
- No sharing/exporting collections between users — personal-layer only, same
  boundary as tags and notes today.
- Any change to the existing tag/bulk-tag-apply mechanism itself.
- Any change to the manual watch-next queue priority ordering — a separate
  concept, not touched here.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] User can save the library view's current filter combination as a named
      collection.
- [ ] User can apply a saved collection to instantly re-filter the library view
      to that saved state.
- [ ] User can rename/delete a saved collection.
- [ ] No new per-anime data — collections store filter criteria only.
- [ ] Verified live at desktop and mobile widths.

## Open questions / notes

- Exact UI placement for browsing/managing saved collections (library page vs.
  Settings) is an implementation-time call.

title: feat(backend): 今日罐内容源策略（Issue #192 子任务 2）
body:
隶属 #192「首页内容化改版（罐头沉浸流 + 自定义 TabBar）」的**子任务 2（今日罐后端）**。

Relates to #174
Relates to #192

## 背景

首页改版后顶部设有「今日罐」tab：每天向用户呈现一个精选罐头，作为沉浸流的内容入口之一。当前后端缺少「当日罐头」的专用内容源策略，前端无法获得稳定的每日内容。

## v1 前端临时策略（过渡方案）

在后端正式接口落地前，前端先用既有数据做确定性轮转，避免阻塞首页联调：

- 复用 `/discovery/` 返回的 `hot_cans` 作为候选池；
- 以「当日日期序」（如按日期对候选池长度取模）确定性地选取当日罐头，保证同一天内所有用户看到同一罐、且刷新后稳定；
- 叠加「本地当日缓存」：当天首次选定后缓存到本地，跨启动/下拉刷新不变，次日失效重算。

该临时方案仅为兜底，不承载运营意图，候选池质量与轮转公平性都不保证。

## 期望的正式接口形态（建议）

- 形如 `GET /cans/today/`，返回**单个**当日罐头（结构与沉浸流卡片一致，可直接复用现有铭牌预览与投票字段）；
- 当日选取策略由后端决定：可为「运营可配置置顶」优先，无配置时回退到确定性策略（如按日期轮转精选池、或按质量分/热度加权）；
- 同一自然日内结果稳定（对同一时区/日期语义一致），跨日更新；
- 游客态可见（不要求登录）。

具体字段与选取算法可在实现时进一步评审，以上仅为形态建议。

## 验收要点

- [ ] 每日内容不同：连续两日返回的罐头不重复（或在候选池耗尽前有明确的轮转/回退语义）。
- [ ] 游客可见：未登录访问返回 200 且内容完整，含铭牌预览所需字段。
- [ ] 与首页 tab 对接：返回结构可被首页「今日罐」tab 直接消费，无需前端二次拼装。
- [ ] 当日稳定性：同一天内多次请求返回同一罐头。

title: enhancement: Per-application audio volume mixer
body:
## Idea

Extend CoAgent's audio control with per-application volume mixing:

- **`GET /system/audio/sessions`** — list all active audio sessions (app name, PID, volume, mute state, peak meter)
- **`POST /system/audio/session/volume`** — set volume for a specific app by name or PID
- **`POST /system/audio/session/mute`** — mute/unmute a specific app
- **`POST /system/audio/session/focus`** — switch default device routing to a specific app

**Implementation:** Uses `pycaw` (Python Core Audio Windows bindings) which wraps the Windows `IAudioSessionManager2` COM API. Pure Python, no external executables needed.

**Why:** Windows 11's audio mixer shows per-app volumes — users expect this level of control. Current `/system/volume` only controls the master volume. An AI agent that can independently control music, browser, and system alert volumes is dramatically more useful for desktop automation (e.g., "mute Chrome but keep Spotify at 40%"). This is a natural extension of the existing system control routes.

**Inspiration:** EarTrumpet (8.7k★ on GitHub) — popular Windows volume mixer; SoundSwitch for per-app audio routing. pycaw is a mature library with 800+ GitHub stars.

**Difficulty:** medium — requires `pycaw` dependency (pure Python COM wrapper), ~200 lines
**Category:** system

title: The eval sweep grades STRIDE only: 63 ASVS references sit unread
body:
## What is true today

The corpus carries ASVS references and nothing scores them.

- `evals/corpus/*/claims/asvs.json` exists in 7 of the 13 cases and holds **63 references**. Every one of ASVS's 17 lanes has at least one.
- `evals/harness/reference.py:165` registers `ReferenceRequirement` for `asvs`. **No other module reads that type.**
- `evals/harness/run.py:116` — `stride_block()` picks the STRIDE block off the report and raises if it is absent. Its docstring says so: "this harness grades STRIDE's open claim set".
- `evals/harness/scorer.py` computes a severity confusion matrix and nothing else. There is no applicability confusion matrix anywhere in `evals/`.

So `evals/verify_corpus.py` checks that the ASVS references are well formed, and the sweep then never reads them. A framework a deployment may select is measured by nothing.

## What #167 already specifies

The design is settled, so this is implementation rather than a question.

- **The match rule is mechanical.** ASVS matches by requirement ID, with no judge and no lane prefilter. A STRIDE claim is free prose; an ASVS claim is a requirement ID. The rule is the harness's data, keyed off the closed framework `Literal`.
- **The reference set is closed.** The file lists the exceptions with a reason — the requirements this case does not apply — and the scorer derives the complement from the package catalog at the case's level.
- **The artifact is an applicability confusion matrix** over that requirement list, as its own artifact key. `scores`, `critic_yield`, `grounds`, `coverage`, `structural_failures`, `exemplar_delta` and `unlisted_for_promotion` each gain a `framework` key on the row.
- **The STRIDE-only artifacts stay STRIDE's**: severity calibration, the judge and its agreement bar. `stability` already keys on `(case, framework, reference index)`.

## Why this matters now

One `strong` fingerprint covers both frameworks, so an ASVS run certifies today on a tier nobody graded. Certification is a claim about a deployment's blessed list, never a claim about quality, and this is the gap where the two read alike.

Found while auditing what remains on #139. Part of the route #158 charted.

title: fixtures: score and promote #94 allergy-reaction ruling cohort
body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Give the #94 allergy-reaction ruling cohort its first valid score and promote it automatically.

**Current behavior:**
The ruling cohort contains day-b R6. It is a promotable REPORTED assertion counted only because no output produced under the #94 rule has been scored against it. Its historical row and the last complete day-b run must remain truthful.

**Desired behavior:**
Generate current output for every encounter named by R6 and grade it independently against the assertion. A pass or a failure is a valid score. Once that score exists, preserve R6 as a historical promoted assertion and append its live equivalent to the appropriate binary class. Do not change the clinical-note behavior merely to make the output pass.

**Key interfaces:**
- Ruling cohort — #94's cohort consists only of day-b R6
- Valid score — output must have been produced while the #94 rule was in force; generation and grading remain separate
- Promoted assertion — the historical R6 identity and verdict remain, and the new enforced row receives a new binary identity
- Targeted scoring — every encounter named by R6 is required; unrelated day-b encounters are not

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Current output is generated for all encounters named by day-b R6 and graded by a separate pass
- [ ] R6 receives an explicit PASS or FAIL with the skill commit and scoring date recorded
- [ ] The targeted verdict does not alter day-b's last complete-run fraction
- [ ] R6 remains as a historical row marked with its binary successor
- [ ] The successor is appended to the appropriate binary class and carries R6's valid verdict as its first score
- [ ] No clinical-note behavior is changed to force a passing verdict
- [ ] Fixture documentation and cross-links describe #94 as its own closed ruling cohort after promotion

**Out of scope:**
- Rerunning unrelated day-b encounters
- Promoting #29's or #96's ruling cohorts
- Correcting clinical-note behavior if the targeted output fails

title: [권한 5c] 벡터 스토어 raw export/import 계약 — 재임베딩 없는 팩 단위 벡터 복제
body:
## 배경 (#148 분해, 사용자 승인)

pack_fork(#148 후속 5d)는 원본 팩의 벡터를 새 팩으로 복제해야 하는데, 현재 어떤 벡터 스토어에도 저장된 원시 임베딩을 되읽는 공개 메서드가 없다(get_by_id 는 id/document/metadata 만, query 는 distance 만).

## 실측 판정 (스크래치 DB, #148 설계 단계에서 완료)
- vec0(sqlite-vec 0.1.9): `INSERT ... SELECT` 는 float-only 테이블에서는 동작하지만 **`embedding_bit` 컬럼 보유 테이블(ann=binary)에서 결정적으로 실패** — SQL 레벨 복제는 채택 불가.
- 원시 임베딩 read 헬퍼 방식은 두 형상 모두에서 바이트 동일 복제 + 새 파티션 KNN 정상.
- vec0 파티션 키 UPDATE 불가(재확인).

## 범위
- 3백엔드(sqlite-vec / pgvector / chroma)에 `export_pack_vectors` / `import_vectors` 류의 raw 계약을 정의·구현한다.
- pgvector 는 실컬럼이라 자명, chroma 는 get(include=["embeddings"]) 경로 실측 필요.
- 백엔드별 정체성 제약(vec0 node_id 전역 유일 등)을 계약 문서에 명시한다 — #197(pack-qualified identity)과 정합.
- #182(non-local backfill)와 설계를 공유한다.

## 의존
없음 — #148(5a)과 파일이 겹치지 않아 병렬 진행 가능.

title: `ctx.http.fetch(hostId, …)` + `ctx.hosts.list()` with verified broker identity
body:
## Problem

Mods doing authenticated HTTP use the raw hoisted `hostFetch`, which has two footguns the mods themselves document: a null host silently targets the same origin, and its deadline stops at headers so a stalled body hangs forever. There is also no stable host identity — update invented `hostFingerprint = host URL`, which breaks the moment one broker is reachable under a second URL (audit G5). The wrapped-RPC idiom that fixes this already exists twice in ctx; HTTP just never got it.

## Evidence

- update raw-`hostFetch`es 5 routes — `mods/update/update.js:610`, `:987`, `:1336`, `:1813`, `:1872`.
- recorder likewise — `mods/recorder/recorder.js:154`, `:238`, `:1539` — and its own header comment documents the `hostFetch(null, …)` silently-same-origin footgun (:105-111).
- mod-sync hand-rolls an AbortController because `hostFetch`'s deadline stops at headers — `mods/mod-sync/mod-sync.js:485-495`.
- update's `hostFingerprint` is just the host URL — `mods/update/update.js:925-928`.
- The house idiom already exists: `ctx.file` never rejects and an unknown host fails closed (86:235-387); `ctx.session` returns `{status, json}` (86:462-514).

## Proposed change

```js
const res = await ctx.http.fetch(hostId, path, {
  method: 'GET',        // default
  json,                 // request body; sets content-type
  timeoutMs,            // TOTAL deadline — includes reading the body, not headers-only
  signal,               // optional; composes with #198's ctx.signal
});
// → {status, json?|text?, error?}   NEVER rejects.
// status is ALWAYS present: the HTTP status, or 0 with error set for transport/timeout.

ctx.hosts.list();
// → [{id, label, url, brokerId, self: bool}]   read-only snapshot
// brokerId: #64's broker_id once the host has answered /info; null until then
```

- **`hostId` is required.** `null`/`undefined` throws **synchronously** — the same-origin default dies. Targeting the origin broker is spelled out: pass the id of the `self: true` entry from `ctx.hosts.list()`.
- Unknown `hostId` fails closed, no request issued — same contract as `ctx.file`.
- **Identity is two fields, and no single "fingerprint" pretends to be both.** `id` is the local registry handle — stable for this browser's list, meaningless anywhere else. `brokerId` is cross-URL identity: `broker_id` from `/info` (#64 established it), and **`null` until the host has answered** — no provisional URL hash, no silent substitution when verification lands. Same broker under two URLs → same `brokerId`; that is the property update's URL-as-fingerprint lacks.
- **A URL repoint RESETS `brokerId` to null** until the new endpoint re-answers `/info`. It is never carried over — carrying it would label a new (possibly hostile) endpoint with the old broker's verified identity. Callers branching on identity must handle `null` (unverified) explicitly rather than falling back to the URL.

Files: `86c_js_mod_ctx_ext.js` (or 86d — see traps), `wiki/Writing-a-Mod.md`, help-corpus regen.

## Traps & constraints

- Sequencing: C-wave, after the B-wave (#204); `signal` composition assumes #198 landed.
- Fragment cap: 86 is at 2490/2500 (ui.py:62); land in 86c, and if 86c is near the cap add `86d` to `_ORDERED` (ui.py:98-187; precedent 86a :173, 86b :177). `ctxVersion` stays 1; feature-detect with `ctx.http && typeof ctx.http.fetch === 'function'`.
- **Total timeout means the body read is inside the deadline.** A stalled body must abort at ~`timeoutMs`. Getting this wrong reproduces, behind the API, the exact bug mod-sync hand-rolled around.
- 401 and empty must stay distinguishable — `ctx.serverStore.get` once dropped the status and they weren't (the #174 fix). `status` is always populated; `error` never substitutes for an HTTP-level status.
- New routes are invisible to old peers: the preflight OPTIONS 404s and surfaces as an opaque network error (#157). That must come back as a branchable `{status: 0, error}` — cross-broker callers feature-detect, they never assume the peer has the route.
- No auth side effects: a 401 returns as a 401. `ctx.http` must never force-pop the host auth prompt — background repaints calling `promptFileHostAuth` was the #161 bug class. Auth recovery belongs to the mod (and later to #195's `host:auth`).
- `id` and `brokerId` are for change detection and cache keys — **neither is ever** a merge key for registry entries (the #174 identity-bridging lesson: an incoming entry id was a live host-repoint vector).
- Broker runs on Windows AND Linux; nothing here may reason from one platform.
- Fragment edits serve only after a broker restart (`INDEX_HTML` cached at import).

## Migration impact

- **recorder** (slice of med-high; **the reference migration — ships WITH this issue**): its 3 raw routes move to `ctx.http`; the :105-111 footgun comment is deleted along with the footgun. The API does not freeze against fixtures alone — recorder is the production proof.
- **update** (high overall; this is its S4 slice): 5 raw routes → `ctx.http`; `hostFingerprint` (the raw URL) → `brokerId`-or-null from `ctx.hosts.list()` — its change detection must treat `null` as "unverified", not as a distinct identity. `update.js` sits at 2496/2500 — budget a relocation/split *before* touching it.
- **mod-sync** (slice of high): the hand-rolled AbortController dies; total timeout is native.
- Everything else unaffected; `hostFetch` remains for core. The remaining migrations (update, mod-sync) ship under #204.

## Verification

- Playwright: `ctx.http.fetch(null, '/info')` throws synchronously; an unknown host id resolves `{status: 0, error}` with **zero** network requests (assert via the network log); `timeoutMs` against a stalled-body route resolves with a timeout error at roughly the deadline, not at headers-plus-forever.
- Playwright: repoint a host entry to a second URL of the same broker → `ctx.hosts.list()` shows `brokerId: null` immediately after the repoint, then the same `broker_id` once `/info` answers; the entry's `id` never changed; exactly one entry has `self: true`.
- The reference migration lands in the same PR: recorder's 3 routes run through `ctx.http` (no raw `hostFetch(` left in `recorder.js`), and a cross-broker record/save round-trip still works.
- `python -m pytest tests/test_ui_assets.py::test_no_multi_thousand_line_fragment`.
- `python webterm/broker/help_corpus.py` regen + drift test; `wiki/Writing-a-Mod.md` (:83/:162/:338/:343 region) updated.

## Out of scope

- Route-scoped families (`ctx.update.*` mirroring `ctx.session`) so update's RPC surface stays enumerable — a plausible follow-up, not here.
- Changing `hostFetch` itself; core keeps it.
- Retry/backoff policy — mods own theirs.
- Server-side egress gating and CSP — that is the A-wave.
- ESM (G12), deferred.

title: arch: split the history-repo layout out of store.py
body:
> Part of #203, which has the argument for these four and the order to do them in.

`woswoar/store.py` (951 lines) carries three vocabularies under one name:

1. **paths under `logs/`** — `logs_dir`, `host_dir`, `log_file`, `iter_log_files`,
   `name_file`, `day_for`. What `cache` and `search` need.
2. **paths under `history/`** — `chunk_dir`, `new_chunk`, `chunk_names`,
   `chunk_days`, `day_stamp`, `iter_chunks`, `day_key`, `day_key_public`,
   `day_key_days`, `day_manifest`, `signer_public`, `name_seal`, `is_chunk_path`,
   `repo_hosts`, `repo_format`, `format_file` — roughly `store.py:545-909`.
   Read only by `sync` and `prove`.
3. **filesystem primitives** — `write_atomic`, `private_dir`, `private_append`,
   `read_tail`, `harden`, `readable_by_others`, `load_json`, `save_json`.

## The consequence

`store` is imported by six of the nine modules, so everything that wants
`logs_dir()` transitively depends on the chunk layout, the manifest path scheme
and the repo format marker. Measured with `tests/test_architecture.py`'s helper:
`cache` and `search` pull in `store` and therefore all of (2), which neither has
any business knowing.

That coupling is what makes the sync split (#201) bigger than it needs to be:
moving a chunk-path decision today means editing a module that `search` imports.

## Suggested fix

Move (2) into `woswoar/repo.py`, leaving `store` as "logs plus filesystem
primitives". Pure move, no logic change. `repo` imports `store` for
`write_atomic` and `private_dir`; `sync` and `prove` import both.

Then update the `LAYERS` table in `tests/test_architecture.py` — that edit is the
review, and it should show `cache` and `search` losing an edge rather than
gaining one.

## The constraint that makes the obvious fix wrong

**`_private_paths` spans both halves and must keep doing so.**
`store._private_paths` (`store.py:280`) walks the data directory for `harden` and
`readable_by_others`, and it *prunes* `history/` by name — with a measurement
attached: 238 ms filtering against 1.4 ms pruning on a two-year tree. So the
permission walk needs to know the history directory exists even though it
deliberately does not descend into it. Splitting naively either loses the prune
(and `doctor` gets 200× slower on a real archive) or creates a `store` → `repo`
edge, which is the cycle the split is meant to avoid. The narrow answer is that
`history_dir()` stays in `store` — it is the boundary, not the contents.

**`day_for` is shared and must not be duplicated.** It defines the day bucket
that the shell hook, the log files and the chunk directories all agree on, and
`sync.compact` reaches for it explicitly rather than spelling "today" a second
time (`sync.py:3087`). It belongs in `store`, with `repo` calling it.

Context: `docs/architecture.md`, "Where the shape is under strain".

title: literary-translator: no cross-volume canon reconciliation for a multi-volume series — the same name freezes to different target forms across books (Тамбонно/Тамбоно)
body:
## Summary

For a **multi-volume work translated as separate projects** (same author, same
recurring names — e.g. Tallemant's *Historiettes* Tome 3 and Tome 5), each book has
its own independent `canon.json` and there is no mechanism to share or reconcile a
canon across volumes. A name that recurs in both volumes can (and does) freeze to a
**different** target form in each — with nothing in either project able to notice,
because every consistency check is scoped to one canon.

## Concrete instance

The surname **Tambonneau** freezes three different ways:
- Tome 3 canon: **`Тамбонно`** (`is_proper_name:true`, established/transliterated).
- Tome 5 canon: **`Тамбоно`** (single н) — used 22× in the delivered text, including
  the chapter heading the reader sees first.
- The canonical published Russian translation (Engelke, *Занимательные истории*, ЛП
  1974) uses a third form, **`Танбонно`**.

Practical-transcription of `-nn-` between vowels gives `-нн-` (→ `Тамбонно`), so Tome 5
is also the less defensible spelling — but the point here is not which is right, it is
that **two volumes of one series disagree and the pipeline cannot see it.**

## Why it happens

`final_audit.py` `warn_glossary_diff` checks `canon.json` self-consistency and
cross-segment drift **within a single project** (final_audit.py:377-438). `CANON_PATH`
is the one project's canon. There is no notion of a parent/shared canon for a series,
no cross-project reconciliation step, and no candidate-extraction inheritance — Tome 5
re-derived its canon from scratch and re-transliterated a name Tome 3 had already
frozen.

## Impact

Lower severity than #P1 — the plugin is book-local by design, and a per-book canon is a
reasonable v1 scope. But series work is a natural use case (the reference project itself
is one volume of a multi-volume set), and cross-volume name divergence is exactly the
kind of defect a reader/reviewer notices immediately ("why is the president spelled two
ways across the set?"). Worth a conscious decision rather than silent divergence.

## Dedup

Not a duplicate. #62 (open) is "second-project pilot run (verify language presets +
experimental adapters)" — about validating the pipeline on a new project, not about
sharing a canon across volumes of one work. No open/closed issue covers cross-volume
canon reconciliation.

## Possible directions (non-prescriptive)

- An optional **shared/parent canon** a series' volumes inherit (read-only), so a name
  frozen in Vol.1 is delivered to Vol.2 rather than re-derived.
- OR a lightweight **cross-project canon-diff** utility an operator can run before
  delivery of a later volume ("these source_forms are frozen to different target forms
  than in <other canon>"), even as advisory output.
- At minimum: document the book-local scope and recommend manually seeding a later
  volume's canon from the earlier one for a series.

title: Keyless start: stay open as a shop window; key-aware greyed lineup, drop '(default)' and the fallback NOTE
body:
Maintainer direction settled 2026-08-16 (dictated design session; this body is the operative spec).

## Problem

Two related findings from a user's-seat review of the engine mechanism:

1. **A fully keyless start never shows the app.** Today the tool launches the settings wizard and exits (#163). A newcomer who wants to see what the tool looks like *before* signing up anywhere is locked out until they fetch an API key — the wrong first impression for the "no lock-in, look first" target user (VISION.md).
2. **The console lineup is key-blind.** Engines without a stored key look identical to usable ones; the shipped default carries a dim `(default)` tag that stopped meaning much once #193/#198 landed; and a missing-key fallback at startup is narrated as an error NOTE ("SONIOX_API_KEY missing -> started on ...") even when a Groq-only setup is deliberate and everything works as intended.

## Spec

**Shop-window mode (keyless start).**
- When no engine is constructible and every failure is a missing key: do NOT exit. Render the normal masthead + cockpit with all four lineup rows dim, plus one extra line under the lineup in yellow, positively worded — suggestion: `To enable dictation, enter an API key in Settings (Ctrl+Alt+G)`. Final wording free, but positive-instructional; never "missing"/"error" phrasing.
- Still auto-launch the settings app in wizard mode exactly as today — the tool simply stays open behind it.
- Recording hotkey / self-test while keyless: a friendly panel repeating the same guidance instead of an attempt. No crash path through an absent transcriber.
- The SETUP-NEEDED panel + `input()` + exit remains only for genuine non-key construction errors (that branch keeps its semantics).

**Key-aware lineup.**
- Lineup rows for engines whose key env var is absent render dim (cockpit lineup, and the SETUP-NEEDED lineup rendering if it survives this change).
- Startup fall-through and Ctrl+Alt+L already skip such engines — keep that, but move the per-skip console lines to file-only: the grey rows now tell the story on screen.

**Remove two console artifacts.**
- The dim `(default)` marker (both render sites in console_ui.py).
- The startup fallback NOTE — deliberately including the configured/remembered-engine-is-keyless case: start silently on the first available engine in lineup order; the greyed row is the signal (maintainer call: a key does not vanish by itself, and the hand-deleted-key case is covered by the grey row alone). A file-log line stays for debugging.

**Unchanged.**
- Startup precedence (respects D-008): configured > remembered > built-in default; a keyless resolved engine falls through in carousel order exactly as today.
- The engine memory (#193) still records only deliberate switches, never fall-through.
- `AVAILABLE_APIS` order stays the single ordering source.
- An *invalid* (as opposed to missing) key changes nothing here: the engine stays active and the error surfaces at transcription time, as today.

## Verification

- `test_console_ui.py` extended: greyed lineup rows, the yellow guidance line (charset/width/red-exclusivity rules apply), `(default)` gone.
- Keyless-mode decision logic kept pure where possible so it tests off-Windows.
- Hands-on (route to the run's `test` issue): fresh checkout without `.env` -> shop window + wizard; add one key, restart, dictation works.

Companions (filed in the same batch, they reference this issue): the settings-side key-awareness, and the Save & Restart mechanism that completes the keyless first-run loop. Relates #40, #109, #163; respects D-008 and D-001.

title: Reconcile recorded adoption bands against the computed signal — and declare the bands first
body:
With PyPI coverage at 100 products (#165), 41 recorded adoption bands disagree with the computed one — 39 after #167 dropped two bad declarations. **They are not one problem, and the direction of the disagreement says which side is wrong.**

There is also a prerequisite that has to land first, described at the bottom: the computed band's thresholds are hardcoded in the UDM.

## The asymmetry

**Recorded *below* computed → the recorded band is wrong.** 17 products. There is no honest reason to band `mcp-python-sdk` at level 3 when the signal reports **328M** monthly downloads. Most are `stars_fallback`, which the rubric caps at 3 — so the human had no number, and one existed:

| product | recorded | computed | downloads/30d | signal_type |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mcp-python-sdk` | 3 | 5 | 328,478,265 | stars_fallback |
| `cohere-rerank-api` | 3 | 5 | 37,933,346 | reported_traction |
| `laminar` | 3 | 5 | 33,882,759 | usage_volume |
| `langfuse` | 3 | 5 | 25,817,410 | reported_traction |
| `docling` | 3 | 5 | 13,825,930 | stars_fallback |
| `markitdown` | 3 | 5 | 12,633,897 | stars_fallback |
| … | | | | |

**Recorded *above* computed → usually fine, but currently unfalsifiable.** 22 products. PyPI is one channel among several: `open-webui` ships mostly via Docker, `verl` and `swift` run from source, `helm` from a clone. The recorded band is probably right — but the judgment is invisible.

## Proposed rule

> A recorded adoption band may **exceed** the computed one only with a declared reason naming the uncounted channel. It may never fall **below** it.

That converts a judgment into a checkable claim, which is exactly what `establishes` did for openness and `relative_to` did for capability. It also produces a work list for free: every named channel is a candidate signal, and "Docker pulls" appearing eight times makes the case for a Docker Hub route better than any argument could.

## Sequencing, so the gate doesn't land on a backlog

`verification.md` is explicit that a big-bang gate fails on day one and gets switched off. So:

1. Fix the 17 under-banded products. Each needs a glance, not a bulk update.
2. Add the named-channel reason to the 22 over-banded ones **during each category's re-read** — the sweep is already opening those files, so this costs nothing extra.
3. Turn the check on once both are done.

## Prerequisite: the bands are hardcoded in the UDM

`currentai.signal_pypi.package_downloads` derives `adoption_level` in SQL:

```sql
WHEN w.downloads_30d > 10000000 THEN 5
WHEN w.downloads_30d > 1000000  THEN 4
WHEN w.downloads_30d > 100000   THEN 3
WHEN w.downloads_30d > 10000    THEN 2
ELSE 1
```

Two problems, and they are the same two the openness scoring SQL already had before it was generalized:

- **The thresholds live in the warehouse and nowhere else.** This is the drift `check_parity` exists to catch, one axis over: repo and warehouse mirroring a rule by hand.
- **It applies one scale to every product type.** The map's convention is that the scale is a property of the *type* — a dataset at 100K downloads is not a software package at 100K, and hardware is qualitative. Only `base_pretrained` declares its bands today; the other fifteen categories follow a convention written down nowhere.

So before a reconciliation gate can mean anything, the bands need to move into `sources/rubrics/` — four declarations, not sixteen — serialize into the registry the way `category_dimensions` did for openness, and the UDM needs to read them instead of hardcoding. Same fix, same shape, already on the backlog as its own item.

Comparing against `adoption_level` before that lands would gate one hardcoded scale against a human convention, which is not a comparison worth having.

## One caveat on the 41

`signal_routing.yaml` declares `sum_across_artifacts: true` for adoption, so a product with both a Hugging Face and a PyPI artifact should be compared against the **sum**, not the PyPI leg alone. The counts above compare against the PyPI leg only, so some of the 17 may shrink once that is done properly. Worth recomputing before anyone edits a score.

Related: #163 (new adoption routes), #168 (artifact drift).

title: [Implementation] Add contextual recall re-evaluation and sleeper-poisoning behavioral harness
body:
## Parent research / sequencing

- #173
- #196
- #198
- #175

## Priority

**P2-C — delayed/sleeper poisoning behavioral proof.**

#173 already provides strong doctrine + structural fixture coverage for sleeper poisoning, but explicitly warns that structural validation does not prove a runtime re-evaluates dormant state when later context changes.

P2-A/P2-B are now merged, so this slice must register its evidence through the existing D/F/H/R/P model and must not claim runtime/production depth it does not earn.

## Existing structural basis

`fixtures/sleeper-memory-poisoning.json` already requires:

```text
write_time_check_may_pass = true
later_trigger_rechecked = true
unsafe_activation_allowed = false
```

Canonical recall doctrine in `docs/26-governed-recall-planner.md` already requires admission-time evaluation of purpose, destination, scope, freshness, policy version, dispute/certification state, etc.

The implementation gap is the reference runtime seam for a current contextual recall policy.

## Objective

Add the smallest generic contextual recall-admission policy seam to the reference adapter, then execute the sleeper fixture behaviorally:

```text
retained memory
-> benign context recall may admit
-> later context changes
-> same retained candidate is retrieved again
-> current contextual policy re-evaluates it
-> triggered unsafe activation is quarantined/blocked/reviewed
-> prior admission does not become standing permission
```

## Generic contextual admission contract

Do not create sleeper-specific flags in the memory object.

A contextual admission policy should be able to consume:

```text
candidate identity
current RecallContext
current policy version
bounded evidence refs / risk reason
```

and return a deterministic current decision such as:

```text
admit
admit_with_warning
require_verification
require_review
quarantine
block
```

The built-in scope/lifecycle gates remain authoritative and execute first. A contextual policy may further restrict admission but must never widen a built-in refusal.

## Core invariants

```text
prior admission != standing recall permission
write-time safety != lifetime safety
candidate discovery != admission
relevance != permission
context change -> current admission re-evaluation
contextual policy may tighten != silently loosen built-in governance
blocked candidate -> no context surface -> no downstream influence
```

## Required sleeper behavioral sequence

1. commit/retain a bounded memory that can participate in ordinary recall;
2. recall under a benign purpose/context and demonstrate candidate + admission;
3. retain the same memory without mutating its stored content merely to force the test;
4. change the current recall context/purpose to the delayed trigger condition;
5. run recall again;
6. demonstrate the same candidate is discovered again;
7. demonstrate a fresh current contextual decision occurs under the current policy version;
8. demonstrate the candidate is not admitted under the triggered context;
9. demonstrate prior benign admission is not reused/cached as authority;
10. demonstrate no context surface/downstream influence from the blocked triggered recall.

## Required negative paths

1. contextual policy cannot override built-in tombstone/scope/dispute refusal to `admit`;
2. prior benign admission cannot be replayed as current authorization after context changes;
3. unknown/unsupported contextual outcome fails closed;
4. missing/failed current contextual policy at a configured high-assurance boundary cannot widen recall;
5. stochastic or learned risk signal may inform the contextual decision but cannot itself be an authority token;
6. current policy-version change is reconstructable in admission evidence;
7. candidate remains physically discoverable while unsafe admission is blocked;
8. blocked candidate never appears in admitted/context/downstream stages;
9. sleeper fixture structural assertions and behavioral observation must agree;
10. no production-resistance claim is made from reference harness success.

## Evidence-depth integration

Register a bounded sleeper-poisoning claim using the merged #196 model:

```text
D = canonical threat + governed recall doctrine
F = sleeper-memory-poisoning fixture
H = new behavioral harness
R = unproven unless independently generated runtime evidence is added
P = unproven
```

No composite score.

## Privacy / minimization

Contextual admission evidence should preserve refs, policy version, bounded reason/outcome, and candidate/context identity. Do not copy raw prompts, hidden reasoning, or full memory content merely to prove the gate ran.

## Non-goals

- generic content moderation system;
- LLM judge for sleeper detection;
- probabilistic semantic trigger discovery;
- live production sleeper attack testing;
- automatic memory deletion on triggered risk;
- rewriting the existing sleeper fixture doctrine;
- changing storage semantics merely to force the scenario.

## Evidence required for completion

- versioned contextual recall-admission decision schema/profile;
- optional generic policy seam in the reference adapter;
- behavioral harness tied to `sleeper-memory-poisoning.json`;
- negative-path tests including monotonic tightening and fail-closed policy unavailability;
- D/F/H/R/P report registration;
- exact-head CI.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] same retained candidate can be admitted benignly then blocked under changed current context
- [ ] prior admission is not reused as standing permission
- [ ] contextual policy only tightens, never widens built-in refusals
- [ ] current policy version/outcome/reason are reconstructable
- [ ] candidate discovery remains distinct from admission/context/influence
- [ ] sleeper fixture and behavioral result agree
- [ ] unknown/unavailable high-assurance contextual policy fails closed
- [ ] D/F/H demonstrated, R/P explicit unproven
- [ ] no raw context/memory copy is required
- [ ] exact-head CI passes before merge

title: [Decision] Canonical system-scope elevation: dmcp pkexec/polkit vs shellmcp sudo -A/askpass
body:
Tracking issue for a design decision. Two elevation strategies for running privileged (system-scope) shell commands landed independently and now overlap — we need to pick one canonical approach.

## Option A — dmcp `pkexec`/polkit (this session's work)
- **dmcp #34** (PR): `dmcp call` re-execs a system-scope **stdio** server via `pkexec` under the polkit action `org.jarvisos.dmcp.run-system-server`, so the server runs as root. The server stays "dumb" (runs the plain command).
- **mcp-registry #31/#32** (PR): the `jarvis-shell-system` server (sync, `subprocess.run`) drops its default kill-timeout and runs the plain command.
- Elevation centralized in **dmcp**; gated by polkit + the daemon's TLA confirmation. No `sudo` in the shell.

## Option B — shellmcp `sudo -A` / askpass (Toufic's #173, on `main`)
- `shellmcp/src/server.py` (async): auto-detects privileged commands (`PRIVILEGED_PREFIXES`, per-OS) and wraps them with **`sudo -A`** + a per-OS GUI askpass helper (ksshaskpass on KDE, an osascript shim on macOS, UAC on Windows).
- Elevation lives **in the shell server**; cross-platform out of the box. Server stays unprivileged; `sudo` is the mechanism.

## The conflict
- Two different shell-server codebases (mcp-registry's sync `jarvis-shell-system` vs Project-JARVIS's async `shellmcp`) with two different mechanisms (`pkexec` vs `sudo -A`). Only one should be canonical — running both would double-elevate.
- The **LLM-facing directive is the same either way** ("send the plain command, don't `sudo` yourself"); only the mechanism and the #199 prompt rationale differ.

## Decisions needed
1. **Mechanism** — `pkexec`/polkit (A) or `sudo -A`/askpass (B)?
2. **Canonical shell server** — mcp-registry `jarvis-shell-system` or Project-JARVIS `shellmcp`? Is the other retired or kept in sync?
3. Consequent fate of: dmcp #34, mcp-registry #31/#32, #199's wording, and #173.

## Considerations
- **Cross-platform:** B already handles macOS/Windows; A is `pkexec`-centric (dmcp added a macOS elevation path in #31/#32 xplat, but Linux-first).
- **Trust model:** A's polkit action + a `jarvis-elevated` rule ties cleanly to the TLA gate; B relies on askpass GUI + sudoers.
- **Single source of elevation:** centralizing in dmcp (A) gives *every* server consistent elevation; B puts elevation logic in each server.
- **Both work in isolation.** Option A was just verified end-to-end: `pacman -Syu` ran as root to completion (247 packages) with REMIND progress updates.

No code change requested here — this is to record the decision. Once chosen, I'll reconcile the losing side's PRs/prompt accordingly.

title: Simulation Setup
body: Hello, thank you very much for providing this excellent FDTD library. I am currently using **fdtdx** to simulate a **1.6 µm × 1.6 µm × 220 nm silicon corner waveguide**, and I encountered a significant difference in transmission efficiency under two simulation settings. I would like to ask for some guidance on how to properly configure the **substrate thickness**, **boundary distance**, and **PML thickness**. ### **Simulation Setup** The device geometry is exactly the same in both cases. The difference only lies in the simulation domain configuration: #### **Case 1 (Large simulation region)** - Device-to-boundary distance: **~2 µm** - SiO₂ substrate thickness: **2 µm** - PML: same thickness as Case 2 - This setting follows a colleague's workflow using **Lumerical** - **Transmission efficiency (Poynting flux ratio): ~61.91%** #### **Case 2 (Smaller simulation region)** - Device-to-boundary distance: **reduced** - Substrate thickness: **0.6 µm** - PML: same as Case 1 - Based on the configuration in the paper *“Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Inverse Design in Photonic Integrated Circuits”*, modifying only the waveguide height - **Transmission efficiency: ~37.48%** ### **My Question** Even though the device structure is the same, the transmission efficiency differs significantly between the two simulation domain configurations. I would like to understand: 1. **How sensitive is fdtdx to substrate thickness and simulation domain size?** Is a very thin SiO₂ substrate (e.g., 0.6 µm) likely causing unphysical leakage or substrate-mode loss? 2. **How should I choose the device–boundary distance?** Is there a recommended minimum distance (e.g., >1 µm) to avoid interaction between the guided mode and the boundaries? 3. **Are there guidelines for choosing PML thickness in fdtdx?** Could too-thin substrate or too-close boundaries cause the PML to absorb the guided mode incorrectly? 4. **Is it expected that reducing the substrate and simulation region causes such a large drop in transmission, or does this indicate improper FDTD configuration?** Any suggestions or best practices for setting the substrate thickness, PML layers, or boundary spacing would be extremely helpful. Thank you again for your work on this library!

title: Remote backup hangs indefinitely every time a specific file is reached
body:
## Have you checked borgbackup docs, FAQ, and open Github issues?

Yes

## Is this a BUG / ISSUE report or a QUESTION?

ISSUE

## System information. For client/server mode post info for both machines.

Client: Raspberry Pi 4B, 4GB RAM, on kernel `5.10.52-v7l+` (64bit CPU, 32bit OS)
Remote: Oracle VPS, 1GB RAM, on kernel `5.8.0-1037-oracle` (x64 system)

#### Your borg version (borg -V).

Both the client and the server are using borg 1.1.17

#### Operating system (distribution) and version.

Client: Raspbian GNU/Linux 10 (buster) armv7l (RaspiOS Lite - 32bit version)
Remote: Ubuntu Server 20.04.2 LTS x86_64

#### Hardware / network configuration, and filesystems used.

Client: backing up from a 1TB HDD connected via USB 3.0, formatted as ext4 (pushing to the remote).
Remote: receiving files to its SSD, also formatted as ext4
The client (Pi) is on my home network, connecting to the remote (VPS) in Germany using borg

#### How much data is handled by borg?

Total size of files being pushed is 26GiB, consisting of ~11400 photos.

#### Full borg commandline that lead to the problem (leave away excludes and passwords)

```
export BORG_REPO=pesav@vps-alpha:/backups/raspivault
export BORG_PASSPHRASE=<repo_password>
export BORG_FILES_CACHE_TTL=50
export BORG_HOSTNAME_IS_UNIQUE=yes

borg create --compression zstd,9 ::'{now}' /mnt/disk-storage/Foto
```

## Describe the problem you're observing.

This is a very strange one. Every time I try to do a backup (script above), it starts successfully, acquiring the lock and starting to send files. When it reaches a certain folder, which is after around ~23GB of processed files, it hangs indefinitely* (without any output, even with --verbose), until I force a ^C, then it stops with "Failed to create/acquire the lock (timeout)" and "Connection closed by remote" *.
I can do many backup attempts, and all fail when reaching files inside a certain folder (I've done 8 attempts, and 3 failed on one file, 3 on a second file and 2 on another file, all "close" to one another). The strange thing is that those files are photos, and I can open them so they're definitely not corrupted... and also, why should borg "fail to acquire the lock" when it has been doing the backup until that point?

**Note**: this could be a network issue, but then it should not so consistently fail with the same files every time, or at least not if they aren't corrupted. There is another borg repo (on a local drive) to which I backup the same files, and that one doesn't fail, so that further proves it's not a problem with those particular files.
* When I said "it hangs indefinitely" I left it in that state for at least 18 hours and nothing happened, and given the fact the "incriminated" files are 3MB large I think it's impossible it could have recovered.
* Also, I think that "Connection closed by remote" is caused by the fact I am pushing to the remote, so when I do a ^C the process stops, thus also terminating the `borg serve` command on the remote, so I don't think this is the problem.

#### Can you reproduce the problem? If so, describe how. If not, describe troubleshooting steps you took before opening the issue.

This problem occurs every time I try to backup to the remote repo, even after deleting it and recreating a new one (then doing a backup with the commands pasted above).
The command I use to create the repo is `borg init --encryption=repokey pesav@vps-alpha:/backups/raspivault`

#### Include any warning/errors/backtraces from the system logs

Nothing gets logged to syslog, both from the client side and the server side.

title: Dataset creation questions
body:
I've been digging around at all I could get my hands on this project, and have a few -mostly random and not in any particular order- questions, mostly on the choices of dataset generation. 

The project you guys are working on sound incredibly cool. I've seen @brunosan post about embeddings understanding and wanted to start taking a closer look at how the dataset was created in more depth as a first step :)

As far as I can understand it, from the '[How to create a datacube](https://clay-foundation.github.io/model/data_datacube.html#how-to-create-a-datacube)' section of the docs and `scripts/pipeline/datacube.py`, the input data consists of:
- [11 Band Sentinel 2](https://github.com/Clay-foundation/model/blob/1fe4fdfacdc04094eeb7ffc3241fe808165881cc/scripts/pipeline/datacube.py#L46), but only [10 are really used](https://github.com/Clay-foundation/model/blob/c2smsfloods_benchmark_datapipeline/scripts/datacube_benchmark.py#L25)?
- 2 Band Sentinel 1, using the MPC [RTC product](https://github.com/Clay-foundation/model/blob/1fe4fdfacdc04094eeb7ffc3241fe808165881cc/scripts/pipeline/datacube.py#L194)
- Copernicus 30m DEM, resampled to 10m

My understanding is that this is based on Cloud to Street (now [Floodbase](https://www.floodbase.com/))'s dataset, it's something they implemented and this initial v0.1 simply uses their dataset setup? That's probably the answer to the following questions, but here you go nonetheless:

1. Sentinel 1 RTC imagery & Copernicus DEM

Why use the RTC Sentinel 1 product? I see from the [MPC docs](https://planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/dataset/sentinel-1-rtc) that it uses the `PlanetDEM` product, which [according to this](https://www.planetobserver.com/blog/planetdem-artefact-free#:~:text=PlanetDEM%20is%20mainly%20based%20on,with%20NASADEM%20data%20(NASA).) is from the ALOS World 3D-30m + NASADEM. I hadn't compared this one to Copernicus DEM before but there might be difference in the two (ALOS is SAR, and Cop DEM is a downsampled version of Airbus's WorldDEM made from TerraSAR-X if I recall correctly, so there would at least be some similarities). This might lead to some inconsistency between the SAR corrected imagery & the DEM used? That being said I also understand this is probably a lot faster to implement with an off-the-shelf SAR dataset :D 

2. Copernicus DEM nearest neighbour resampling (?)

I followed the basic tutorial [to get MGRS tiles over Puri India](https://clay-foundation.github.io/model/run_region.html) and checked the tiles in QGIS, and noticed the Copernicus DEM, band 13, seems to be interpolated to nearest neighbour, i.e. that pixels are resampled from 30m to identical values of 3x3 pixels of 10x10 meters, with all the same value. Here using QGIS's `Value Tool` plugin I can see there are 3 pixels, with the DEM raster not changing value on a 3x3 grid

![CleanShot 2024-03-27 at 20 19 54](https://github.com/Clay-foundation/model/assets/44133329/9fed8139-06ab-4e79-bd16-1faec0b27d3c)

I was wondering if there was a reason for not interpolating using something like a `bilinear` that might smooth the DEM more? I feel like this might weight the edges of these 3x3 grids more heavily in changes compared to the central pixel, when that's not really how the terrain is?
I didn't find the code that resamples all datasets to the 10m, so may have gotten that wrong, this is only based on my visual interpretation in QGIS. 

3. Band choices

I'm not too sure why this code has 11 Sentinel 2 bands, while this here in the [benchmark only keeps 10](https://github.com/Clay-foundation/model/blob/c2smsfloods_benchmark_datapipeline/scripts/datacube_benchmark.py#L25-L26)? And of those 10, why remove the `SCL` band?

Also in the [benchmark script](https://github.com/Clay-foundation/model/blob/c2smsfloods_benchmark_datapipeline/scripts/datacube_benchmark.py#L26) only `VV` and `VH` are kept for Sentinel 1, why not `HH` & `HV`?

These are probably details in the grand scheme of the project, but questions I had so here we are! 
I'm quite amazed at all the work that you all have made in just a few months, this gets me really excited for the next iterations to come!

title: URDFSpawner <device reference=”link”> does not work when the link is defined in the urdf and not in an existing PROTO
body:
**Describe the Bug**
When defining a robot using only one URDF and no existing PROTO, `reference` property of the `device` tag does not work.
In the turtlebot example, it works because the turtlebot already exists in the world file and the urdf is only used for defining webots plugins : https://github.com/cyberbotics/webots_ros2/blob/master/webots_ros2_turtlebot/resource/turtlebot_webots.urdf#L4

**Steps to Reproduce**
Consider the following urdf : 
```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<robot name="myrobot"
    xmlns:xacro="http://ros.org/wiki/xacro">

    <!-- Webots -->
    <webots>
        <device reference="laser_link" type="Lidar">
            <ros>
                <enabled>true</enabled>
                <updateRate>5</updateRate>
                <topicName>/scan</topicName>
                <alwaysOn>true</alwaysOn>
                <frameName>laser_link</frameName>
            </ros>
        </device>

        <plugin type="webots_ros2_control::Ros2Control" />
    </webots>

    <!-- BASE LINK -->
    <link name="base_link">
        <visual>
            <origin xyz="0 0 0.075" />
            <geometry>
                <box size="0.3 0.3 0.15" />
            </geometry>
        </visual>
        <collision>
            <origin xyz="0 0 0.075" />
            <geometry>
                <box size="0.3 0.3 0.15" />
            </geometry>
        </collision>
    </link>

    <joint name="laser_link_joint" type="fixed">
        <parent link="base_link" />
        <child link="laser_link" />
        <origin xyz="0 0 1" />
    </joint>

    <!-- LINK2 -->
    <link name="laser_link">
        <!-- Here the link could be empty resulting in only a Transform Node with a Lidar object, but due to issue cyberbotics/urdf2webots#201
        a <collision> tag is required in order for the link to exists in webots -->
        <visual>
            <origin xyz="0 0 0.075" />
            <geometry>
                <box size="0.3 0.3 0.15" />
            </geometry>
        </visual>
        <collision>
            <origin xyz="0 0 0.075" />

        </collision>

</robot>
```

A Lidar object should exist in Webots and the ROS ropic `/scan` should be advertised.

title: Why the model are not restored in leave-one-out?
body:
Hi,

As far I know, the LOO algorithm for deep learning models works as below. I could not find any model restore operations in "value" and "utility" packages of yours. The aim is to find best samples for the model (by not changing the model weights) and then train only with these samples to improve accuracy of the model. If the model is not restored, then the model will be trained len(samples) times (can cause overfitting), and model weights will be changed. Do I miss anything?

Thanks a lot.
Best regards.

```
def loo(model, train_samples, test_samples):
    reference_w = model.get_weights()    # save weights for restoring later
    model.train(train_samples)
    reference_accuracy = model.test(test_samples)    
    model.restore_weights(reference_w) # not to affect the utility of remaining samples
    values = []
    for s in train_samples:         
        subset = train_samples - {s}  # the subset without the sample s
        model.train(subset) 
        values.append(reference_accuracy  - model.test(test_samples))
        model.restore_weights(reference_w) # not to affect the utility of remaining samples
   return values
```

title: Why multithreading?
body:
Simple suggestion, since you've change the name of the executable, it would be nice if the [vcstool ROS wiki page](http://wiki.ros.org/vcstool) was updated as well. I would do it but I am not whitelisted AND I am not sure I should do it either. 

And now to the main issue. 

When I was trying to automate a docker ROS 1 build using vcs (since wstool is deprecated) and I found out that often some repos would time out. I think I was hitting bandwidth limitations because vcs was trying to download from multiple repositories all at once. 

In any case, it was annoying to debug and I think setting `--workers 1` helped, but I am not sure. It could just be completely random. In any case I am questioning the multithreading implementation as default here and if it is even necessary at all. I mean, the downloads in a series will just complete each of them faster and in the end the time it takes will be the same. This would only make sense if the repositories themselves have a bottleneck, but I think, unless someone is hosting a git repository in their home, this is not very likely.

Anyway, just my 2 cents. Close this if you know better. Cheers!
